Review Text: This is my 3rd pump and honestly I had high hopes for it. My previous pumps broke and I thought this one would hold up but it’s not great. The suction is strong and it does empty me but getting it going is such a process. There are only a few parts to put together to start pumping but it’s difficult to assemble. It’s also neat that the pump can be controlled by an app but the buttons to adjust the pump is right on top so the app is kind of pointless unless you’re tracking how much milk you pump which you manually add at the end of your session. The heating feature is just ok nothing to write home about. It doesn’t really get that hot and I haven’t seen any difference in my supply beacuse of it. The heating feature also DRAINS the battery life by 20-30% a session. One thing I really dislike is that it doesn’t pump in sync. There is a button on the app to sync the left and right pump but after a few seconds it falls out of sync again. I find with this pump a 15 minute session turns into 25 minutes with having to readjust and configuring the settings to pump comfortably. It’s convenient that it charges in its carrying case as well as has a few pockets in the case. I haven’t had any issues charging. All in all the pump is just ok. It’s definitely overpriced and not worth the money.

Review Title: Great output but there are tradeoffs
Author: JA
Review Text:
I never write reviews, but I feel like there are some key things moms should know about this pump:

Pros:
- Really great output (on par with my Spectra!). The warming feature is a game-changer for maximizing the amount of milk you can pump for a wearable.
- The charging case is extremely convenient for travel and work; I've never had to charge the pumps with a cord and its so nice not to have the pumps rattling around in my work bag.
- Provide flange inserts so you can get your correct size (also huge for output!)
- Not much worry about leaking AS LONG AS you have it put together correctly (see Cons!)

Cons:
- The flange is very difficult to put onto the container and you MUST make sure its completely sealed or you will have milk everywhere. This happened to me several times before I realized just how much sheer force I had to use to put the pieces together.
- If you need/want replacement parts (and you do if you are using this as a main pump or using it for travel), Eufy is going to take complete advantage of you and charge highway robbery. The price for extra parts is OUTRAGEOUS compared to other wearables (2-3x more) and they are conveniently always "sold out" of the bundle so that you have to buy each part individually at a higher price.
- It is BIG and not inconspicuous. You will look like Amy Poehler from Mean Girls.

SUMMARY: I have tried both this pump and the Elvie, and despite its flaws, am still using this pump as my wearable pump for travel because the milk output is just so good. However, Eufy could do a lot to improve.

I was between the Willow 360 and this pump but ultimately decided to go with the eufy S1 for the warming feature since I use the fridge hack and HATE having to either put on the flanges cold or wait for them to warm up.

Let me tell you, the warming function is a game changer. I think it’s also helped with my output. I’m not a big supplier so every ounce counts.

I also love that the machine doesn’t automatically start pumping when turning it on. You have to press the power button one more time to get it started. This is important for me because I like to start at a lower setting and gradually build up. The pumps usually save your previous settings so if I’m at a really high setting to end and don’t adjust it, then my next session starts out painful.

I didn’t think I would care about this, but I love the charging case! I don’t have to have all of these cables on my nightstand anymore and it’s good to have traveling. Plus, I feel like the charge doesn’t last as long as advertised (mine only lasted about a day), but that might be because I use the warming feature so frequently and sometimes forget to turn the pump off after a session.

I love that it converts between oz and mls. Something small but it’s a nice touch.

There are some issues that I don’t like. For me, these are minor issues and just more annoying. I would get the pump again just for the warming feature alone.

-The major annoyance is that when I sync the pumps on the app, it’ll start off at the same rhythm but for some reason starts to go off as time progresses. Also, I’ll frequently have one still in simulation while the other one has moved on to express mode but that doesn’t make sense why it would do that since they SHOULD be doing the same thing. It’ll show on the app that my right pump has progressed a lot farther than the left side even though the time is the same. I thought maybe it’s an app glitch but even if you don’t sync it and you manually start it on the pump itself, it still has the same issue. The only way I’ve gotten around the rhythm issue is by manually changing between expression and stimulation.
-There’s no timer on the actual pump. You have to rely on the app in order to know how long you’ve been pumping.
-The pump itself easily tips over and  the milk spout is right next to the charging port and the buttons so it may get damaged over time if you’re not careful.
-The measurement on the cups are off. It’ll say like 0.5oz but when I actually measure it out into my Medela storage containers, it’ll be more like 1-1.5 oz.

I’ve only been using this pump for two days but it’s my favorite pump so far. I’m probably going to use this as my main pump. :)

I do like the pump, but finally went out this week and realized you can’t put the pump inside the case without removing the protective flange cover because there’s a bump in the middle… what’s the point of having a flange cover if you can’t use it at all times?

Author: emily
Review Text:
As a pumping mom, I heard a lot about the need to have wearables AND a wall pump because wearables “don’t empty you all the way”. I specifically purchased these because I read a blog post from a woman who tried about 20 wearables and tested how much milk was produced from a wall pump directly AFTER using wearables, and the Eufy’s were the pumps that left her most emptied. While this varies person to person, I can attest to the fact that these DO empty me and I have returned my Medela wall pump to the hospital! I only pump once a day now, but I wish I would have got these sooner when my baby had a bad latch. I love the charging case, charge lasts a long time and heating function too, not sure if it gets more milk but I do think it helps to achieve a letdown.

Just know this - wearables are great to be able to pump and drive, pump and do chores etc but NOT easy to hold a (Velcro) baby with these on. It’s do-able but awkward.

They do NOT leak. You just have to make sure the flange is properly sealed to the plastic part, I’ve never had a leaking issue.

The app is useful if you are going to be pumping discretely, so you can turn on / off or adjust settings without digging in your bra. However I do not use the app, I just use the buttons on the pumps.

Most women are not the standard flange size (24) so I LOVE that these come with a bunch of different flange size inserts, AND a flange size measuring tool!

I’ve not tried any other wearable pumps so I can’t compare but I definitely recommend these. They are pricey, but I paid for them with HSA funds.

My only complaint
- the pockets in the case are annoying. They don’t even fit the pump covers? And there is no Velcro, zipper, button etc so my milk bags just always fall out of the pocket, which pretty much makes the pocket useless because you could just shove bags loosely in there without the pocket.

Review Title: Eufy has gained a new fan! But with the exception of
Author: Kendall Trevethan
Review Text:
I’m truly impressed with this product, which is why I’ve given it a 4-star rating. For its price, it’s fantastic, though I believe a few minor tweaks could elevate it to perfection. Assembly is a breeze, taking less than a minute per pump, and the pumps themselves are remarkably quiet—barely noticeable during use. The heating feature is an absolute game-changer; it’s ingenious and has noticeably boosted my milk supply, making it one of my favorite aspects.

That said, there are a couple of small drawbacks. I’ve noticed some leakage when removing the pump and pouring out the milk. It’s not a major issue—I’ve learned to anticipate it and prepare accordingly—but it’s worth mentioning. Another minor wish is for an option to automatically track milk output rather than manually entering it. I’ll admit, this might just be my laziness talking, but it’d be a nice touch.

Regarding the charging case, it’s sleek and stylish, but I find myself not using it as much as I expected. The covers don’t fit inside, which is a bit inconvenient for carrying, and I tend to stick with the charging cables instead—which, by the way, are excellent and reliable. While the case is a nice feature, I wish I hadn’t opted for it since it doesn’t fully suit my needs.

Overall, these pumps are exceptional, with just a few small areas for improvement. With some refinements in a potential 2.0 version, they could be even more incredible for the price. I’d still highly recommend them as they are! I hope to be purchasing more things from this brand in the future, so far; big fan.

Review Text:

2. All of the parts seem like they’re very high quality, I like that there is both a charging case and separate charger to charge the motors directly
3. Good production output. I have always had an average to above average output, so I saw no increase or decrease with this product

1. Even though there is an option on the app to synchronize the two pumps/motors, the two pumps will not actually sync. They will start almost synced, then quickly become out of step with each other. This resulted in the product being extra loud, which drove me nuts. It also is annoying that because of the lack of synchronization my boobs would alternate getting pumped (I know this is a weird comparison, but it made me feel like I had utters being milked individually)

I have not experienced any pain from either breast feeding or pumping since my daughter was born a month ago, so I think there was just something about the shape of this pump that didn’t fit on my nipples/boobs well

Ultimately I will be returning. I want to love this product, but the two things I can’t get past are it slightly hurting when I pump, and the motors not syncing up. I think it might still be worth a try (maybe I just received a defective motor for one of them?), but this product was not for me.

Review Text:
Wait until it’s on sale… not worth paying over $400.

This pump was great until the suction failed. I was pumping a minimum of 120 ml per session during the day and up to 400 ml at night when the pump was working properly. Once the suction went down substantially (I was having to use the highest setting) I went to only producing 15-40 ml per session on average.

I am beyond devastated. Eufy immediately sent a replacement with no hassle that should arrive in 4 days. But this shouldn’t have been an issue at all since the pump is so expensive and I only used it for 2 months. The replacement unfortunately does not make up for the fact that I’m having to thaw three frozen bags a day when I was freezing a bag a day prior to the pump going faulty. I’m only pumping 2,950ish ml rather than my normal 8,770ish ml per week.

The heating setting is phenomenal though and the charging design is well thought out. However, I do not like the shape of the pump. It’s not discreet in any way. It’s such an odd shape… I wish they would’ve re-thought the design to actually form the shape of a boob… not just sit on top of it.

I also have a $50 wireless pump that I’ll be using until the replacement comes. But after comparing the two, Eufy technology is far superior/comfortable. BUT they are equally as loud and the $50 is more of a natural shape. The only reason I’m sticking with eufy is because it is the most comfortable pump I’ve used/the heating feature.

I will also say I feel a little mislead from the marketing. You still have to log the amount of milk you pump. I thought it automatically calculated and logged it for you. Not sure if it’s just because my pump has issues but sometimes it doesn’t save the logged session. Which is a huge flaw, especially if you are trying to track how long you can keep fresh milk out of the fridge. I have had to use the ParentLove app to track pumping as well to avoid any issues.

3.5 stars when it was working properly. 1 star for its current “working” state.

Author: Amazon Customer
Review Text:
These are great pumps, and I recommend them. The Eufy customer service is also excellent and fast. They come with all the usual flange sizes and a great little wire brush that I used for ages. They feel nice, materials are clearly durable and high quality. One charge lasts forever! Motors also seem pretty water resistant as I have spilled so much breast milk on them before. Suction is good, the app is simple, and the pumps can be used without Bluetooth as needed. Much less to carry around than a full pump setup, though they are heavy little things. I liked using them mostly when it was the middle of the night and I was too tired to do the whole usual pump setup. Just shove in your bra and doze back off (sitting up) until it’s done. Although you do have to be vigilant about it filling up, because once it hits 5oz or so it starts to spill over. I see several people saying the motor is hard to detach - if you read the instructions it explains how to pull back the plastic just a bit and if pops right out, no problem. I used and sterilized this about every other day for a year, and I still really like them. I appreciate having these a lot, and feel they are worth the price.

The negatives, none of which I would discount this product entirely because of but would prefer to be improved upon: It is annoying to put together. Perhaps all wearables are like this, I’m not sure. You have to make sure the seal all the way around is REALLY good or it WILL leak, which while not an unreasonable demand is not always easy when you’re in a hurry to pump or only have one hand with baby in the other. It also drips when you take it off the breast, sometimes quite a bit. It only comes with one duckbill flange, and those things are TINY. The cost to replace the parts is absurd, so you better not lose them. Finally, the heating element is touchy and doesn’t always work. It may just be my item and Eufy gave me a partial refund for that part, which I was content with. They are pretty heavy so at least for me I can’t easily walk around with them in my bra (wired or T-shirt) without them moving or leaking.

Review Title: Would have been great but too many problems out of the box
Author: K.L.
Review Text:
I received a damaged part, one of the heated flange showed visible issues, preventing good contact of the metal pins that would allow the heated feature to work. Amazon offered a $20 credit, which I accepted (figuring I could buy replacement flanges and replace the broken one  —currently 2 for $40, so the $20 would just break even).

What I didn’t anticipate was the other flange also not working properly either. The other side, which had no signs of wear or damage, would only heat up half the surface when it’s supposed to heat up everything evenly. So, both of the flanges out of the box from a new, sealed product were either damaged or not working. I got reimbursed for one of them (and not the other because i didn’t realize there was a problem).

Now, for the replaced heated flange that does work. It’s actually quite a wonderful product. No pumps clear me (is it because my ducts are too small?) but this one does or comes closest to. Even on gentle mode and low suction, I got better output than my other pumps, including wall pumps. The heat makes a huge difference for me, as someone who easily clogs. I suspect I also have very low storage capacity. I currently am producing very little, at the start of my breastfeeding/pumping journey and suspect this would be very helpful with increasing my supply.

I actually really love this pump, but I can’t recommend it with all the problems that come out of the box, especially if you already have a main pump.  If you are willing to throw money at the problem to have this work for you, and you are someone who tends to clog easily, then go ahead and get it. Otherwise this may end up being either a money sink or a time sink, while you try to get everything resolved. Which, when you’re at home with a newborn is less than ideal.

Review Text:

I’ve had this pump for two days so this review is obviously only based off two days of use. I exclusively pump. I have a 3 month old and a 3 year old so I’m constantly moving. I needed a wearable comfortable pump. This is my second wearable pump the first one was cheap and got the job done for the most part but it only had two modes. I have been researching other wearable pumps and these wearable pumps are an investment. I bought the Eufy on prime day which was an amazing deal. I was sold on the Eufy because of the heat setting. I’m very sensitive like I have to have the suction low but I’m also an over producer. Anywho I love this pump!! There is an app to connect it to your phone and you can control it from there or the pump itself. You can sync both of them or have separate modes. You can have an auto shut off! Whatever setting you leave off on will be the one that is suggested when you turn it back on. Also in the app you can track your ounces you do have to manually put them in which isn’t bad. I absolutely love the heat setting it’s very comfortable and you can have it automatically shut off on a timer too, I’m a hot person and this doesn’t add to it or make pumping unbearable. Now moving on to putting it together and taking it apart. Once you get the hang of it man it’s super easy! I haven’t spilt any of my milk while taking it apart which I’m thankful for because we all know it’s hard work making it anyways we don’t want to waste it! So I take my fingers and pull by the spout in the opposite direction from the motor. Someone pulling them in two different directions at the same to get the magnet to come apart once I fill that it’s not connected anyone I pull the motor off. Also, the app is pretty user friendly if that is important to you but the only feature I saw value in was the ability to differentiate each pump's suction mode/rhythm. I have issues with convenience.  It's easy to not get your nip position right and since you can't see the milk catch from above your bra, you won't know if you've wasted 20 min of "pumping" and need to reposition + start all over. Also, there can easily be milk leaking down the bottom of the intake if you don't have firm compression from a bra, but if you get the position + good compression right, it's magnificently fast and efficient pumping!) The heating element has been a constant issue: I had to contact customer support after 4 days of use because I kept getting flashing error lights for the heating pins. Nothing would work until support advised a system update .... This requires setting up an account and downloading the app to your phone. I am suspicious of this, so curious if others had the same "issue." Then today the heating element pin basically malfunctioned and fried itself - I think a charging issue?? I've had the heating element get extremely hot, i.e  too hot at full temp to touch breast skin - i get a red mark where it lies if I can even get it to lie flush but you have to get it *perfect* inside the bra to do this. I will try to get a replacement part but they never have any available. You cannot bend over without milk pouring out of the spouts; they do make plugs to prevent this but it's an after-sales accessory and it's NEVER in stock 🙄 This model is  inconvenient for cleaning or charging. They want you to manually clean the parts every time and sterilize with boiling - no dishwasher or microwaving, even for the basic plastic parts because it will degrade them faster?? Sorry but no one has time for this. And the inside of the milk catch seems to develop a weird film that is thick and tactile - it doesn't come off even with dish soap and a bristle brush. You have to take vinegar and manually scrub it off. I don't think this is worth $240 - the heating element has been more trouble than it's worth. I'd go with the basic one or wait for them to update/upgrade this one with the heating element in v 2.0. I hope they will make the next version compatible with USB-C charging cords instead of the proprietary magnetic ones. (The magnets do work great, but if I lose this cord, how will I replace it? Their shop has little available for replacement parts, so I don't even know how I'll replace the duckbill valves - only the diaphragms are available the past month.) This is weird because customer service through the Amazon seller interface has been pretty decent, and the parent company is Anker, so I expected better electronics and parts supply chain.)

Review Text:

I had got the M9 because I was excited about the app. What I've learned is you have to manually turn on the pumps first before they Bluetooth to the app. From the app you're able to change the mode, the strength, you can see how long they've been on and you can also power off.

However, the pumps do not weigh the ounces you produce and automatically send this information to the app. The collector cups have ounce lines on them but they are not accurate so I would suggest pouring into a bottle and reading there before manually entering this information into the app.

Another dislike of mine is the actual pouring of the milk from the collector cups. You've gotta take the pump apart and then you're not able to get every last drop due to the shape of the collectors.

That's something I've come to really appreciate about the M5 is that you don't have to take them apart and they pour right out.

The M9 are not as round/bulky as the M5, however as far as noise level I think they're fairly similar, not necessarily more quiet as I had read in some reviews.

Like I said, I've only been using the M9 for a couple of days now but so far that's been my experience.

Review Text: These pumps have really helped my wife. They work well for her and they are easy to assemble, use, disassemble, and clean. However, there's a systematic flaw with the flange. I've been forced to buy the complete set just to get the flange (we don't need all the other parts, just the flange) which is more than twice the cost, making this issue even more annoying. If you buy this pump, I'd recommend ordering additional flanges from the start because it's only a matter of time until it breaks and you don't want to be left with 1 (or worse, 0) working flanges. Review Title: Functions well, great battery life, quiet, discreet…love it!
Author: Anita
Review Text:
First time mom here, and I absolutely LOVE this pump. I breastfeed about 80-90% of the time and use a spectra pump the other 10-20%. I noticed I needed a wearable pump to use when out of the house for long periods and unable to breastfeed. I had no idea which wearable pump to choose as there are sooo many out there but the app capabilities and positive reviews on function for this one really won me over! I’ve used it in all sorts of places such as long car rides and local outdoor fairs. At first I noticed the flanges would slip down a bit and not stay centered on the nipple, but after using it a few times I found that the key is to tighten your bra straps all the way. Personally I use a nursing bra - first I unclip the cup, then tighten the strap all the way. Then I’ll insert the pump and clip the cup back on (and repeat on other side!). This works perfectly for me every time and they do not move!

I love:
-I still produce the same amount as I do with my spectra
-It comes with additional flange inserts in various sizes
-Pumps auto shut down after 30 minutes (even though I usually only pump for 15, I tend to forget to power them off)
-Battery life is great! I’ve never had them die on me. Once pumped 10 times (for 15 min each) without recharging and they barely dipped below 60%.
-the pumps allow me to be completely hands free
-can’t tell you’re wearing pumps, just looks like you’ve got big boobs
-they’re extremely quiet
-no leaking
-comes with two sets of collection cups, duckbill valves, & plugs to seal cups, and a compact carrying case
-that I don’t have to stick my hands in my bra to adjust the settings
-the app is easy to use
-can create custom settings via the app, and if you have it selected it will automatically begin that setting upon powering on

Don’t love:
-There are quite a few parts which was confusing at first, but after 1-2 times of taking it apart and putting it back together you quickly get the hang of it.
-Measurements on collection cups seem to be inaccurate

The many pros vastly outweigh the few cons and I’m so glad I chose this pump, highly recommend!!

Product Title: Momcozy Breast Pump Hands Free Upgraded Mobile Flow | M9, App Discreet Control with Personalized Multi-Modes & 15 Levels, Wearable Breast Pump 24mm, 2 Pack Cozy Red
Author: Morgan O.
Review Text:
First, this is NOT sponsored or fake in anyway — genuine experience from a first time mom who’s been deeply struggling with depression rooted in pumping. My baby never learned to latch properly due to a lot of facial and full body tension, but I desperately wanted to give him breast milk due to the research behind it, so I started pumping. Unfortunately no one told me how much a stationary pump sucks — and how much more it sucks when you have to sit at it 8 times a day due to being an undersupplier. So that’s accumulatively like 5 hours a day dedicated to pumping. My baby is 6 weeks old now and I’d been at this the whole time, to no avail. My supply has struggled to increase. It did a little, but then dropped down again, and I believe part of that had to do with depression itself. The stationary pump literally felt like a ball and chain; my back was killing me from having to sit and lean forward with it all the time, and I couldn’t get a single thing done. My life became feed the baby, change the baby, pump, repeat. There was no time to play with my baby, no time to go to the toilet, to shower, to get myself food, to clean, to get enough sleep to exercise or even go outside. My house was getting messier and messier around me and all I could do was watch. My husband helped as much as he could, but he couldn’t keep up with cleaning everything on his own, he was already doing all of the laundry, cooking, dishes, shopping, working, as well as waking up at night to help with the baby. I was crying every day with anxiety about missing any pumps, because I was already making so little and I was sure I’d just dry up and stop altogether if I missed one. I couldn’t envision the future, keeping this up for 6+ months would’ve been torture.

If this sounds like you, get a portable pump. Do it sooner than I did. Though to be fair, the reason I didn’t is because I was mismeasured by my LC and I didn’t think there were flanges in my size for most wearables. After reassessing, I realized I might actually need a 13mm, which is the smallest offbrand flange out there for this pump.  It’s a pricey pump, but we bit the bullet and haven’t had a single regret. I can actually do things again, it feels like overnight I got my life back.

For the pump itself: I do like it so far, it has a fairly low profile (or as much as you could hope for), you can sit comfortably while using it and move around, I can still feed my baby and change his diaper, I can clean, I even went for a walk with it. People say they have a hard time with it slipping around and falling out but I haven’t had that. What I will say is you NEED a very secure bra, you can’t use just anything. I’m using the Kindred Bravely bras I bought. You don’t need these, but you need something with a similar tightness that is going to be stretchy enough to allow for the pumps, but firm enough that it’s going to hold them on you and not budge. The app for this is okay; I like the auto feature for increasing milk supply. I don’t think I’ve seen too much increase, but I am at least seeing all of my normal levels, so I know it’s emptying me all the way.

Negatives:
The app is a little annoying and could use some work. I have yet to get my pumps to be perfectly synchronized while using them. I also find it really annoying that they don’t supply you with wall plugs??? You have to plug in two cords to charge each pump individually, but you have to provide your own wall plugs. For this price, I find that to be wrong. They should either provide you with two wall plugs, or invent their own with two input slots in it so that you can charge both pumps on one plug. And the other thing I find irritating is that the smallest flange insert they offer is 17mm. They are leaving out a HUGE part of the population, it’s not uncommon at all for people to need smaller flanges than this. I was fortunate to know to look for smaller flanges that are offbrand, but some people may not know about this and might try to use the ones supplied that are too big for them. Why give a nipple measuring tool that starts at 11mm if you’re not going to offer flanges for them? Anyway, the only other thing is that there’s a lot of parts to this to clean. I’ve been using the method of sticking them (minus the motor) in the fridge so that I have to clean them less often, because that in itself would be quite the task.

Otherwise, I would give these a solid 4.6 out of 5. I am so happy I invested in them and I’ve gotten my life back overnight.

Update: One other negative I’m noticing is that the markings on the collection cups aren’t accurate. I’ve been testing them against my baby bottles, which I know are accurate. It’s accurate at 30ml, so you can put two 30 ml quantities into my baby bottle and get 60. But when you pour the whole thing back into the collection cup, it doesn’t reach the 60ml marking, it’s more like 55. The factory has the lines perfectly spaced apart, which you can’t do because the collection cups are not one width, they’re small at the bottom and get wider. So that’s pretty frustrating when you’re an underproducer and carefully trying to measure how much milk you’re making and if you’re trending upward or downward.

Product Title: Medela Pump in Style Breast Pump Starter Kit | Classic Pump | Double Electric Breastpump with Bottles
Review Title: This pump is going to kill my supply…
Author: Nina
Review Text:
I’d like to mention that I received this pump through insurance, we started off rough.. the first pump in style I was initially sent didn’t work for crap so I reached out to medela and was sent a replacement within the next two days. Nonetheless I was extremely excited to use this despite its mixed reviews!

The first day or two of using it as an exclusive pumper (due to my baby having a severe lip tie) it was great, I mean honestly. I loved the simplicity of it, I loved that it had no memory function so my sessions don’t start off painful. The suction was fairly decent and I loved the vibrating pull it has on the nipple and that it self led me to believe it was emptying me  pretty well not to mention it have me let down after let down which was insanely impressive to me. Until the other night.. I woke up for my nighttime pumping session and I was EXTREMELY engorged.. I don’t have to go into details moms,  iykyk. I went to use the pump and 5 minutes in I noticed nothing was coming out but it was suckling so I messed around with it, made sure everything was secured and turned up the suction and still nothing. Normally 5 minutes in I at least have and ounce or ounce in a half so it was weird to see nothing was coming out. I used it for about 30 minutes and only had that much.. an ounce each side. I hand expressed as much as my boobs could handle but it was painful so I just went to bed. I woke again in so much pain so again, I used the pump and still nothing. So I used my old reliable wearables by Lansinoh and there it was, I had to stop half way through my pump session to empty the extremely full containers and still filled that up again by the time 20 minutes flew by.. that how backed up I was. Since then I’ve received nothing but MINIMAL output from this pump, for perspective i stash up to 40-50oz a day, as of right now, I make enough for a bottle per session and the let downs have stopped.

All in all.. my honest opinion is that I don’t think this pump can withstand exclusive use before it’s over worked. Even in the manual it states that it’s meant for 3 times a day, 15 minutes each, for 6 months but even then I would think this is something I was run into a few months from now, not now! One of the other cons is the battery pack, its heavy and it only holds 8 batteries that only last you a few seconds at most. I still can’t seem to figure out why it isn’t working for me anymore, is it the pieces? The suction? It should be neither since only received the pump about a week ago.

So as I’m using this pump again for another nighttime session, engorged again to the max.. trying to give the pump another shot.. take it from me, don't buy. But who knows, this pump works great for others and for some it just doesn’t. So, try it at your own risk.
Date: Reviewed in the United States on September 17, 2024

Author: Amazon Customer
Review Text: So, I ordered this 1/17/23, and I used it as my basement pump for when I was on the desktop. I have a newborn, so it is safe to say I was not on the desktop every night. This wasn't my main pump, but after less than 4 months of it existing in my home and maybe a month worth of washing, the pump cups broke. These cups are made of hard plastic, and one cup broke at the part where it locks into the flange. For the price, I would have expected more. Medela is a popular brand and the brand that I used at the hospital, I love my hand pump by them, but this product missed its mark. I find there is no variability with the suction pattern, and you have to cycle through increasing pressure with no identifier of which you are on. My main pump is a Spectre which insurance paid for, and my portable pump is a momcozy; both pumps have screens so that you can see the suction level, switch suction pattern, and time pumped. I didn't know I would appreciate those features prior to pumping. I'm giving it 3-stars since the machine itself is still working, but I have no incentive to purchase replacement parts if they are just going to break in a few months.

Product Title: Medela Pump in Style Breast Pump Starter Kit | Classic Pump | Double Electric Breastpump with Bottles
Author: Aimée
Review Text:
I uses the Medela Pump in Style Advance for years (for a year with my now 5 year old, and 10 months with my 1 year old).

I treated myself to a new model, loving the idea of "hands-free" and 10X more milk production. I also thought the bigger parts would be easier to clean between sessions and at the end of the night. Wrong, wrong and wrong!.

1. Not "hands-free." You are still very much attached to a machine so not a difference there.
2. From November 2023-April 2024 I likely got comparable milk production. I started having sessions where I would produce no milk the last week. I almost quit pumping, but realized my breasts definitely had milk. After going back to my older "Pump In Style Advanced," I pumped a great deal of milk. I will add I clean and care for my parts meticulously.
3. The parts are no easier to manage than my older model. Just bigger. And more expensive.
4. It takes 10 minutes for me to express on this model vs. 1 minute with my older Medela model.
5. The way I have to bend my neck to check on progress during sessions and troubleshoor the painfully long expression sessions hurts it!

I would not recommend this at all!
Date: Reviewed in the United States on May 7, 2024

Review Text:
This is a good option for a pump if you would prefer to not have to change into a pumping bras each use. It is easy to use and overall a good pump. It doesn’t have the same portability of a hand free like the Elvie or Willow, but not quite as clunky and limiting like a traditional  pump. I would consider this an option for your “main” pump vs a truly portable pump.

Pros:
Cups are see through so you can see expression
Good suction- I found this to be better output than a portable (like elvie)
Easy assembly - few parts that make this easy to assemble and wash

Cons:
Can’t customize pumping per side
Can’t see how long you have been pumping
Can’t see what level you’re pumping at
Difficult to disassemble- I often have trouble when trying to take apart the pieces to wash

Product Title: Medela Freestyle Breast Pump
Review Title: Used with twins plus two more.
Author: Maria
Review Text:
10 minutes fills up this bottle at the beginning of the day (times of day, hydration, and personal milk supply make that amount different for different people though). I fed twins, a single child, and now another one with this one. So technically 3 years and 2 months of children drinking.
Besides my tips in the video, here is my milk supply trick: Pump first. When your breast are full, pump first, or at least put the baby on the more “empty” side. Nursing does seem to “let down” milk faster than any kind of pump, and the baby will be satisfied as long as they are getting a tiny bit. Meanwhile, pump the full side until you get what you want. THEN put the baby on that side. The baby will nurse longer to get what they need, and that will slowly increase your milk supply.
I pump until I have 6 ounces every morning before the baby drinks. And I always wake up with that one side more full. The baby always has exactly what she needs, because I always take the same amount, and my body has adjusted accordingly.
[I had to mention that, because with my first, the twins would nurse till it was “gone” and then I would lie them on the bed and cry with them, because they were still hungry and I thought I just couldn’t make enough. I didn’t realize that letting them suck on empty breasts IS EXACTLY what increases your supply. ]
Anyways, every situation is different, but this has been the perfect pump for me.
Imagine waking up refreshed and beautiful and excited to pump away...or not. Forget the advertisements. It is still hard. Pumping is harder than breastfeeding because of the prep and cleaning and juggling machines in addition to babies. It’s one more thing that makes moms such awesome multitaskers. But this one makes it EASIER. Imagine rather waking up tired and grumpy and trying to stay awake sometimes with a baby on one side and a pump on the other. [And sometimes falling asleep and the bottle filling up and running over on your lap] It’s not as easy as nature, but when it is needed, this is the efficient one.

Product Title: Medela Freestyle Breast Pump
Author: Amazon Customer
Review Text:
Summary: I never write reviews but felt I owed it to all the moms that are trying to pick a pump. I have three breast pumps: the Willow, Medela Freestyle and the Medela Sonata. My winner hands down is the Medela Freestyle. I wanted it to be the Willow but it’s not and the Willow is very first generation and has a long way to go. That said the Willows customer service was excellent and I had to call them often because some part of my Willow pump was not working or I was not getting a latch. The Medela pumps are gentler on nipples, easier to use and clean, less expensive and more effective and efficient at pumping.

Who am I? I am a working mom of three kids. I pump once or twice a day at work. My baby was a premie and did not successfully breastfeed until she was six weeks old so for the first 6 weeks I only pumped.

The Medela Freestyle verse the Sonata and compare to Willow:
I also have both of these pumps. I keep the Sonata at work and the Freestyle I keep at home and use when driving or traveling. I just put on my hands free bra and keep one of these hand free bras at home and another st work. I wanted the Willow because I thought it would be easy to stick in my bra and pump at work or driving. It’s not that easy. The Medelas just work every time without the issues of failure to properly latch, etc. There is less frustration with them. I did take the Willow with me on vacation and it was great for those occasional pumps on the go where I didn’t want people to see me pumping. The Sonata is a great pump but you can’t stick it in your purse and go like the Freestyle. The Sonata is a great pump if you not traveling with it much. I typically pump every morning before work too and I stick on my hands free bra and put the Freestyle in my robe pocket, cover up and walk around the kitchen getting breakfast for my older kids. The Willow is more discrete to do this but it was not as comfortable either. I do have larger breast (34 C or D) so maybe if you have smaller breasts it would work better and not pull so much on the nipples. I also tried a different flang size and that didn’t help.

So my winner is the Medela Freestyle and good job mommas for doing your best to try to breast feed. It’s not easy.

Author: KY
Review Text:
I decided on the Freestyle pump after considering the Pump in Style Advanced. From the reviews, it was obvious that the PIS has stronger suction and is a good alternative. However, I decided on this finally due to the size and compactness of the entire package.

The good:
- whole package including a universal voltage pump, all-in-one solution including hands-free package and an ice-bag.
- The pump was easy to use, with illuminated display and simple but versatile function. To my relief, suction was strong enough for expression.
- With the option of suctioning one or both breasts at the same time, I can breastfeed the baby and express from the other breast at the same time.

The not-so-good:
- flimsy hands-free kit - the clamps look like a strange contraption, and although we bought a breastfeeding bra with clasp, the clips tend to be too tight and presvent adequate expression, or too loose and cause leakage while pumping. Based on other reviews, we decided to buy the Easy Expression bra instead.
- The bottles tend to topple over, and with both pumps being used, both bottles tend to topple due to the pull of the suction tubing. A simple stand adaptor like the harmony pump should be included, especially if pumping intermittently.
- Sound: would be noticeable in a quiet environment, e.g., in a toilet cubicle. Otherwise I was not bothered with the sound at all.

Overall we are extremely happy about the Freestyle pump. My suggestion for further improvement:
a) option for a sling instead of a belt clip
b) removable/replaceable battery as the pump tends to lose power especially in heavy use after a while
c) a stand to prevent accidental toppling
d) consider including an easy expression bra (it retails for $26 for one) - way better (and cheaper) than including all the flimsy clip contraptions
e) Including a teat would probably top off this all-in-one kit very well. Even better, include the fantastic "Calma" teat - good marketing strategy if you ask me

Product Title: Medela Freestyle Breast Pump
Review Title: Great pump, not so great valves
Author: Kate
Review Text:
I am exclusively pumping for twins, and have been using a hospital grade pump (Medela Symphony) for the first three months. About a month ago, I bought the Freestyle to be more mobile around the house and on travel. It is a fantastic little machine that has great suction. I have not noticed a drop in supply when I switched from the Symphony to the Freestyle (I log my pumping output, so I'm pretty certain of this). As some reviewers have pointed out, it is louder than the Symphony, but as my engineer husband explains, that is a function of its size: a smaller machine will be louder compared to a bigger one of similar strength. And this pump is pretty strong. Sure, the Symphony is stronger, but I've never been able to use the Symphony at full power anyway; that would just be too uncomfortable.

However, and I think this is why this pump gets such mixed reviews, the valves, which are different from those on other Medela pumps, are a problem. Certain aspects of them are better than the other Medela valves, such as that there are no flimsy plastic flaps. But - if you put together the valves without drying them first, or if you - like many who pump a lot do - keep them in the fridge after each use and only wash them every 24 hours, they will lose (sometimes all) suction. This problem can be fixed relatively easily by unclipping and re-clipping the valve part, but it is still quite annoying, especially when you have to do it several times to make it work. But it can always be fixed pretty quickly, and then the suction is strong. I do not believe that the pump running off a battery is an issue for suction strength, as another reviewer argued; I think the problem is all in the valves. Maybe (probably) the battery loses strength over time, as any battery will, but out of the box, it is good. I hope the battery will hold up for at least a year.

Especially given the problematic design of the valves on the Freestyle - but even if this problem didn't exist - I find it highly annoying that Medela has not made the accessories of this pump compatible with their other products. I already own several sets of accessories for the Symphony pump, and it would be very nice if I could connect these to the Freestyle. The way they have designed it, they force you to buy several different sets of pump accessories if you switch pumps or go back and forth between a hospital grade pump and the Freestyle. While this increases their profits, it's not only expensive but also irritating for the user, who has to keep several different sets of pump parts ready to use.

One other issue with the valve apparatus is that it does indeed leak when you bend over, much worse than the parts of other Medela pumps. The opening is way too big and in the worst possible spot. A pump that is designed to walk around with should not have this issue.

Lastly, I agree with other reviewers that you should absolutely get a hands-free pumping bra. I didn't try the hands-free kit that comes with the Freestyle, but it doesn't look very practical.

Overall, I like this pump. I love the mobility that it allows me, and it does the job quickly and with no difference in output compared to the Symphony. I would recommend it to a friend, with the caveats about the valves outlined above. Maybe Medela will improve their design one day.

Product Title: Medela Freestyle Breast Pump
Review Title: Highly Recommended, Great Pump for Active Moms
Author: Wendy
Review Text:
Pros: Light and portable which is HUGE when taking it back and forth to work, or just moving it from room to room in your home.  I got the same supply from this pump as I did with the hospital-grade Symphony model.  I used it with my twins and I'm using it again with my newborn.

Cons: The clip on the back of the pump is difficult to open so I usually just carry it from place to place, the bra attachment device is cumbersome (a simple pumping bra works better), the bottles will leak if you bend over while pumping or if they tip over with milk in them, and it is on the louder side compared to the Symphony pump.  It is difficult to clean; you need a straw cleaner to get between the grooves under the back cover.  It also won't pump if any of the parts are wet so you really need to get everything clean and dry in between pumpings (to solve for this, I just rinse it most of the time and take it apart for a full cleaning once a day, then sanitize it once a week).

For what it's worth: You can use any normal size bottle as a milk collector, you don't have to use the small bottles it comes with.  The smaller breastshields can be replaced with larger PersonalFit Breastshields without replacing the whole connector device.  Also, some insurance companies will cover most of your breast pump purchase if you have a prescription from your doctor.  Just call them in advance to find out if you have that kind of coverage and how to properly file the paperwork.

Bottom Line:  This is a great pump and I highly recommend it!

Product Title: Medela Freestyle Breast Pump
Review Title: Disappointed - buy the Pump in Style instead
Author: Anne Greenfield
Review Text:
I really wanted to like this product.  My girlfriend used it faithfully for a year so I figured I'd try it too.  Before I bought it, I was borrowing the Pump in Style from another friend and it was working great.  I figured the Freestyle would be the same product as the Pump in Style just cordless.  Wrong!

The accessories are different, and they are a pain in the butt to take apart and clean.  The Pump in Style accessories are so much easier to clean and contain fewer parts.  Furthermore, the design of the accessories are such that they seem to lose suck.  In fact, when I first received the pump, one side didn't even work and Medela had to send me a replacement accessory kit.  (which they overnighted - very nice)  My girlfriend had the same problem with one side not working - a leak in the tubing.  Great quality control, Medela.  I am now on my second set of accessories and noticing what appears to be a suction problem with the left side once again.  And I've only owned the product for two weeks.  :(

Furthermore, my girlfriend's husband is an engineer, and he promptly diagnosed all the problems with the Freestyle.  He actually had a job interview with Medela and explained how they should change their design.  They didn't hire him.

If the hands free option is what appeals to you, you can buy the Simple Wishes hands free pump bra and use it with any pump, thereby making it hands free.  Perfect solution!  Of course, you'll still be tethered to an outlet because only the Freestyle is battery operated, but do you really need to be running around while pumping?  I don't.  I purely want to use the hands free to check email.  Even if you want to pump in your car, you can buy a car outlet adapter for a plug-in pump.

With all that said, I don't feel like the suck on this is too weak.  A few of the negative reviews said it makes your supply dwindle.  That hasn't been the case with me thus far - I pump once a day right after the morning feeding, and I get about 8 ounces.  (I haven't gone back to work yet)  So I think that's pretty good.

BUT, I feed him on the left side before pumping (he usually only takes one side at a feeding) and then pump.  I get about half as much milk on the left side as on the right.  (5 oz on the right and 2.5 oz on the left)  So this could be because that's the side he just fed off of (probably, necause 2.5 oz sounds about right for a feeding for a month old, which is what he is right now) but the left side is also the side I notice the pump suction problems with, so ... I think it might be a combination of the two factors.

If I develop further problems  I am going to call Medela and beg them to exchange my Freestyle for the Pump in Style, but I really hope it doesn't get to that point.

While I wrote this review, I pumped.  And ended up using the stronger pump on both breasts individually because I am worried about the left side losing suction again, so I doubled my pumping time, thereby giving me more time to bash this product.  Kinda ironic, no?

Bottom line is, save yourself the frustration and buy the Pump in Style!!!

Product Title: Medela Freestyle Breast Pump
Review Title: Warning - this is not suitable for travel has a known battery 'reset' issue that takes 24 hours to fix
Author: AmazonQueen
Review Text:
The short review is I would NOT recommend this pump.  Unless you are planning on using it plugged into the mains.  Don't trust it for travel - especially on a long distance flight when you can't plug it in anywhere.  If the battery gets knocked out of connection - it needs a 24 hour plugged in 'reset' to fully recharge.  Which is completely useless when you need a travel pump, and are relying on it.  It crashed out on me on a 15 hour flight and left me unable to pump for 24 hours, and then unable to leave the hotel room with it for another 24 hours.  Any nursing moms can imagine that makes for a very uncomfortable and stressful flight, and then kills milk supply...  Medela confirmed the issue is just part of the design (!) of this freestyle pump.  If you google it there are reviews on moms websites dating back to 2011 with this issue.

Longer review is I want to love this pump, it's now the 2nd one I've owned.  I threw the first one out in the trash in frustration after 2nd baby arrived and I was relying on it exclusively for the first few days.  I got blocked ducts and developed mastitis, which my lactation consultant said was likely due to the pump - I got the hospital grade symphony rental immediately and it resolved.

I needed a travel pump option, and after much research online it looked like this was the (only?!) option for battery operated and could be used internationally.  I had to travel to China this week for work.  I somehow still had the old battery from the original pump I threw out, so decided it would be smart to charge that up and carry a spare battery before I left. I did that - but had some battery error with the old battery displaying on the screen, assumed it had just 'died' as 2+ years old, so switched the original that had been working fine back in.

So then on my 15 hour flight to China, I go to use the bathroom on the plane having not nursed for 5-6 hours at this stage, the pump runs for about 4 mins and just dies on me.  With the battery flashing. Which makes no sense as I had fully charged it before I left.  And I packed the charger in my case knowing I can get at least 4/5 pumping sessions out of it.  Not that there is a power outlet in the plane bathroom anyway.. And even if I had my charger, even charging it at my seat for an hour or so wouldn't have done anything.  As it had to be plugged in for a full undisturbed 24 hours after the battery is disconnected, or just dislodges from connection per Medela support. Which can easily happen when traveling with it they told me.  It's a TRAVEL PUMP!!!

So if the connection between the battery and the pump is ever lost, i.e. you take out the battery (it's a regular looking battery, that has instructions by way of an arrow to open the back to get to it, and tape to help remove it - and no warning to say if you do remove it's a 24 hour 'reset' process). Or the battery connection is lost from a knock say when traveling - it requires a 'reset'.  Meaning you have to plug it back in and leave connected to the wall for a full 24 hours.  If you unplug it to travel anywhere with it, like out of your hotel room - 1) it will probably cut out on you as won't have reset and 2) need to start the 24 hour reset charging process from start again.

Make up your own mind - but this is a stupid flaw for a travel pump.  And if it can't be fixed - Medela should at least make the warnings very clear that removing a battery will do that.  If you buy it because you can't find another option (yet) travel with a backup hand pump or something.  Don't rely on it.
Date: Reviewed in the United States on May 2, 2017

Product Title: Medela Freestyle Breast Pump

Author: Katie M.
Review Text:
I have now been back to work - pumping around two to three times a day five days a week - for five months and I feel that I can accurately review the Freestyle. I breastfed exclusively for six month before introducing solids and continue to only bf (pump while at work) now that we have introduced solids. So I use my pump - A LOT.

At first I liked the Freestyle. I bought the Medela Bustier to allow hands-free pumping. But one day while at work I realized I had forgotten my tubing at home. I rushed out to buy tubing only to find that Medela doesn't sell tubing for the Freestyle in stores - you have to specially order it from them. I do not think that is the case with the tubing for the Pump In Style. So that was my first issue with the pump. I also quickly learned that there are a TON of parts to clean with the Freestyle that I don't think you have to clean with the other double Medela pumps. Another issue when you have to pump three times a day at work and have a limited window for pumping.

A few weeks ago I noticed that the adapter cord on my pump was fraying. So I contacted Medela and they sent me a new cord. In that time, too, my battery was having trouble charging, I assumed because of the frayed cord. So I couldn't pump on battery power.

Product Title: Medela Freestyle Breast Pump

Review Text:
I've been using this pump now for more than 6 months.  So far, the only parts I've had to replace are the soft fit shields which tend to warp after a few short weeks.  You can still use the shields after they warp though and have not noticed that this defect affects the performance of the pump.  As a working mom, I use this 2-3 times per day. I have not had any big problems with decreased supply as long as I nurse frequently with baby when we're together. I can say that I can pump just as much now with this pump as I could 3-4 months ago. This has been a good pump for the last 4 months but recently the battery has stopped taking charge and although we've followed the process for "resetting" it, it's dead.
