The good is that the pump seems strong,  it's portable (until the battery dies), it's lightweight and small and two bottles can be filled at the same time.

The quality seems good (except for the rubber gaskets & plastic encasements that snap around the gasket).

I would recommend this product but after 4 months and the two issues I've mentioned I'd be hesitant to.  We'll wait to see how their support shakes out.
Date: Reviewed in the United States on July 25, 2011

Product Title: Medela Freestyle Breast Pump
Review Title: Unfortunately the best portable pump - Medela needs to improve durability/quality
Author: Eric
Review Text: I am a mom of 3 little boys and a physician. I have limited time to pump and find myself pumping in odd places and so portability and use without plugging in is important to me (I would only recommend this product if you are in a similar need to be able to pump anywhere situation). Unfortunately this is the best product out there if you want something portable and small. It is loud but it works well and allows me to pump quickly anywhere. The big downside to this pump is that it is expensive and it doesn't last.  I know because I have now purchased 4 of these over the past 5 years (now on baby #3). My first 2 pumps each lasted through 8 months of heavy use (lasting through 1 baby each) before breaking but my 3rd pump only lasted 2 months before breaking. When I called Medela they told me I needed a new motor unit but it was not in stock and that it would take weeks to get me the new part. I can't go weeks without a pump and so I just had to purchase my 4th Medela Freestyle. I wish there was a better option for a portable pump, if there was I would have bought it 3 pumps ago.
Date: Reviewed in the United States on January 11, 2016

Product Title: Medela Freestyle Breast Pump
Author: Mariana Rotondo
Review Text:
When I was pregnant I made thousands plans, read books, articles, subscribed online website, etc... only to find out that once my little girl was born she came with a plan of her own!
So my plan to breastfeed exclusively went down the drain when I could not give her all that she needed. Sadly I had to give her additional formula (use natural nipple for the bottles, it helps). It is true that the more you breastfeed the more you produce, you may not increase as much as you want but you do increase production. I started out with an electric single pump (I got as a gift) but ended up buying a double pump because time is VERY IMPORTANT and RARE. This Medela Freestyle pump lets me pump fast and I can also multitask, not many things but you learn to appreciate all the details you usually got done before your baby.
Great buy, easy to clean, easy to carry around... haven't used the cooler yet but it is great to have so many bottles.
Date: Reviewed in the United States on July 14, 2013

Product Title: Medela Freestyle Breast Pump
Review Title: Good pump and the battery lasts a long time
Author: Vanessa D.
Review Text:
It's a good pump but ONLY if you pump infrequently. If you plan on pumping daily don't get this one. Plus this particular pump has parts that are not interchangeable with other madela pumps, so if you end up renting a hospital grade pump you'll need to buy an entirely new set of adapters.

Update:
I really like this pump. The actual pump is super light and small, so I pump while doing things around the house. I plug it in and charge overnight and it lasts for over a week (pumping 2-3x/day for 15 minutes). I love that! I gave it 4 stars because the parts get worn out and I spend time adjusting and playing with membranes and parts to get the suction right. Once it works you’re golden, but it takes a while to do it. I use this to pump while driving too because it’s so small. I just stick it in the cup holder.
Date: Reviewed in the United States on January 1, 2017

Product Title: Medela Freestyle Breast Pump
Review Title: Awesome pump, would recommend to friends!
Author: sheenastyles
Review Text: I bought this pump in 2011 and have used it with my 2 children I have had since then. It's incredibly convenient to use, I like the fact that I can plug it in to recharge the battery and then take it with me out and about and use a few times before having to recharge. I like the letdown setting, and its nice you can choose the different suction rates. The pump itself it small so it's easy to throw in a purse etc. My husband's boss is a research fanatic, so they did some serious digging around when it came to finding the perfect pump, so we took their lead and bought this one. I used it about twice a day for 7 months with my first child, and about 3 times a week with my second and I'm not working full time anymore, and the battery, motor, etc have all been fine and never died. Still in good shape, and if I had to, I would definitely buy this pump again! My only complaint is that when the pump dies and the battery needs to be recharged, I have to have it plugged in for a full 24 hours or the pump will just die, but other then that, it's worked great.
Date: Reviewed in the United States on December 2, 2013

Product Title: Medela Freestyle Breast Pump
Review Title: Pisa, freestyle both great pumps and equally comparable production
Author: Julia Gilday
Review Text:
I am exclusively pumping for twins. They are one month old. I have researched pumps extenaively and had the opportunity to use ameda hospital grade, medela pump in style advanced and freestyle. I pump every 3 hours for at least 15-20 minutes.
Pisa: strong, small, easy to clean, fewer parts than freestyle, quiet, portable but I have only used plugged in to outlet. I recommend this pump and know many moms who use it exclusively.
Freestyle: just as strong suction as the Pisa and hospital grade, louder than the other pumps but I love this pump because I can walk around house, vacuum, do laundry and soothe crying babies while pumping. Because of the ability to be mobile, I usually end up pumping for longer time periods as well because I am not confined to my chair. Provides great mobility.
I use both the Pisa and the freestyle and get the same milk production and output with them both. I read all of the reviews for these pumps, most are negative for the freestyle so I was hesitant to buy, but after personally using and comparing it to other pumps, I found that the Pisa and freestyle are equal when it comes to suction and milk output!
Date: Reviewed in the United States on July 27, 2014

Product Title: Medela Freestyle Breast Pump
Review Title: Great for first time mothers who need some additional 'help'.
Author: bmbranno
Review Text: I got this for my daughter-in-law as her baby was born prematurely at 33 weeks and breast-feeding was nearly impossible at times.  Since the baby was in NICU for over four months my daughter-in-law would do a lot of pumping and take the milk in to the NICU nurses for feedings.  It never let her down, either!  She was very pleased with this breast pump and feels it made her journey as a first time mama with a preemie baby much easier and more bonding.  Great product that has been reliable since the first day she used it, and even when she went back to work as a teacher and the baby came home she used this pump.  It allowed her to keep the baby on breast milk for over a year even with the babysitter.  I would highly recommend this unit for all first time moms.
Date: Reviewed in the United States on March 17, 2013

Product Title: Medela Freestyle Breast Pump
Review Title: If you don't want a lot of milk quickly, this is the pump for you.
Author: Lauren Hetherington
Review Text:
I don't usually write reviews but I wanted to share my experience to hopefully save some other new moms the headache I went through. This pump is decent if you have an oversupply situation or missed a feeding. It's portable, which is why I got it since I travel for work. The only problem is it's weak and you wind up spending twice as long for half as much milk.

And as other reviewers have said, the pump motor itself dies/weakens over time. I used this pump for only 5 months before pumping sessions started to get rough. I was worried my supply was going down. I called Medela to troubleshoot. (They were very responsive and kept sending me replacement parts to see if something was broken and are now sending me a new Freestyle, which I'm not going to use.) After several weeks of this nonsense, I broke down and bought the Pump In Style to protect what little supply I had left. OMG, now that's a good pump! Twice as much milk in half the time. It was clearly not a supply problem for me. It was a pump problem.

Don't waste your money on this pump. Get the Pump in Style and the hands free pumping bra. Much better than this pump.
Date: Reviewed in the United States on October 23, 2013

Product Title: Medela Freestyle Breast Pump
Author: Andrew Park
Review Text:
(Andrew's wife writing this review)

For those who are contemplating between the Pump In Style versus the Freestyle - let me help you.  If you want a product that will pump quicker and pump more milk - buy the Pump In Style.  I consistently use both (one for the office, one for home) and I can tell you that the Pump In Style is more efficient.  What it lacks in "freestyling" - the machine makes up 100% in efficiency.  I usually pump 5 oz in 10 minutes with the Pump In Style.  It takes me 25-30 minutes to pump the same 5 oz with the FreeStyle.  Those extra minutes may not seem like a lot to some - but to every mom who is pumping multiple times a day, this adds up big time.

Disappointed by this purchase. I would give it 2 stars but since I can brush my teeth while pumping, I am bumping it up to 3 stars.

Grateful that I have my pump in style in the office to save my supply.
Date: Reviewed in the United States on September 30, 2012

Product Title: Medela Freestyle Breast Pump
Review Title: As powerful as the hospital grade pump
Author: Kendra
Review Text: I had this pump with my first child and really enjoyed the portability and small size.  I had supply issues with her but I really felt this had nothing do with my pump.  I have a friend who with her second child rented a hospital grade pump and also used this pump when traveling.  With my second child I really wanted to make sure I was doing everything I could to keep up with him so I also rented a hospital grade pump.  After using both it and this pump for a month I felt like this was absolutely as effective for me as the hospital grade pump and infinitely more convenient.  I can pump anywhere and it's super convenient for travel.  I would (and do) recommend it to anyone.  For those that say it doesn't have as  much suction I guess it's possible that I just have a really easy time pumping but my pumping volumes and my impression of the suction were very equivalent with this pump and the hospital grade pump
Date: Reviewed in the United States on August 6, 2013

Product Title: Medela Freestyle Breast Pump
Author: Jon Leach
Review Text: This pump is amazing.  When I had my third baby in the hospital my husband and the lactation consultant help me hook it up and use it the freestyle way.  I felt it was very humiliating and overwhelming at first because it takes awhile to learn how to hook everything in place. I also felt silly when I looked at myself in the mirror with tubes and things hooked up to my bra/breasts. Despite all of that it is well worth all the trouble.  Now that I have used it several times holding it in place I decided to try it by hooking it to my bra and doing dishes, etc. while pumping.  I am amazed at all the time I am saving.  I pumped an entire bottle as we drove to church and then was able to feed it to my son in church.  I couldn't ask for a better machine.  This pump must be designed by someone who understands what it is like to be a breastfeeding MOM.
Date: Reviewed in the United States on October 7, 2009

Product Title: Medela Freestyle Breast Pump
Author: Noaa
Review Text:
I can't say enough good things about this pump!!!

I was on the verge of giving up breastfeeding altogether. This pump brought me back from the edge! No pain, no fuss. Super quiet pump, very portable, very efficient. They say that the battery lasts only four 15 minute pumps - my experience is that it lasts much longer. Pumping 50 minutes a day the pump lasted me 3 days with no charging.

The whole issue of "let down" hasnt been an issue for me at all with this pump. It actually vibrates instead of just suctioning, and I found that no matter what I'm doing or thinking about or what state I'm in, it always empties me out very quickly and efficiently. 10 minutes of pumping 5 times a day and I pump enough to feed my 10 week old!

I never write reviews but if I can influence one woman to keep breastfeeding by using this pump, it's a win :)
Date: Reviewed in the United States on September 11, 2016

Product Title: Medela Freestyle Breast Pump
Review Title: believe the naysayers and save your money
Author: Elizabeth
Review Text:
I toyed with a different title for this review - "So Loud Our Downstairs Neighbor Can Hear It," but changed it because this pump has more problems than just noise.  If it was as loud as it is but actually made pumping easier, I probably wouldn't be writing this.  But not only is this pump unbelievably loud - it also has terrible suction.

I recently returned to work.  Before that I had been using a friend's used Medela Pump in Style (which she used through two children) - which still works wonderfully. (I just bought all new attachments for it).

But lugging it back and forth to work was proving very challenging.  So I decided to buy another one and chose the top of the line - assuming that the price would guarantee pumping success.  I even went as far to assume that it would be a better experience than the used pump.  Was I wrong.  The pump is ineffective, does not have good suction (I use it at the top suction level), and is causing my milk to lessen.  I also now hand pump after using this to continue to pump.  Then, to add insult to injury, our neighbor downstairs emailed us last night to ask us what the horribly annoying noise she hears coming from our home is (I took this one home from my office because the first time I used it here, the noise reverberated all over my office).

I am very disappointed in both myself and in Medela.  In myself, because I thought I was better at research than I must be - because I somehow ordered this pump without reading all of the negative reviews about it, reviews I agree with completely.  Please save yourself a lot of money and do not order this pump.
Date: Reviewed in the United States on April 3, 2012

Product Title: Medela Freestyle Breast Pump
Review Title: I was given another one and this thing is awesome. I understand why it's one of the most ...
Author: Natasha
Review Text: I had to return this BUT, I was given another one and this thing is awesome. I understand why it's one of the most popular ones without being a hospital grade machine. It's pretty close. The entire set up is very intuitive and from what I've seen, it should last for a very long time. I had an old one that I used for two children previously and it was great then. I feel like they updated something with the motor as it's not quite as loud as it was before. It's still a fairly loud machine but it never bothered me much. The freezer pack isn't the best quality. I think I might replace it with something that will last a bit longer, especially on a hot day. Still would suggest this to other people looking for a convenient on-the-go unit.
Date: Reviewed in the United States on July 19, 2017

Product Title: Medela Freestyle Breast Pump
Author: DenverMom
Review Text:
I had read many reviews on this pump and was expecting a powerful and quiet pump.
Boy was I wrong.  I actually cried the first time I used it.  My hand-me-down pump-in-style is equally powerful (and I'm the SEVENTH mom who has used it!) and the 'shush-shush' sound of the pump in style is much more tolerable than the 'wha-u-ga, wha-u-ga' sound of the Freestyle.

I travel a lot for work and was looking forward to the portability of the freestyle.  I read a review that said it was quiet enough to discreetly use under a nursing cover in the airport.  No way, no how!! I'd have people calling security!!

Granted, on the lowest level, it is very quiet, but gets markedly louder as you increase the pump level.  I had to use level 9 (the highest) to achieve the same level of suction as my older-than-dirt, seven-times-used pump in style. And at level 9, you wouldn't want anyone within 50 feet of you.  I even tried burying it in my bag with towels and a scarf wrapped around  it and I could still hear it thumping and vibrating away.

So in short, if you are using this pump in the privacy of your own home, and you're looking for portability and the battery option; get this pump.  Otherwise, go for the pump-in-style. I'm so dissapointed that I spent over $300 on this pump that I now hope to sell on ebay.

Pros:
pump can be used in any bag
rechargeable battery

Cons:
NOISY!!!!
Weak suction (compared to others)
Expensive
Date: Reviewed in the United States on March 22, 2011

Product Title: Medela Freestyle Breast Pump
Author: Kristin
Review Text:
I got this pump with my first child so I could pump while doing other things like cleaning, dishes and while on my 30 minute commute to and from work (using a hands free pumping bra of course).  I loved the ease of it but like other reviews say, the suction doesn't stay strong for long and I'm beginning to think that's y I started having supply issues later on.

That being said, I still really like this pump and will get another for our next baby, HOWEVER, I will use the freestyle more as a secondary pump for when I want to pump while up and moving  I will use the pump in style the majority of the time and for longer periods of time, but i think it will still help to have the hands free up and about system to be able to pump and keep supply up when I wouldn't have been able to pump otherwise.
Date: Reviewed in the United States on March 10, 2013

Product Title: Medela Freestyle Breast Pump
Author: kdjones4
Review Text:
I love this pump! I use this in combination with the Simple Wishes D Lite Hands Free Breastpump Bra and I clip the pump onto my belt and I'm free to walk around the house and do whatever I want while I pump. I'm so glad I didn't get the pump attached to the bag! It's nice not to worry about carrying the bag around while I pump. The only thing that would make this product better would be a better clip on the back of the pump. I can't just clip the pump onto my pants because it's too unstable and the pump falls off easily. I put a belt on and the pump seems to stay clipped onto a belt much better.

Sanitizing everyday is kind of a pain. I would reccommend getting a microwavable bottle sanitizer and putting the breast pump supplier in there to sanitize. It's so much easier than boling water or using the $5 sanitizing bags!
Date: Reviewed in the United States on October 10, 2013

Product Title: Medela Freestyle Breast Pump
Review Title: The best pump on the market
Author: Dovile
Review Text: I hesitated several months before finally deciding to buy my own breast pump. I had no question as to what brand, as I was told by several experts, Medela was the best. I chose Medela Freestyle mainly due to its mobility: my son went on nursing strike when he was 3 months old, so I had to rely on the pump for constant breast milk supply for him. I wanted to have a reliable, strong pump, that could go with me wherever. Once I got my Freestyle, I was not disappointed. I used it daily, 6-7 times  a day, took it on the road, to restaurants, planes etc. It worked perfect and even exceeded my expectations. I did have a problem with the battery 3-weeks after the purchase. But Medela customer service shipped me a replacement pump the day I complained to them about it. Since then, it worked perfectly.
Date: Reviewed in the United States on September 4, 2012

Product Title: Medela Freestyle Breast Pump
Review Title: Not as good as expected for what I was told was the best commercial alternative to a hospital pump
Author: Eileen Kirkland
Review Text: Weak pump, arrives without nipples, rings and keep-clean caps you'd need to actually start feeding. I'm using it for twins and have had leaks that lead to spilled breast milk if I don't keep the parts perfectly upright while pumping.  (I purchased the most commonly needed replacement parts right away - which came with 2 more bottle bases, so I'm now *five* nipples, rings, tops, etc. short of what I need to make and use six bottles at a time.  The bottles that come with the pump have colored measurement numbers and are much easier to read than the clear plastic embossed ones that come with the replacement parts.) Overall, I'm glad I have a pump, but think I could have done better for the price.  It should be clearer that you don't have all that you need to start pumping and feeding if you buy this approximately $340 setup.
Date: Reviewed in the United States on December 30, 2013

Product Title: Medela Freestyle Breast Pump
Author: Pegaus28
Review Text: This pump is awesome, so convenient to travel with and even just walking around the house without having to be plugged in or have a bulky machine. The problem however is that the warranty on the motor is only good for one year. If you want to breastfeed more than one child or for longer than a year than you run the risk that the pump will no longer be covered if the motor dies. In my case it did in less than a year and a half. I was really hoping it would last at least through my first child if not into future children but not so lucky. I did buy it again because I know that it works well while it works, but I gotta say it is a lot more expensive than i even realized if you have to replace it every year.
Date: Reviewed in the United States on February 7, 2013

Product Title: Medela Freestyle Breast Pump
Review Title: "what's in the box" isn't what's in the box
Author: ellieray
Review Text:
The pump itself is great.  It is very portable, has variable settings for suction, and it isn't too loud. My only qualm and the reason I couldn't give it more than 3 stars is that what the description says comes in the box...isnt what comes in the box.  It states that it comes with softfit breastshields.  It does not.  It comes with 2 sets of 'personal fit' shields, 24mm and 27mm, which are hard plastic.

They work....for a while but at least for me I have to hold and massage my breast inorder to coax the milk out of the ducts in order to empty the breast...which kind of defeats the purpose of a hands free pumping system.

Its still a good pump and I would buy it again...but you have to buy the soft fit shields seperately.
Date: Reviewed in the United States on February 17, 2012

Product Title: Medela Freestyle Breast Pump
Review Title: Depends on what you plan on using it for.
Author: Caitlin
Review Text:
I bought this pump because I have a preemie and am exclusively pumping. I have a hospital grade pump at the bedside and have a Medela Instyle set up at home but wanted something more mobile for on the go pumping. I was hoping I could pump and vacuum or atleast walk around the house. I DO like how small and portable it is. For that I would give it 5 stars. I knew it wouldn't be as powerful as my hospital grade pump, but would give it 3.75 stars for its suction power. However, if you move or slightly lean forward while pumping the milk will spill out of the back and get in the tubing since it is not a closed system. To me, this defeats the convenience of pumping on the go. I have a low supply to begin with and any wasted/lost milk is a sad affair. I would not use this pump as a primary pump... it's simply not strong enough. I have the Medela Instyle and it works much better.

If you plan on using this as an occasional pump and have some extra money to spend on it (and don't plan on moving much) go for it.
Date: Reviewed in the United States on June 26, 2017

Product Title: Medela Freestyle Breast Pump
Review Title: Lansinoh is Much better than medela freestyle and much cheaper
Author: Jeffrey and Sandra
Review Text: Lansinoh is Much better than medela freestyle and much cheaper!!!  Medela paid a lot of $$ for the advertisement I'm sure. Medela is much louder than Lansinoh,  mine kind  of broke within a week, I was only able to pump if it was plugged in as it says battery is not charged, today I discovered that there was mold when I took it appart, it explains why my baby was so sick for days. I boiled it and put it back together, sadly the suction is not working at all anymore. I didn't know that they match Amazon prime price, this way it's much cheaper, medela  was almost $500 and Lansinoh is $150 at toys r us.Only can give 1 star for their bottle as the niple goes in every 20 seconds when baby is sucking on it and Lansinoh 5 starts it has holes on the nipple to let the air out. I'm glad I was able to compare these two.
Date: Reviewed in the United States on March 17, 2016

Product Title: Medela Freestyle Breast Pump
Author: AP from DC
Review Text:
I know there are mixed reviews on this pump but I found that for my needs it was very good. It can hold an 8 hour battery charge so you dont have to constantly have the plug with you. The small pump I could carry around easily by attaching it to my waist and I found that it had adequate suction. I did find that the sheilds it comes with (the soft sheilds) did not work as well for me as the harder ones (they are interchangable) and sometimes woman find that they need to increase the size of the sheild that comes with the pump. Ask a lactation consultant about what size of sheild you might need.

Otherwise, its a great and simply pump that for the money was pretty good.
Date: Reviewed in the United States on August 3, 2011

Product Title: Medela Freestyle Breast Pump
Review Title: Read the Bad Reviews...They are 100% Accurate!!!!
Author: Stephanie H.
Review Text:
I decided to 'upgrade' to this pump with my second child. A huge mistake/disappoint/waste of time! I really wish I had taken the poor reviews seriously because they were 100% correct. The suction on this product is terrible and needs to be adjusted my manufacturers. My first pump was Medela In Style Advance (tote bag) and it has worked very well...still works very well. But with insurance providing a new pump for the birth of my second child I decided to opt for the newer model and not have to be restricted to staying by an outlet. The first time I used it I was still charging the battery and thought that the charge should probably be complete before it works well...so I waited the full 24 hours and tried again on the second night. Thank goodness I still had my old pump as an option because I would have been miserable and in a lot of pain. To compare, I pumped 8 minutes (the time feature is handy on the Freestyle model, but not really worth it) to produce 1.5 ounces on the left side and not even enough to cover the bottom of the storage bottle on the right side. With the In Style model in 8 minutes I was able to produce 4+ ounces on both sides.

Please do not waste your money until the company does some adjusting to the product. They really have great customer service and I have never been disappointed with their products until now, it's only a matter of time until they correct the flaw.
Date: Reviewed in the United States on August 12, 2016

Product Title: Medela Freestyle Breast Pump
Review Title: Professional breast pump and easy to use
Author: arcgod
Review Text:
My wife has used it for about 5 months and she recommends it.
1. You can choose a different size of shields in order for better pumping and less hurting. Cheap pumps don't have such replacable parts.
2. Easier to adjust the pressure with LCD screen than Swing.
3. Easy to clean up with baby bottle soap.
4. Double pump. You can use it for single side as well.
5. Good battery life, as for now. A full charge lasts two days with more than 10 pump cycles one day.
6. Global voltage adapter. Convenient for international buyers.
7. Quite durable. I tried sucking water with it to test whether it was really working when first time used. Stupid... A lot of water went through the tube and inside the pump... But after drying it up, the pump has kept alive and working:)
Date: Reviewed in the United States on December 18, 2014

Product Title: Medela Freestyle Breast Pump
Author: HLA
Review Text: I would highly recommend this pump to all women who plan on returning to work and pumping at the same time. This pump is very efficient. It works really well and it is light weight. Since it is a freestlye and not attached to any bags I can wear different bags to work to match my outfit (I don't have to carry it in the nursing bag that it comes with). I know the price is a bit steep but for the amount of milk that I am able to get it's worth it. I pump every three hours and I am able to get at least 4oz of milk per pumping session. It only takes me 10 minutes to pump per session. Also it is not painful at all!
Date: Reviewed in the United States on September 12, 2011

Product Title: Medela Freestyle Breast Pump
Review Title: I have had this for 18 months now. I ...

I am due for another baby in September 2016 so we will see if it  still works.

Product Title: Medela Freestyle Breast Pump

I went cheap my first pregnancy and got an avent .. I had to pump 20 min or moreand the pump had zero capability of being portable, had a ton of parts to clean .. Just a huge pain.  This pump is small, completely portable, and the charge lasts at least a week or 2 when I only pump about 2-3 times per day. I recommend this pump 100%!

Product Title: Medela Freestyle Breast Pump

Review Text: This is a very good pump, very comparable to the Medela Symphony in terms of suction power. I like this pump alot, but I found it doesn't come with all the pieces the description says it does. My kit was missing the gray hands free adapters, spare pump kit, and car adapter. When I opened it up, there was a pink paper that says you cannot return the product due to the nature of it, but who knows. This product would have been 5 stars had it actually come with everything in the description.
Date: Reviewed in the United States on March 9, 2012

Product Title: Medela Freestyle Breast Pump
Author: Orange Tree
Review Text:
Great pump so far! I have been using the Freestyle for two weeks now and I am very satisfied with it. Compared to the Medela Pump in Style that I had previously, this one is so much more convenient to use. No more being attached to a large bag, no more looking for electric outlets, no more dealing with tiny parts/membranes.
It has great suction power - I am comfortable using the power settings 3-5 currently. I like the stimulation phase/expression phase features and the timer as well. The noise level seems to be about the same or maybe slightly lower than my PIS was, but the type of sound this one makes is much less annoying for me.
Date: Reviewed in the United States on September 22, 2010

Product Title: Medela Freestyle Breast Pump
Review Title: This pump is wonderful. I had been renting a Medela Lactina hospital ...
Author: Jennaya Fernane
Review Text: This pump is wonderful.  I had been renting a Medela Lactina hospital grade pump, which was great, until I went back to work and had to start travelling.  I have found the Freestyle is comparable to my Lactina in suction, which was my biggest worry.  I love how compact and portable it is. Product Title: Medela Freestyle Flex Breast Pump, Closed System Quiet Handheld Portable Double Electric Breastpump, Mobile Connected Smart Pump with Touch Screen LED Display and USB Rechargeable Battery
Author: Nick Tewell
Review Text:
I used a lesser known Avent pump for my first two kiddos that worked perfectly- I had an abundant supply and despite working full time and exclusively breast-feeding/pumping, I was able to keep my kids on frozen milk for 3-4 months after stopping pumping at 1 years old. It was 5 and 7 years ago though so I figured I’d try the Medela pump that had been hyped up by so many and that was wireless, which the Avent was not. At 4 months post partum, this thing has left me in tears of frustration on more than one occasion due to several design flaws.

1- the flanges suck (and by suck I mean they suck at sucking!). The ones this pump comes with (2 different sizes) don’t fit well as they are hardened plastic with no silicone fitting over top to really form to your breast. The Avent and others come with this extra piece that not only molds better to your body to get better suction but is much more comfortable. As a result, I’m not convinced that buying other hard plastic sizes would be the fix for this and I think I’m missing out on ounces that could be banked.

2- the tubing easily gets moisture trapped in it, presenting a contamination hazard and the possibility of destroying the lithium battery if it gets sucked into the machine. I’m not even sure how this is happening half the time as my pieces are fully air dried (maybe condensation somehow??) but on several occasions I’ve started pumping only to see water droplets in the tubing and had to literally hold the phalanges to my boobs to catch letdown milk while using an air compressor in the garage to blow out the lines (helpful tip if you’re being faced with having to buy new tubing). Neat trick but not cute, not convenient, and not possible if I weren’t working from home.

3- the phalange/bottle weight ratio is off so they tip over far too easily, causing precious milk to be spilled (cue the tears part). This would RARELY happen with my Avent pump, likely because while they held the same ounces, the bottles and phalanges were shorter and heavier. The Medela does come with a plastic “cup holder” type thing but there is no suction cup or anything on it to give it some weight or stability and it really feels like just a waste of plastic.

Overall I think my supply has suffered because of this stupid pump. Lesson learned- don’t fix what’s not broken!

**For reference if it’s helpful, I am usually a 36C bra size**

Product Title: Medela Freestyle Flex Breast Pump, Closed System Quiet Handheld Portable Double Electric Breastpump, Mobile Connected Smart Pump with Touch Screen LED Display and USB Rechargeable Battery
Review Title: A FTM's Best Friend - Portable, insanely quiet, powerful suction, increased my supply.
Author: Isthatpaleo?
Review Text:
TLDR: I am an exclusively pumping mama who also has the Willow, Lansinoh Smart Pump, and Medela Pump in Style (old version from a friend). Let me tell you -- I use the Medela Freestyle Flex for all of my pumping sessions. It's the quietest of all, incredibly portable, increased my supply, and customer service is amazing.

Reasons why I love this pump -
While this pump is a traditional breast pump (it sticks out of your bra while you're pumping, and you have to watch how far you bend over so you don't spill milk out of the tiny holes in the connectors), it is slightly less annoying than other traditional pumps. The updated pumping parts are more intuitive (and therefore, easier) to assemble than previous versions, and the accessory parts are of nice quality. It is *insanely* quiet, and super portable (Yes, you can take it out of the house and pump, say, in your car, but you still can't pump in at like, the grocery store, because it sticks out the front of your special pumping bra and there's a fair amount of your breasts/nipples that is visible). The built-in, rechargeable lithium battery is really powerful, so suction power is great, even disconnected from the wall. It has a traditional USB plug on one end (this is how I charge in my car), and a USB-C plug on the other end. Another bonus - I think it increased my milk supply. The buttons can be a little picky - just make sure you don't stash the button surface pressed up against your body while you're wearing it lol. Customer service is *exceptional* - at least for me in the US, they overnighted me a new one when needed.

And while we're on the subject of Medela, let me say that Medela is the brand that most hospitals use, which should tell you something about its quality, durability, and consistency. The pump I used right after I delivered, for example, was this huge machine that was on wheels - I was later told it was the Cadillac of pumps lol. While you definitely don't need to get this massive pump for yourself at home (the price tag on it is like $2-3k), I do recommend the Medela brand in general - they just know what they're doing, and the Freestyle Flex is the most portable pump they have right now. And bonus - you can use a 20% off coupon at Buy Buy Baby.

While the Freestyle Flex is more of an "obvious" pump when compared to the Willow (which I also have) because the Flex is a traditional pump that sticks out of your pumping bra, rather than getting tucked inside, it is actually still quite portable, and also *insanely* quiet. It is the quietest of all 4 pumps that I have. It also has a slightly smaller profile than the versions before it, as well as other traditional breast pumps. And by that I mean, it doesn't stick out in front of you as much - don't get me wrong, it still sticks out, which is annoying, but slightly less so. Also, with all breast pumps, you really can't bend over, otherwise the milk will spill out some tiny hole somewhere at the top that I can never really locate lol. The Medela flex lets me bend slightly more forward before it spills. The fact that it doesn't stick out as much, and lets you bend forward slightly more may seem like only slight advantages on paper, but in everyday use, they actually are huge. It means that I am able to bend slightly more forward in order to pick up or put down the baby (saving my back), and I am able to hold her slightly more comfortably & securely because they don't stick out as far. Basically, multitasking is slightly easier - I am able to do laundry a little bit easier, or make a sandwich, or brush my teeth, all because they don't stick out as much to get in my way, and I can bend down a little bit further before I start panicking that I'm going to spill milk all over.

The other thing that I really love about the Freestyle Flex is that I swear it increased my supply. I am one of the lucky ones whose body makes enough milk, so I was making about 32oz a day with my other pumps (for reference, my lactation consultant told me that anywhere between 28 - 32 oz a day was a good goal). After 6 weeks with the Flex, my average daily output has increased to 36oz (for my little one, that's an entire extra feeding). Obviously this isn't guaranteed for everyone, but I can only report on my own experience, so there you have it.  
**UPDATE** After 2 mos, my supply has increased another 2 oz, for a total average of 38 oz per 24-hour period. I've literally changed nothing else, so I kinda feel like it's the pump??

Beyond all that, it holds a charge well - I can go 3 sessions before I feel like I need to plug it back in, and it charges via USB-C. It also can be plugged into the car (if your car as a USB slot, or via an adapter), since it has a regular USB plug on the other end - amazingly portable! The pump itself is also quite small and slim, so it fits in pockets really well, including pants pockets (the back one). I even have a pair of yoga pants that have side pockets down the leg, and it fits in *those* small pockets (Kindred Bravely high-waist yoga pants - highly recommend!). 

Finally, I'll say that all of the accessory parts for the Medela are the best out of all of the traditional pumps that I've tried. The collection bags are better quality, the tubing, the little bottles for collecting the milk, even the lids - everything is just better designed, and better quality. Honestly, for as much as I rave about the Medela, they really should be paying me lol. The Willow actually is fairly nice quality as well, though the collection bags felt a little chintzy. And sidebar - the best storage bags (for freezing, essentially), in my opinion, are actually the Dr. Brown's bags (link below). And yes, you can mix and match for storage bags only - you'll still have to pump into whatever plastic container or storage bag comes with your pump, but after that, you can dump that milk into any plastic bag for freezing. 

I've had my Freestyle Flex for over 6 weeks now, and I can tell you that the *only* negative thing I can say about it is that the buttons can be a little overly-sensitive. I occasionally change the settings while the pump is in my zip-up pocket if the buttons accidentally get bumped in just the right way *through* my clothes. Easy fix - just tap another button to undo the accidental settings change and you're good to go again - but still, slightly annoying.

Finally (finally!) a word on their customer service - Because of some dumb way I was initially carrying around the pump when I first got it, I thought the buttons weren't responding to my presses, so I acutally ended up retruning the first pump that I got. This process was *seamless*. Medela customer service is EXCELLENT. I contacted them both via online chat and email, and they were super nice and responsive, and sent me a replacement pump next-day-air, so I had a new pump literally the very next day. I also found out that their pumps have a *one year* warranty - all I had to do was take a screen shot of my Amazon invoice and I was good to go. Anyway, I think you can tell a lot about a company based on their customer service, and Medela is the real deal. Not surprising, though - I looked it up, and turns out, Medela was the first company to design & sell electric breast pumps for home-use in the early 90s (before that, electric breast pumps were relegated to the hospital). And home-use pumps - get this - were all manual before roughly 1991 *shudder*. We all need to thank our mamas for having to deal with manual breast milk expression for allllll thooooooose yeaaaarrrrrssss. 

Ok, that's it! Congrats for making it all the way to the end! And also - YOU GOT THIS, MAMA!!!!

Product Title: Medela Freestyle Flex Breast Pump, Closed System Quiet Handheld Portable Double Electric Breastpump, Mobile Connected Smart Pump with Touch Screen LED Display and USB Rechargeable Battery
Author: Laura Gajauskas
Review Text:
There are a lot of things I love about this pump! I used the the Medela Pump In Style for many months, until I got this pump. Here are my list of pros and cons:
(*I was given the pump to test and review.  I am not a Medela employee, and this my honest review!)

PROS
-Portability! It’s a game changer to be able to move around and not be stuck sitting next to an outlet.  You definitely need a good hands-free bra, but the portability has allowed me to do chores while pumping, or easily take the pump with me when going somewhere.  It’s also much smaller than the PISA
-Battery life is good! I often charge it after a couple pumps (and I pump for 30 minutes at a time), but I would guess it could last for multiple pumps… if you use the app/bluetooth connection, it tells you the exact battery life percentage which is very helpful! It has a USB charger which is also helpful
-Parts are easier to clean than the PISA.  I felt like the PISA had hard-to-reach crevices that would build up milk residue… I haven’t found that with these parts
-I love the bag and cooler it comes with… definitely helpful/useful for traveling
-suction is good, every so often I have to adjust the flanges to get correct suction)… but I feel less discomfort with this pump even when I have it on the highest level.
-Bluetooth connection to the app is helpful for tracking pumps. I also like you can see how many minutes you've pumped by just looking at the pump…. I ALWAYS forget the time I start pumping, even if I look at the clock 5 times… when you are sleep deprived, it is helpful to not have to think much about tracking time!
-You can easily switch back and forth to to let down mode, and there are 9 suction levels.  I usually use at least level 7

CONS:
-It is quieter but still not “quiet”, especially on the higher levels.  Not sure that you’re going to get a quiet/silent pump with a high-quality motor though
-You still have flanges sticking out a few inches past your nipple, so while you can move around and do things you still have to be careful not to bump the flanges
-I am not sure if you can do single side pumping… maybe there is a way and I haven't figured it out!
-cost is high, but you’re getting a very good pump and pump accessories… so if you pump a lot, want to be able to go places and pump… then it’s probably worth it!
-mine only came with size 21 mm and 24 mm flanges, and I use 27 mm.

Overall this pump helped me to persevere through another couple months of exclusive pumping, and I am getting closer to my 1 year goal!
Date: Reviewed in the United States on February 6, 2020

Product Title: Medela Freestyle Flex Breast Pump, Closed System Quiet Handheld Portable Double Electric Breastpump, Mobile Connected Smart Pump with Touch Screen LED Display and USB Rechargeable Battery
Author: Amazon Customer
Review Text: This is a decent pump, a bit expensive for what it is. I’m an exclusive pumper and been renting a Medela Symphony from the hospital and periodically I use a Spectra S1 as well. The pump is pretty intuitive to use and I didn’t need to consult the manual. I like that it counts the time, unlike the Symphony. I use the Symphony at suction level 5 and I also felt most comfortable using the Flex at level 5. I usually get about 6oz per 20 min session (2-3 hours apart) with the Symphony but only got 4oz with the Flex on the same settings. The Symphony is very smooth during pumping with very little vibration, the Flex is similar to the Spectra in terms of vibration while pumping. I was able to use the personal fit flanges from the Symphony with the Flex. I found the parts from the Flex to be much easier to clean than the Symphony (one brush vs 2). The Flex is slightly louder than the Symphony but not bad at all. All of the accessories that came with the Flex were really well thought out: 2 sets of collection bottles, bag, cooler with ice pack, usb charger, and personal fit flanges. The flanges that came with were 21 and 24mm, I need 27mm, so that was a little disappointing. The lanyard is also weird, it’s for your wrist apparently but that kind of defeats the purpose of a portable pump. So you may need a neck lanyard, it also fits in the back pocket of jeans alright. Overall I would recommend this pump, especially if you have been using another Medela. I wouldn’t recommend it as your main pump if you exclusively pump, but it is good for light jobs in between using your main pump and if you just need to release pressure while out and about. I’m not sure I’d recommend it to use while you’re at work, I think the Spectra would be better for that.
Date: Reviewed in the United States on August 2, 2020

Product Title: Medela Freestyle Flex Breast Pump, Closed System Quiet Handheld Portable Double Electric Breastpump, Mobile Connected Smart Pump with Touch Screen LED Display and USB Rechargeable Battery
Author: L Guerr
Review Text:
I previously had the Medela pump in style backpack and the freemie Liberty from my first kid.  My freemie Liberty broke and I was about to go back to work and hadn’t quite weaned enough to go without pumping.  I was on the fence about buying another mobile pump, but I simply can’t be chained to a wall, even while at home.  After a few days of use, I’m satisfied with the Medela freestyle flex and glad I purchased it, even if it’s not perfect.

The suction power for me is plenty strong, even at just level 5, so that was not an issue for me as it was for some reviewers.  The cons for me are: (1) the buttons are super sensitive so it’s easy to accidentally hit them walking around or if you try to put it in your pocket, (2) I wish it had a belt clip or neck lanyard instead of just a wrist lanyard and (3) the new pump parts obscure the nipple (as opposed to my old pump in style parts that are clear at the nipple) so I can’t totally see if my nipple is still making milk.

As some users pointed out, this pump is not an “in cup” or in bra option, meaning you still have to look like a fembot or a dairy cow while using, but it seems to me the in cup options are pretty expensive with mediocre reviews, and my old freemie Liberty that broke (that was one of the cheaper in cup options out there) wasn’t as strong suction-wise or as durable/high quality as medela, so I’m happy to make that compromise back to an external option now, as long as I can still move around.

In any case, I think this is a very solid option in the portable pump department.  I think the quality is very high, as with most things Medela, and I’m glad I purchased it because I think it will encourage me to keep pumping 20 or so oz a day even after I go back to work since it’s easy to clean and use.
Date: Reviewed in the United States on July 22, 2021

Product Title: Medela Freestyle Flex Breast Pump, Closed System Quiet Handheld Portable Double Electric Breastpump, Mobile Connected Smart Pump with Touch Screen LED Display and USB Rechargeable Battery

Product Title: Medela Freestyle Flex Breast Pump, Closed System Quiet Handheld Portable Double Electric Breastpump, Mobile Connected Smart Pump with Touch Screen LED Display and USB Rechargeable Battery
Review Title: Good but not great for exclusive pumping moms
Author: NC
Review Text:
I liked this pump initially. I ordered it to replace my 6 year old Freestyle from my first pregnancy. I had to start exclusively pumping after a week of baby’s birth.

Regarding suction:
After about 10 weeks of EP, 7 x a day, I noticed the suction was weakening so I naturally increased the suction from L4 to L5. I didn’t think anything of it until a couple days later when my supply dropped by 2 oz. thought it was stress or something else. Then one morning, one connector felt like it was on permanent expression mode while the other was fully suctioning. I played around with the tube, switched parts and was able to identify that one of membranes (yellow rubber that goes into connector) was faulting but couldn’t find if there was a tear. One side pumped 1oz while the other pumped almost 3oz. I typically pump 2.5oz on each breast so this was when I realized there was an issue with the connector. I looked for spare parts for just the membrane but as another reviewer mentioned, you have to buy a brand new connector set which is inconvenient.

Thankfully for Medela customer service, they are providing me a brand new connector as a “courtesy.” I’m hoping there are no more issues for a pump that is pretty spendy and less than 3 months of use.

Flanges:
The flanges that come with it were useless for me as well. I needed a bigger size and the new design hurt so I used the older ones which defeats the purpose of being portable. My baby would often kick it and it would feel like my nipples were being dragged bc they are so long. Wish the new design didn’t feel so uncomfortable bc the length of them are perfect.

Not sure why Medela provides defaults to 21mm and 24mm. We should be able to choose so we don’t waste money and they aren’t producing product that isn’t being consumed and likely get tossed.

Based on my experience I wouldn’t recommend for new moms who have low milk supply. I am pumping on average 30+oz a day so baby has plenty while I wait for new connectors to get delivered and am experienced with hand expressing.
Date: Reviewed in the United States on December 8, 2020

Product Title: Medela Freestyle Flex Breast Pump, Closed System Quiet Handheld Portable Double Electric Breastpump, Mobile Connected Smart Pump with Touch Screen LED Display and USB Rechargeable Battery

Product Title: Medela Freestyle Flex Breast Pump, Closed System Quiet Handheld Portable Double Electric Breastpump, Mobile Connected Smart Pump with Touch Screen LED Display and USB Rechargeable Battery
Review Title: Worst product I have ever purchased
Author: Jamie Boutilier
Review Text:
Hello,

I am absolutely in shock and in tears. My Freestyle Flex breast pump stopped working after 5 days of use.

I am a brand new mom. Breastfeeding has been the most frustrating and difficult thing I have ever done in my life. My son lost significant weight after he was born and dropped to the 2nd percentile weight. We struggled so hard for so long to come up with a plan to feed him and keep him healthy. Finally, the past 5 days gave me hope when I started pumping last Thursday, because he is not able to transfer all of the milk that is in my breasts. For those 5 days, I have been working around the clock to increase my milk supply.

Yet, all of the sudden, my brand new pump stopped working overnight. As of this morning, the suction is sometimes incredibly powerful and painful. Turning down the suction level does not actually reduce the suction. I have tried to pump several times, and other times when I start, there is no suction at all. The motor runs, but the pump does not actually pump no matter how high I increase the suction level. My breasts are in so much pain from engorgement due to the pump not working and the pump malfunctioning This will have a serious impact on my son's health after working so hard to increase my milk supply and get him fed. Everything was working fine until last night.

Review Text:

 The 24 mm flanges are too short. My nipples go through all the way to the connectors and I can't see how much Im expressing and it feels uncomfortable.

The parts are not that easy to clean. I put them on microwave and when i tried to put the membranes on, they wouldn't fit perfectly, i had to support them with the outer lid.

The machine makes almost the same noise with Avent. The suction length (while at max) was same with Avent.

I got avent for 150 eu, and medela for 324 usd which was the worst investment.

If i used medela for longer I am sure I would have lost my ability to breastfeed my baby.

P.S. all negative comments I read where straight to the point, the yield of the milk, because this is what matters the most. The positive comments were focusing more on the noise and convenience of transporting.

I wish Medela pump worked for me.
Do better, MEDELA!

If I had to mention a downside, it’s that it isn’t the quietest pump. Personally, that never bothered me, but it might be something to consider if noise level is important to you.

Cons:

Author: Danielle Cloutier
Review Text:
I honestly didn’t expect to love the Medela Freestyle as much as I do. I had heard so many stories about hands-free options causing supply dips due to incomplete emptying, so I was wary of straying from my Spectra pump. But I've been VERY pleasantly surprised!

In terms of output, I’m seeing comparable results to my standard plug-in pump with only about 4 extra minutes of pumping time per session. For the ability to move around and not be tethered to a wall, that’s more than worth it. That’s a small tradeoff for the freedom to move around and actually do things while I pump.s

Compared to other hands-free pumps I’ve tried (like the Willow), this one is much more user-friendly. The setup is intuitive, the controls are simple, and the whole experience feels streamlined and user friendly. With a newborn, I just don't have time to troubleshoot complicated gadgets while juggling everything.

Small critique: the touchscreen is a bit too sensitive, so if you slip the pump into a pocket or bump it the wrong way, it can accidentally pause. It’s not a dealbreaker at all, but something to be mindful of. Other than that tiny note, I have zero complaints. This pump has made my daily routine so much more manageable.

If you’re on the fence about hands-free pumps or worried about supply issues, this one is 100% worth trying.  It’s a great balance of convenience and performance — and it’s now my go-to for daytime pumping sessions.

Product Title: Medela Freestyle Hands-Free Breast Pump | Wearable, Portable and Discreet Double Electric Breast Pump with App Connectivity
Author: Katelyn Jones
Review Text:
Product arrived today and I have been so excited about trying this pump! I use a Spectra normally. While I can carry the Spectra around, it doesn’t exactly make moving around comfortable and the pump is bulky. This pump has good previous reviews and looked like it would meet my desire for being able to do other things whilst pumping.

Pump was packaged nicely in box. Included charger for pump which is great! Instructions are very clear and set up is very easy. It comes with a 24mm and 21 mm cup. I just so happen to fit the 21 mm so I didn’t need to do anything with that. The pump part comes charged, but instructions say to charge before first use.
The pump itself is very simple and easy to figure out. The display is clear and the design is sleek. I would say it’s about the size of a thick TV remote, so maybe not necessarily easy to store in a pocket, but it does have a short lanyard attached for carrying on the wrist. I personally bought a separate lanyard so that I am able yo wear the device around my neck. Hands free with a pump on my wrist defeats the purpose to me.
I immediately Connected the pump to the Medela Family App, which is super great. App has lots of articles to read about various feeding topics. It also allows you to keep track of pumping time and has a virtual storage part that allows you to keep track of milk that way. App is user friendly and definitely a nice addition to the pump. I am looking forward to storing my sessions because I am the worst at keeping track of my daily output. Unfortunately I’m a just enougher so it’s nice to keep track of what I’m making so I can trend it.
Washing: super easy! Only three parts: the cup itself, membrane and flange.
My first pump: cups are nicely shaped. Fit perfectly inside my nursing bra and have a natural shape to them. I do look like I have large breasts, but honestly with a looser fitting top, pumping in public would be no big deal. The cups are better shape and size than some that I’ve seen. Very comfortable and easy to see nipple alignment/let down through the clear side. I also love that there is an audible click when the cup in in place. Makes worrying about leaks a thing of the past (a common issue with many wearable pumps).  I do worry about this breaking down over time, but the cups look and feel well made.
The tubing can be configured two ways:inward and outward. Easy to string down inside of shirt for even more discreet pumping length is adequate and seems sturdy.
I figured the best way to break this pump in is to do laundry!  I was able to easily do this task without worrying about spillage or the cups moving due to being too heavy. Very light and I honestly hardly noticed them! I will say, however, the touch screen on the pump is SO sensitive. I did accidentally change settings several times while folding clothes and it was kind of annoying. I wish there was a way to lock the screen so that this doesn’t happen. The suction is pretty strong. While the strength is 245 (I think) it feels stronger than my spectra and is easy to toggle down. It automatically starts in let down mode as well which I love as my other pump starts in expression mode and can be a real shocker if I forget.
The pump is not loud being worn, but when set on a hard surface it vibrates around quite a bit. But since I don’t plan to be sitting while using this pump, it’s not really a concern for me personally.
Output: I have tried other wearable options and not gotten great output. I pumped maybe half an ounce less than my usual output, not a big deal and could be that time is needed for adjusting to the different type of pump.
Overall, I would recommend this pump for ease of use and quality. I am excited to have this option for more freedom of movement as the worst part of pumping is feeling chained to the couch all the time.
Date: Reviewed in the United States on July 30, 2023

Product Title: Medela Freestyle Hands-Free Breast Pump | Wearable, Portable and Discreet Double Electric Breast Pump with App Connectivity
Author: Amazon Customer
Review Text:
I bought this pump for going back to work with my second child. With my first child, I exclusively pumped for 12 months using the Medela Max Flow and Swing Maxi pumps, and after that experience I decided to go with a hands-free pump with my second (who exclusively breast feeds except for while I'm at work a couple of days per week). I had a great experience with my Medela pumps for my first daughter, so after reading reviews of all of the popular hands free options, I ultimately decided to go with Medela for two reasons: my comfort level with the brand, and the simplicity of the collection cups being only three pieces.

I started using the pump at the end of February, and I use it two to three times during the day while I'm working, twice per week (so about 5-6 uses per week). It has been perfect for me. The suction is great and honestly I haven't notice much of a difference between my hands free pump compared to my Swing Maxi pump. It's super easy to take apart and clean while at work, and although the actual pump isn't super small, it does fit well enough in a large jacket pocket. The only complaint that I have so far is that the pump has a very sensitive touch screen, so sometimes while it's in my pocket, occasionally buttons accidentally get pressed and the settings will change or it will turn off.

Here's where this pump really sets itself apart from others. One of the breast shields started to crack (after only about 2 months of use) but was still functional. I called Medela's customer support and spoke with a woman who was very helpful. Not only did she replace the cracked breast shield with no questions asked, she also shipped me replacement O rings and membranes as a courtesy. She also offered to send everything "next day air" to get the new breast shield to me asap. 5/5 stars for customer service!

Product Title: Medela Freestyle Hands-Free Breast Pump | Wearable, Portable and Discreet Double Electric Breast Pump with App Connectivity
Review Title: Great pump w/ some major flaws
Author: alibythesea
Review Text:
The pump works well for a hands-free option, which is why I’m giving it 3 stars. I still use my hospital-grade pump twice a day because it produces more milk, but this is a good supplemental option. That said, there are some serious design flaws that need addressing:
 1. The cups were incredibly difficult to open at first. Postpartum moms are already overwhelmed—why not include clearer instructions or a video tutorial to make it easier?
 2. The touchscreen is overly sensitive and changes settings at the slightest touch—from clothes, counters, or even my hand. This is frustrating and limits my movement while pumping because I’m constantly afraid of accidentally messing up the settings.
 3. Why are there only two flange sizes? Many moms need a better fit to get proper suction. I had to purchase flange inserts separately just to get it to work effectively.
 4. On top of all this, there’s no option to return the pump through Amazon if you decide you’re not going to pump shortly after purchasing—even if the box is unopened. This is a major issue, as pumping is not for everyone, and new moms should have the flexibility to return such an expensive item if it doesn’t work out for them.

Medela, please test your products with real moms and use their feedback to improve. These issues are avoidable, and postpartum moms deserve better!

Product Title: Medela Freestyle Hands-Free Breast Pump | Wearable, Portable and Discreet Double Electric Breast Pump with App Connectivity
Author: Frances Rios
Review Text:
This is a long review, but if anything READ THIS: When I read the manual one thing caught my attention, that I think is important to note, especially if you are an EP and/or are planning on pumping for an extended period; “The operating life of the breast pump is 250 hours.” That means that at 15 min a pump, 8 pumps a day, this will last you a little over 4 months. Medela has a 1-year warranty but will it cover it if it states the operating life is 250 hours? My guess is no. For the cost of the pump to only be good for 4 maybe 5 months I don’t find it worth it, but of course it’s not advertised.
I wish I could get my money back.

I really wanted to love this pump. I was so excited when it went on sale for prime day and I got it. I paid $279 (from $349).

I’m a first time mom, & the pump that I got through my insurance did not work for me at all (motif duo). My son was in NICU for 11 days so I was able to use the Medela Symphony during that time. The lactation specialist recommended that I look for a Medela pump, so I got the Medela Advanced pump, and it worked very well, but it was not hands free so i was stuck to the spot for 20 min every 3 hours (I over produce so my Dr. recommend that I pump a little extra so I don’t have to pump every 2 hours).

Back to the freestyle; the suction is not the same, so my expression is way less (even at a high level) I only get about half of what I usually get & it leaves me feeling still full & wanting to pump sooner. The pump has a vibration feel that lingers around for sometime after every pump. The pump/monitor is hard to carry around, there’s a wristband but you’ll hit everything as you move your hands around, and yes, it can easily fit in your pocket, but it is very sensitive to touch, so you’ll accidentally press the buttons all the time. I tried putting it in between my boobs, but the vibration feeling was even stronger. It’s almost like you’ve got to sit and place if face up when pumping so it doesn’t touch anything, which completely defies the purpose. If you pump longer than 15 minutes the pump/monitor freezes, the buttons don’t work and it won’t stop when you press the play/pause, you’ll have to power it off from the power button and then when I power it back on it gives me an error (E2) which I’ve looked for in the manual and did not find anywhere. I also asked the chat on the app and it did not give me an answer. It kinda freaks me out a little when it happens because I’m afraid it’s just going to keep pumping and I won’t be able to turn it off & will have to pull my nipples free.
The Medela app (iPhone) has good potential, very good informational articles/videos on baby development, breastfeeding, pumping, etc. but the stats from connecting to the pump, are glitchy, it won’t let me input my own pump session & it freezes often.
I also do like that it will automatically change to expression mode after two minutes. & I also like that it’s only 3 parts to clean per pump & no tiny parts.

I did extensive research on a hands free pump because of how pricey they are, other brands such as Momcozy, Willow Go, & Elvie are ranked higher, but I love my Medela pump so much that I wanted to give Medela Hands Free a shot.

Again, I wish I could get my money back.

Product Title: Medela Harmony Manual Breast Pump - Compact Swiss Design Featuring PersonalFit Flex Shields and Medela 2-Phase Expression Technology
Review Title: Affordable, effective and faster than electric pumps
Author: Alexa Coote
Review Text:
For my first baby I used an electric breast pump, one of the leading market products of the time. I since donated it to a friend and was looking for a replacement this second postpartum period, after my newborn's feeding pattern began to change.

I wish I'd purchased this first time around. Seriously, don't look any further if you're after something to help you express between feeds (especially the sleepy, less than full night feeds) and maintain a good supply.

But also make sure, via Medela's website, you measure your nipple size and get the right nipple shield to fit this.
This product comes with the M (medium) size and it just may not fit you. Wrong size makes expressing slower or unable to pump at all. So order this and don't be afraid to size up (I got size L shields separately) to give your nips adequate room for suction.

I used to hate sitting up in bed at night, or on the toilet next to the power outlet, listening to the beeping of my previous electronic pump. I also got way less milk out of the 40+ min spans I'd give myself to express. But this pump is quick, lightweight, easy to manoeuvre and compact without stupid wires and tethers. It can fit in a small handbag.

All the parts are lightweight plastic, very easy to clean and sterilise. I've even been able to hold my newborn securely with one arm and pump from the other (yes, cos I'm counting on getting as many minutes of sleep as I can get!!) This is possible thanks to the fully rotatable pump handle and that it's manual; I don't have to try to time my grip or stimulate the let down according to some motor or program.

I recommend operating two-handed though. You can get excellent results from massaging or hand expressing with your dominant hand, while using the other hand to hold onto the neck of the pump/nipple shield. That way you speed up expression and drain the breast evenly.

The pump is so quiet and the clear parts make it easy to see if anything is coming out. If there isn't a proper seal to create suction, you'll know that it'll be because the siphon/flap inside is clogged ((can happen from longer pump intervals). Or because a part you've just washed is not securely fitted.

No bulls*** electronic beeps orcryptic error messages to deal with.

PS: seek out Cherub Baby reusable milk bags with the Medela pump adaptor. You'll actually enjoy pumping even more. I bought them and successfully fitted the pump to bag adaptor onto this product, so milk can be quickly measured and stashed in the fridge. I've also done an amazon review of those bags and adaptor.

Review Text:

To save time, energy, even money, this is what works to produce more milk:
- use this manual pump. Or any other, but this one I tried and works very well; that's why I said "even save money" because a manual pump is actually enough. If you find it's weak, that's only because the handle isn't assembled properly, I've done this mistake myself. The pump is super convenient, very easy to use, to wash and does a very quick and efficient job, can use it anywhere, anytime as a long as you have some privacy! Honestly, I get more milk and faster with this pump than an electric one! No need for bra to keep it on the breast or charging, etc.
- while using the pump, here comes actually the most IMPORTANT PART, the one that is vital to produce more milk but noone actually tells you about it! No midwife, no professionals or online articles. Everybody says pump, pump and pump as often as possible for like 15-20 min, BUT that's just not it!!! What you need to do is express the milk with your own hands, also called COMPRESSING the breast. This is the second best way, after baby sucking, to get the milk out of the breasts! No pump, no matter what kind, has the same efficiency as your hands to express the milk! And if you don't empty the breasts as much as possible, they won't produce much milk. So manual pumping with one hand + compressing the breast same time with the other hand, it will give you the best results!
- in parallel with the above, hydration, healthy food, supplements, teas, etc will do the very best.
The results are almost immediate because a breast that gets emptied as much as possible will try cope with the demand and produce more milk.

Review Title: Good choice for a primary pump
Author: Dan Dewald
Review Text:
This pump is being compared to the Spectra S1, as this is the pump we already owned as our primary.

Some things that are great about this pump:
1. It starts in stimulation mode, and automatically moves to expression mode for you! This is an improvement over the Spectra.
2. It starts in low suction mode, unlike most pumps that just start at whatever suction you had it set at. This is great for people who like to gradually ramp up the suction as the pumping session goes on.
3. No duckbill valves!!! Duckbill valves are a huge pain; they fail quickly and are expensive to replace. This pump has a membrane that also functions as the backflow valve. Very good design.
4. It is small but mighty. It is SO easy to pack this pump since it is so compact.
5. Output is great and it’s easy to use.

Some things that could be better:
1. There is no timer or display on the pump. This isn’t a huge deal since most pumpers use an app to track.
2. The collection cups are not easy to read when you are tracking your output. You’ll need to pour them into another cup with easier to read measurements. (Photo shows the Medela on the left, harder to read output)
3. Wish it had an onboard battery. They perfected a small but powerful pump, but you still need to stay plugged in. Looking online it seems like you CAN get a battery pack for this pump for an additional cost.

Overall, this Medela Pump in Style Pro is a solid choice for a primary pump. The parts are easily customizable (you can use almost any flange shield you like), easy to wash, and the replacement parts are reasonably priced. Definitely prefer this pump over the Spectra and it has become the new primary pump in our household.

- comfort: just fine. I used flange inserts with the cups without issue. No pump/cup is really that comfy but at least this isn’t painful.

Cons:
- pricey. Hard to justify $90 for these few pieces of plastic and silicone. You are paying for convenience.
- As other reviews mentioned, it is hard to take apart. When I was deciding to purchase it, I read about this but disregarded it. It does make a difference though since you have to disassemble it daily to wash it. It requires prying the cups apart with your nail and it’s easy to accidentally catch the skin under the nail.
- output decrease. I am able to pump about 75% my normal output, but I can get closer to my normal amount if I pump for longer (40 rather than 25 minutes). This is unique to each person, but for a just-enougher like myself, it meant I couldn’t use this as often as I wanted.

Overall, if you are looking for convenience—anything to decrease the misery of pumping— this is a great product. Minimal parts to wash, doesn’t require special bra, decent output if worn for longer. I use it at work and when I’m running errands and stick with my normal spectra parts otherwise to keep supply up. It’s a decent product if you know about the cons ahead of time.

$90 is a steep price to pay but I don’t think there are more convenient cups available. I think if Medela lowered the price it would be way more popular.

Review Text:
I exclusively breastfeed my baby, but I'm an over-supplier so I need to pump at least 1 or 2 times a day on top of nursing. • Seem to be compatible with any pump.
• Holds a good volume, I had 6oz in one cup and not even close to overflowing.
• Only 3 pieces to clean.
• Can use with a regular stretchy/roomy bra, you don't need a special hand free pumping bra.
• From a reputable and consistent brand, so replacement parts should be easy to purchase (as long as they don't get discontinued)
• Easy to pour milk from

• They aren't small -- you will have Dolly Parton boobs while wearing. Not a collection cup you could wear with nobody noticing.

Product Title: New 2nd Gen Medela Pump in Style Pro Breast Pump, Clinically Proven Hospital-Efficiency, Compact Portable Double Electric Pump with Bottles and PersonalFit Plus Breast Shields
Author: Ally Christmas
Review Text:
Alright, I’ve spent countless hours reading reviews about hands-free pumps trying to find the *absolute best option*… I don’t think this is it, but it’s definitely helped me a lot on my pumping journey.

Pros:
- obviously, hands-free, but only if you can conveniently put the pump itself in a pocket or something - it’s a bit big so has to go in a back pocket of pants or a large sweater/hoodie pocket etc.
- very easy to clean, easier than my Spectra and Maymom parts; it’s only 3 pieces!
- lightweight, easy to travel with (stuff in a tote or large purse)
- can be completely hidden under shirt, though the tubing does have to stick out
- suction level seems good, I’ve never had to go above level 5
- I haven’t had any leaking issues except for when I didn’t have it assembled correctly (but also I can’t fully bend over or do any rigorous activity)

Cons:
- way overpriced, it’s ridiculous that I have to spend like $90 if I want more than one pair of cups
- also if you need any replacement parts they’re not super cheap, especially if you buy them from the Medela website directly (better if you can find them on here because the shipping will be way cheaper, but some parts I’ve struggled to find on Amazon)
- even though it comes with two sets of shields (21mm and 24mm), it only comes with ONE set of cup parts and ONE set of o-rings, so you have to wash stuff after every pump regardless (make sure you have the o-rings properly installed!!! they will leak if you don’t!!)
- only available in two sizes so if you’re not a size 21 or 24mm nipple, you have to buy separate flange inserts (not sold by Medela)
- pump is a bit loud, like I’ve been pumping near other people before and they ask “what’s that noise??”, but I doubt it’s the loudest pump out there
- not intuitive to figure out how to open or assemble when first using it (I recommend finding a how-to video first, which I didn’t think I needed to do but in hindsight 🤷‍♀️)
- kinda hard to open; I have to use a towel to pry it open because it hurts my thumb otherwise
- does not have clear amount markers on the side so you have to measure it out after you pump (I use a breast milk storage bag on a small digital scale)
- there’s been a few times where they just could not get good suction; I think if they’re even remotely wet from the last washing, that causes issues with suction
- the pump has a touch screen and it’s a bit sensitive, so the buttons might accidentally get activated in your pocket or while you’re holding it (ouch! went from suction level 3 up to 9 in my pocket and I had no idea what was happening at first)
- also the touch screen has randomly frozen on me at least twice that I can remember, had to force it off and start the pump session over
- pretty difficult to hold my baby while wearing these but I can lift him from the floor to his bassinet or simple movements like that (can carefully clean kitchen or fold laundry, I’ve also used them while driving without issue - obviously put them on and take them off while you’re safely stopped!)

I know it seems like a lot of cons, but again, these have made a huge difference in my pumping journey considering that my other pump is the big Spectra S2 which is nowhere near as portable and is definitely not conveniently hands-free. With this pump, I’m able to sit on the floor and be with baby while pumping, I can do basic chores or use it in the car, and I can use it around other people without my boobs or nipples fully hanging out.

The pictures I attached here show me from the side with and without the cups in - they are pretty big so it’s not something I *like* to use out in public but I have done it in a pinch several times. I hope this review is helpful to anyone trying to decide what pump to buy!
