Product Title: Medela Sonata Smart Breast Pump, Hospital Performance Double Electric Breastpump, Rechargeable, Flex Breast Shields, Touch Screen Display, Connects to Medela Family App, 101037319
Author: FiG
Review Text:
Seriously, the BEST thing I’ve ever bought. I’ve had my Sonata for almost 5 and a half years! Unfortunately, after 2 babies and 3 and a half years breastfeeding and pumping between them, she no longer holds a charge. On the third baby now and putting a new one on my registry as a “must have”. What I love about this machine is mainly the options you have to be able to create what your body needs. For new moms, this means every baby is different and they don’t all feed the same and our bodies adjust to the baby’s feedings so free selection of how long a stimulation you need or strength or pulse = more milk. I love that I can take apart the entire top piece and replace piece by piece. Clean each piece independently and when taking it apart after pumping allows me to get EVERY LAST DROP of milk. I like I can change out the flanges and clean those individually, it makes it easier to apply into a feeding bra, while others I’ve tried, I had to hold and not move my hands because the flanges didn’t come off from the head so it wouldn’t fit through the hand freeing bra.
I could pump one side while feeding my babies on the other without hassle.
Noise is quiet. Never bothered the babies while sleeping.
The head piece is easy to clean, easy to reach every space touched by milk, and easy to take apart and assemble. It has 4 pieces to each head.
We are a Kiinde bottle family and the adapter adapts AMAZINGLY to the head of the Sonata. Never had a leakage or air problem. So milk goes from breast to pump to milk bag and no extra clean up or transportation other than the head itself for those last few precious drops :)

The only thing I’d say is that the machine itself is bulky and a little heavy, never something I enjoyed taking while traveling. Fit in a suitcase just fine in between clothes, but not great to take to work as it isn’t discreet.. for me anyways. It was the nursing bag, my purse and a lunchbox. But definitely smaller and more compact than MANY other popular choices out there.. all pieces (except the machine) fit in a small make up bag, milk bags and all. The nursing bag only had the machine, a make up bag and wipes. It was pretty great. Compared to other handheld, on the go ones I’ve tried where the machine was small but the heads didn’t collapse so it took up more space than the machine itself.. the machine can definitely be used on the go if needed. Doesn’t need to be connected to a wall and even when not plugged in, it holds a charge and strength.

All in all, if I didn’t explain how much I love this machine in this review, than I’m sorry but this machine is definitely worth the money. Costs as much as a stroller but it lasts just as long as one also. :)

Product Title: Medela Sonata Smart Breast Pump, Hospital Performance Double Electric Breastpump, Rechargeable, Flex Breast Shields, Touch Screen Display, Connects to Medela Family App, 101037319
Author: Kindle Customer
Review Text:
I have a love/hate relationship with this pump. I am an exclusive pumper due to my baby having tongue ties and not latching well to my elastic nipples. I pump 5 times a day for 30 to 60 minutes to produce enough milk. I have two sonatas- one for home and one for work. Both pumps are different year models which I bought second-hand because I couldn't afford them new. They both act the same way and have the same quirks so I know it's not a fluke when the pumps act up.

First the good:
-I am producing the most milk I ever have with rhythm #2 on this. I am making enough now to feed my baby. Even with renting a symphony, I was not able to do that.
 -There is no vibration on this pump, which I prefer and respond better to.
 -The suction is not painful. I have slightly elastic nipples and I can use a higher suction on this because of the rhythm.
-The parts are easy to clean and last a long time.

The bad:
 - The battery does not last long enough unless plugged in to go an entire day pumping. It barely lasts 15 off of the plug before I feel a difference in suction.
 - The pump sometimes randomly loses suction in the middle of a session even when plugged in- 15 to 20 minutes in. This happens more often if I try to enter the letdown/massage mode again to get a second or third letdown. To fix this have to turn off the pump and reset it by holding the power button. It doesn't always work the first time. This is time-wasting and annoying. My pump sessions are already long enough without having to troubleshoot.
-The pump is not extremely portable- sure, it's better than dragging a symphony around or even a spectra, but the "handle" is slippery and I'm always worried about dropping it.
 - The pump is NOT as quiet as they claim it to be. I feel like three other pumps I've tried are quieter than the sonata, including the symphony. I've toyed with the idea of pumping in my cubicle instead of going to the lactation room, but the pump sound would definitely be disruptive to my neighbors.
 -The pump parts are heavy and require a SUPER supportive bra. I know the parts are part of what makes this whole thing work, but again it's annoying to have so much weight on the front. I use a heavy silicone flange which also adds to it. This makes it difficult to multi-task. Even changing my baby's diaper is quite the task when I'm worried that flanges might shift or fall out of my pumping bra.
-Parts are expensive and not compatible with any other pump parts (thankfully you can use silicone flanges)- yes they do seem to last longer than parts on other pumps, but they still need to be replaced often enough that it's a nuisance- especially if you are exclusively pumping and want multiple sets to cut down on washing.

Overall- I will use the sonata because it is more effective than any other pump I've tried, but I would like a pump that has more reliable suction, better battery life, and is more portable.
Date: Reviewed in the United States on January 11, 2023

Review Title: Glitchy from day one, but still the best pump.
Author: Julie Kim
Review Text:
First of all, this thing has glitches. They might even start from the first time you use it. Why am I still giving it 5 stars? So far, glitches are all they are, and they're manageable.

The comfort of the breast shields on this pump is by far the best I've experienced, and the suction is on par with a hospital pump, even when it's not plugged in and running portable. I have a large chest, so the rims of pump shields will invariably cut into my breast tissue; these have a soft rim, so it's more comfy than others. The kit also comes with two sizes of flanges, the second being a smaller size instead of a bigger one (like a Spectra comes with), so that's a plus for me, since I need the smaller flange.

The extras are nice, like the little bottle holder and the freezer pack - I've definitely used these. The pump is overall quite portable and I can generally pump at least twice without charging it, which I don't usually do, because of the glitches. Which I'll go into now.

The glitches seem to be related to the power cord or the connection with the cord. You need to really watch when it's plugged in and make sure it's making a connection - you should see the little lightning bolt to indicate it's plugged in, and it should stay steadily lit. If it's not, you need to unplug it and replug it, mess with the cord position, whatever works.

You will definitely see the thing come on with CALL on the display, indicating it's broken and you need to call customer service. If it's plugged in when that happens, unplug it, then turn it off. When you turn it back on, it should be fine again. If not, turn off again and back on again until it clears. It happens to me multiple times a day, from day one, but so far it hasn't been actually broken and I haven't had to really call. It definitely freaked me out the first time it happened, though.

As long as the glitches stay mere annoyances, I'm very satisfied with this pump. It's as comfortable as pumping can get, portable, powerful even without being plugged in, and as effective as a Symphony. It takes a little patience sometimes, but it's overall very worth the price to me. (I paid for it, since I got a Spectra with my insurance, and this one wasn't offered.)

Product Title: Medela Sonata Smart Breast Pump, Hospital Performance Double Electric Breastpump, Rechargeable, Flex Breast Shields, Touch Screen Display, Connects to Medela Family App, 101037319
Review Title: I had a lot of trouble with poor supply and inability to let down for the pump ...
Author: Erin C.
Review Text:
I'm a working mom who pumped for a year with my last child, and is back to work now with a 6 week old at home. I pump 2-3 times at work, plus 1-2 times at home, in addition to breast feeding at night and on weekends. With my first child, I had a lot of trouble with poor supply and inability to let down for the pump or my baby at first, but with a lot of work, was producing enough to stop supplementing at 6 weeks, and then enough for twins by 3 months. This time my supply has been abundant. I use my pumps on high settings as that shortens my pumping time, and my nipples are able to tolerate it. Pumping does not feel like breast feeding, and once I had accepted that, I stopped looking for a setting that felt good, and instead focused on comfortable enough and efficient. Not everyone is able to tolerate that, so my preferences may not be for everyone. I use a hands free bra, and usually pump 10-12 minutes (past second let down and stop when completely dry).

I've used an Ameda provided by my insurance during first pregnancy (worthless), and older model Medela PIS with all mechanical parts and only single mode rhythm, a Medela Freestyle, a Medela Symphony, and now this Sonata. I also use a Haakaa pump at night as DD only nurses one side each feeding, and I don't want to have to get up and pump after feeding her.

My favorite pump is the older PIS. Without the let down mode, I do get a bit of a jolt the first pull on the nipples, but it is incredibly reliable, has very strong suction, and I get better volumes with that than even the Symphony. However, it is no longer made, a bit awkward to lug around, and has the tendency to suck milk into the tubing which I replace regularly. I got mine used with baby #1, and will keep it until I know that I will never need a pump again.

The Sonata is my second favorite. I can get the same volumes as the PIS, but it took me figuring out that I had to switch the rhythm over to the second rhythm, and takes about 2 minutes longer. I'm currently using power level 7 with it. It is a bit gentler than the PIS in terms of nipple sensation.

Here's what I love:

Portability! I travel for work, and being able to pump in the car or on the plane with a built in battery is huge. Also, just being able to walk around the house with it is amazing. It does require a hand to hold the pump (not like the Freestyle) and is a bit awkward to hold.

It equally the PIS in production. This is huge.

It is quieter than most other pumps (but not anywhere near silent).

The new design for the collectors makes this essentially a closed system. No more milk in the tubes.

Here's what needs improvement:

It has a computer and is single user, but there is no way to program in a setting. This seems a bit ridiculous in 2018. Its not hard to change from the default setting, but why should I have to do that every single time?

They used a different size tubing, so there is no way to chose to use your milk collectors from prior Medela pumps without jerry rigging with 3rd party parts. Since no one makes parts for the Sonata except Medela, and things are not sold separately, it can be very expensive to have back ups or multiple sets, which is essential for anyone who pumps regularly.

There is no way to buy a the accessory set with anything but at 24mm flange. Those of us with normal size nipples who need a bigger one then have to spent more to buy the correct size, and throw out the useless ones with the set.

There are unnecessary beeps. Why add noises when you advertise that the pump is "very quiet."

I am very concerned about the reliability reports in other reviews, and the obvious planned obsolescence given that the manual states the pump is designed to work for 12 months using only 3 times a day. Who pumps only 3 times a day?

UPDATE : The unit suddenly stopped working entirely in the middle of one of my pumping sessions at work when the pump was 2 months old. No warning signs. Customer service was great and got me a new pump via UPS the next day. The new one has required a hard reset once, but has been working for about 3 weeks without failure. I've taken 1 star away for reliability, and just purchased a Spectra S1 to travel with, since i need a reliable pump when I'm not near my back up PIS.
Date: Reviewed in the United States on January 31, 2018

Product Title: Medela Sonata Smart Breast Pump, Hospital Performance Double Electric Breastpump, Rechargeable, Flex Breast Shields, Touch Screen Display, Connects to Medela Family App, 101037319
Author: Abigail G.
Review Text:
I am an exclusive pumper and this is the only pump I have tried, other than the Medela Symphony in the hospital.  The nurses at the hospital suggested I rent a Symphony to establish my milk supply in the first couple weeks, but it was not necessary.  This pump had enough power to establish my supply just fine.  Below are the pros/cons:
PROS:
--Holds a charge for a long time.  I can pump 3 times (30 min ea) before it completely dies.  Also, the charging cord is pretty long, so I can keep it plugged in while pumping all the time at home.
--Very quiet, often my husband doesn't even realize I'm pumping!
--Pleasant.  This may seem silly, but when you're using it so many times a day, the fact that it's a nice color, looks simple and streamlined, and makes happy, nice noises makes a big difference!  It lives on our coffee table most of the day, but does not look like a big ugly machine.
--Lightweight.  For a pump of its size/power, it is lightweight and not heavy at all when carrying it in its bag.

CONS:
--Big.  I'm sure the size is necessary to make it powerful enough to maintain a supply, but it is a real pain to carry around if I try to accomplish anything or need to do anything while pumping.
--SO MANY PIECES.  As someone who has to wash and sterilize the pump parts after every use, this pump is a huge hassle.  There are so many pieces to the heads.  Not only do they take a long time to wash, but it is also really easy to forget pieces when trying to take the pump on the go because there are so many of them.
--Bright/Dim.  The display does not have brightness options.  When it's really dark at night, the numbers can be a bit too bright, but if I'm around a lot of sunlight, I can barely read the display.
--Hard to attach.  The hard flanges have a difficult time attaching sometimes, so it can take a couple minutes for the true pumping to start.

Side note also, the bag is kind of small.  The pump and its parts do fit, but if you try to put anything else in the bag with them, even just a burp cloth, it's a tight fit.  Overall, I'm happy I made the investment as making it possible to maintain a good supply is the most important thing a pump needs to do, and this does it.  But I do hope to purchase a more portable pump with less pieces in future to use instead of this one sometimes for greater ease and convenience.

Review Text: Currently 2 1/2 months into nursing and pumping. Was inclined towards medela due to my great experience with my symphony and this wearable did not disappoint. I’ve only used it for a day now and I already love it, having a wearable has already saved me hours that I’d otherwise be stuck on the couch with my symphony. It feels great to be able to multitask pumping and house chores. I use it for the same amount of time (20-30 mins) and still get my usual 4-5 ounces on each side. I definitely credit my symphony for developing my supply so I don’t know if I’d necessarily recommend this wearable to an exclusively pumping mom or a mom just starting out her breastfeeding journey, but over 2 months in with a strong supply I can confidently recommend this for when supply is established. Didn’t even know medela had an app but I love the Bluetooth feature and being able to track all my pumping sessions by syncing my swing maxi to the app. Also greatly appreciate the simplicity of cleaning with this pump, only three pieces that are straightforward to clean and don’t have a bunch of nooks and crannies to worry about like symphony parts. The only struggle I’ve encountered right away is slight difficulty opening the collection cups but I’m sure over time the pieces won’t be as stiff. Very glad it came with 21mm inserts too, I would’ve ordered them separately if the pump only came with 24mm so nice touch to include a smaller size. Overall great product, strongly recommend to anyone on the fence!!

I’m already past the return date so I have to use it but my son is just one month old and I think I’m going to get another brand because I can’t keep pumping with this product, otherwise I’m going to loose my mind.

Review Text:

Eventually it became so dysfunctional that it would pulse two or three times and then die, even while plugged in. Maybe it was just a malfunction with the one I received, but it made everything that much more frustrating and stressful.

So if you need to fully rely on pumping to get your baby that amazing breast milk, I don't know if I can recommend this as your daily pump. It's good for on the go and supplemental pumps, but you might need something a little more heavy duty for constant use.

Product Title: Medela Swing Maxi Hands-Free Breast Pump | Easy, Intuitive, Ideal for On The Go Double Electric Hands Free Breast Pump
Review Title: Pump works well! No plugged ducts yet!
Author: Amazon Customer
Review Text:
I was given this pump as part of a Friends and Family Program with Medela by a friend of mine who works for the company. In return, I am to provide an honest review of the product.
With my first child I had a different brand of pump and I had plugged ducts ALL THE TIME and mastitis twice. I produce A LOT of extra milk so it was hard to get it all out. So I was excited to try this pump since they stated that you could extract more milk with the pump + the Medela name, I figured it would be a good one to try. I have not had a plugged duct yet and feel like my breasts are draining well.
This pump works FAST! I can pump 14 ounces total in 10 minutes and feel like my breasts are drained completely. It's quiet, which is always a huge plus, it's super portable - the small pump has a loop on it that you can easily put a lancet on and hook it on you and get chores done while you pump.
The only thing worse than cleaning a juicer is cleaning a breast pump 5 billion times a day. But as far as pumps go, this one is easy to clean, no hidden nooks and crannies to get into. So that's nice.
The one draw back is that the tubing did get water in it. I think because the pump wasn't 100% dry when I put it back together and had to use it again. This was a bummer as it says in the literature that the tubing will stay dry. Pump number 2 and the tubing had water in it. So I will have to replace that as to avoid mold in the tubing. Overall, I am super happy with this pump and will continue to use it for the duration of my time breastfeeding my second child, which I plan to do for 2 years.

Product Title: Medela Swing Maxi Hands-Free Breast Pump | Easy, Intuitive, Ideal for On The Go Double Electric Hands Free Breast Pump
Author: Erin
Review Text:
I received the pump from Medela at no charge in order to try it and provide an honest review. Initially I expected a lot from this pump, it's #4 in my pumping journey.

Initially I had issues with it, because it didn't look like it fit together -- but an email to support helped me figure out my issues. The pieces looked like they were supposed to fit flush together, but didn't. After talking to support, I understood that as long as there was suction it would be fine.

As far as this pump goes, it is great for travel. The suction is effective and the bag makes the pump very easy to tote around. The flanges come in 21mm and 24mm which was great to help me figure out what size i needed (all my other pumps had 25mm and 28mm options). I really appreciated the rubber edges to the flanges, too, as they made the pump more comfortable to hold against my breasts. I have used this on road trips and the size and portability have made pumping in the car so easy. It was also quiet.

My biggest complaint is that if you don't have the Medela family app, you cannot check on how the battery level is. If you're at home that isn't an issue, but on the road it can be harder to keep track of. Another point against it is that if you press a button while pumping, to change the suction for example, it restarts the 30-minute countdown to shutoff.

Overall, though, this is a good pump. Very easy to clean and use, even without the app.

Product Title: Medela Swing Maxi Hands-Free Breast Pump | Easy, Intuitive, Ideal for On The Go Double Electric Hands Free Breast Pump
Review Title: Perfect for Mom’s On the Go - Lifestyle Change

Review Text:
I absolutely love the new Maxi Swing portable pump. I have 3 children and have breastfed/pumped with all of them. As a busy mom, I am always on the go, go, go. This pump was life changing.

I am able to plug it in during car rides and pump while I drive since it is hands free. Once I get to my destination, I just pour the milk into a bottle and I am ready to feed the baby.

Around the house, I use a Fanny pack and place the pump in it so that I can do laundry, wash dishes, change diapers and even eat meals while pumping. It’s working out great.

I only wish that Medela provided a Fanny pack for the pump that fit it perfectly. They do provide you with a backpack, but you can’t wear the backpack while pumping.

The backpack is very sleek, lightweight, small and portable. It is very cute and stylish. I love how the side pocket opens and has the cooler. That is a very cool feature. There are also stands that hold the pumped milk so that they don’t fall over and spill.

This would be my favorite backpack/carrying case and pump out of all 3 Medela pumps that I have used over the years!

As far as battery life, it gives about 10 hours I would say before it needs to be charged again. I can charge it at home or in the car.

As for suction, it does a really good job on my right side, but does not do the best job on my left.  In the beginning, I wondered if it was even working on the left side. My right side will get 4-5 oz and the left side 1-2. This can also be normal as the baby nurses mainly on my dominant right side.

Overall, I give this pump a 10/10. I highly recommend for busy moms. Anything to make life a little bit easier. And not having to be tied down to a machine is wonderful.

Author: Amanda Crawford
Review Text:
This pump worked great for me. I ended up buying this one, and not being too sure about it at first. After getting a medela max flow or whatever its called through insurance (which I'm happy it was free otherwise that would've been another expensive test), I went back to the Dr Browns. The flanges that fit me I had to order separately as it only comes with the 24mm, but other than that the suction power and the customization is great and the suction is better than my hand pump and the medela.
The only down side is it feels as if there are a lot of parts to clean, and when you have to pump multiple times a day, it feels tedious.
The suggestions for this pump I can give is purchase a second set of pump parts so you're not constantly hand all the little parts if you can. The other is crank up the suction right until it's uncomfortable, and then go down a notch or two. That's what gave me the maximum amount of drainage power.
Overall, worth the money!

Author: Allison Smith
Review Text:
I have this manual breast pump, and the Madela manual pump. This one works, but as a small breasted woman, I do prefer the Madela. I don't know if my size is actually a factor, but this one isn't as comfortable for me and it doesn't seem to pull as much, with or without different flange inserts (ive tried so many sizes with this one).

The shape of the breast shield part doesnt lay naturally on me and the material is sort of harsh. Its like really thick TPU, which sounds malleable, but it holds its form and sort of creates an uncomfortable pull for me.

The pump lever is also a little uncomfortable to hold and difficult to switch between modes. You have to stop the session all together to switch between the short pumps and long pulls after let down.

Still, 9 months later, this has remained true. It does serve it's purpose and I do still use it, but it isn't my go to just because I have another option. It isn't a bad pump and it does what it's supposed to, but it doesn't really do it as comfortably or effectively as it could.

Product Title: Elvie - Double, Wearable Breast Pump w/App - The Smallest & Quietest - Portable - Hands Free & Discreet - Automated with Four Personalized Settings
Author: Kayla Bartoli
Review Text:
For context, this is my review after 3 months of use with a 3 month old and a 3 year old as a stay at home mom.

I have nothing to compare it to except my Spectra S1, but even that is more portable than these wearables...

Pros:
● Wearable - wireless, tubeless, fits easily into, not only a pumping bra, but even a not-too-tight sports bra
● Output - actually comparable to my Spectra
● Discreet - any time I have pumped in public, no one has had any idea until I took my pumps out of my shirt. They are not overly bulky and they are super quiet.

Cons:
● Leaking - Leaks FAR too easily - I cannot change a diaper or feed or even be barely hunched over or else they will leak, which in my eyes, defeats the purpose of a wearable
● Pump Parts - parts are too fragile - you cannot even put them into a sterlizer or else they will shatter/crack. I dropped one of the sheilds once by accident and it cracked. For a mother of a new baby (and 3 year old), the parts should be far more resilient considering the accidents that could happen.
● Charging - the charging cords it came with were garbage - they have barely worked at all. I would have to move the pumps around and contort the wires in very specific ways every time I charged them just to get the charging light to come on... I almost thought it was the pumps giving me the difficulty until I bought a 2 pack of fast charging wires for $5 on Amazon and they instantly worked; no contorting required. Which is WILD that such expensive pumps didnt come with better cords...
● App - the app does not work well, at least for android. It is supposed to do all kinds of useful things like time your pumps, measure output, records pump times, and maybe more things that I have yet to discover because the app really doesnt work for me... every time I look at the controls to see how long I have been pumping, one of the pumps is always not working/loading, and the other one will allow me to see the timing for a moment and then will randomly stop the timer even though the pumps are still going. The output of milk is also SUPER inaccurate. There are all kinds of functions that the app is supposed to have, but when I press the buttons, nothing happens so it just doesnt work... and I will say. That is not because I am not tech savvy; it is just a garbage app.

To me, the cons far outweigh the pros. I literally only use them at this point because they are easier to put on, as they can go into any bra (even a sports bra that's not too tight) and because they are so expensive. Other than that, I honestly wish I would have bought a different set of wearables and saved my money AND got better functioning pumps.

Product Title: Elvie - Double, Wearable Breast Pump w/App - The Smallest & Quietest - Portable - Hands Free & Discreet - Automated with Four Personalized Settings
Author: Brielle
Review Text:
I bought this pump from the Elvie website during a Black Friday sale. I was so excited to use the pump because it is hands free/wearable, discreet and quiet. I figured this would be worth the $550 (I bought it for $330 still expensive) to help my quality of life while pumping.

You see all these videos of people wearing these style of pumps and still producing a lot. After multiple tries in different modes I can say that in 30 minutes I don’t get even half of what I would get while using my spectra. It’s disappointing but understandable. I’m an exclusive pumper and I need my pumps to fully drain my breasts and work efficiently. This is the biggest down fall with this pump (and type of pump). For the price? It’s just not worth it unless…..
1. You want to be discreet and pump while in the presence of others without anyone being able to see or hear (I mean it is noticeable through the shirt but not physically seen)
2. You want to pump and be mobile or need to do other tasks (remember it’s like a 45 degree tilt maximum before it might leak out)

The battery life seems to be about 120minutes … also inconvenient but understandable since it’s battery powered.

This will heat up and feel really warm on your body while pumping. This can cause some discomfort but also is potentially a good thing since milk seems to flow better when the breasts are warmed.

It’s cool to see it measures output but it’s not as accurate as I wish it was. I find my self correcting the pump totals after each pump.

It’s cool that it has the ability to identify milk flow / let downs and adjust accordingly, however you must choose that mode before your pump session.

It’s really just disappointing to me that despite ease of use and cool features, it’s not efficient and can’t be used as a main source of pumping due to battery life and inefficient breast draining. As well as those cool features not being as accurate as I would expect for a $550 breast pump.

Product Title: Elvie - Double, Wearable Breast Pump w/App - The Smallest & Quietest - Portable - Hands Free & Discreet - Automated with Four Personalized Settings
Author: Callie
Review Text:
To preface this review I would like to add that I have worked with three different lactation consultant with my Elvie pump, so my review is not based off of poor fit, not using it properly, etc,

While the Elvie Double Breast Pump offers some positives, such as being quiet, discreet when worn, and easy to clean, the negatives unfortunately outweigh these benefits.

One of the most frustrating issues is the design of the suction cup. It lacks a rigid edge, causing a significant amount of breastmilk to leak from the bottom. While the flat suction side may add comfort, it’s hard to justify the milk loss. As any breastfeeding mom knows, every drop counts, and this flaw alone can be discouraging.

The app, which is meant to enhance the experience, falls short. There are no varied modes to simulate a baby’s natural feeding pattern—just a basic stimulation and expression mode, with limited intensity levels for expression. On top of that, the app’s tracking feature is unreliable, often displaying an output that is wildly inaccurate, leading to disappointment, especially for moms working to overcome low supply.

Finally, the battery life is a real letdown. It only lasts through about two pumping sessions, and even by the second session, the intensity noticeably weakens if the battery falls below 50%. This means you’re left recharging after nearly every 20-30 minute session, which adds unnecessary stress to an already busy feeding schedule.

Overall, I would not recommend the Elvie Double Breast Pump. Given its high price, these issues should not be so prevalent, and I found it to be more frustrating than helpful.

Review Text:
This product was a HUGE game changer for my family and I cannot recommend it enough. I needed to pump in order to give myself more flexibility and freedom without having to give my son formula if it wasn’t necessary. I pump when I’m driving, blow drying my hair, making dinner. Seriously amazing.

My advice: read the directions thoroughly! Suction is everything and if you don’t fit it super tightly in your bra, you’re not going to get NEARLY as much milk. I had them loosely in my bra and the suction on the flange wasn’t completely sealed all around my breast and I produced a 1/2 oz from both breasts combined… once I kept at it and figured out the suction and which flange would fit my nipple best, I produced 3 oz between both breasts in half the time! While you can def accomplish a lot of chores and things while pumping, don’t do things that cause you to lean over or have to be bounced around a lot because the suction with release and you’ll be pumping very little if nothing out. Next, create a solid routine/system for how you’re going to clean, dry and store your pump and it’s pieces. I have an amazing pump backpack that came with the pump my insurance provided me and I converted it to have everything I need for this pump so it’s incredibly easy to bring with me.

I feel like a human woman again with this pump because you don’t have tubes going everywhere and your nipple exposed. I hating pumping, I was embarrassed and it took SO much time out of my day. Granted, you still need to clean all the parts but you gain back so much time because you can do things!

Another thing I absolutely love is that for me, this pump helps to stimulate my breasts to produce more milk. You can literally wear these for an hour each day and get so much milk and it’s perfect because it increases your production overall which is something I needed because my son wasn’t getting enough milk at the breast and we had to start supplementing with 4oz of formula a day - which none of us enjoyed.

I’ve only been using this a few days (though I’ve used it like 7 times already haha!) so I’ll try to update as time goes on to be sure this product still stays as top notch as I currently think it is.

I hope this helps any lactating mammas out there to know that this is expensive but absolutely worth the time you gain back from it if you can afford it!

Review Text:

Pros:
 1. The obvious is that is cordless/portable. This in itself makes it worth having on hand. For me personally, my baby would not allow me enough time to pump without having to entertain him or pick him up at some point. My corded pump was not realistic for this reason. So the Elvie really allowed me to continue my breastfeeding/pumping journey. I don’t know that I would have been able to pump during the day without it.
 2. Its also very convenient being able to take it on the go. I don’t know how much I would wear it in public because it is not entirely silent and your boobs look comically huge with the pumps on. However, being able to pump in the car or while hanging out with friends and family was always a nice option.

Cons:
 1. It slowed down my production drastically. I felt like the suction power was good so I still can't figure out why this happened but once I started pumping full time with it my production went down and I would need to pump for 30-40 minutes at a time. Milk was coming out very slowly.
 I felt that the effectiveness of the pump got worse over time. For example, after pumping for 30 minutes i will have 2 ounces of milk. I will then hand express another full ounce. That’s 50% of what i pumped being left in the boob and after 30-40 minutes of pumping.
 I LOVED them when i first started. Maybe this is because over time my nipples got more elastic ruining my production. After having them for almost 3 months now i am buying the spectra to replace this. More money :|
 2. The instructions emphasize that ALL parts need to be perfectly dry in order for the pumps to work properly. Well the membranes (green discs) that are a main component in the suction process end up getting moisture/milk on them during my pumping session. It happens every session and I don’t know how to prevent this.
 3. I also feel like it made my nipples elastic. I had never had this issue before but after trying to go back to my regular corded Ameda pump, my nipples would extend so far into the flange which also caused output issues for that pump. This was not the case before using the Elvie and made it to where i can't really use my Ameda pump anymore because the output is so bad due to the elasticity of my nipples.
 4. It damaged my nipples pretty significantly. The chaffing was SO bad that my nipples were always raw and missing layers of skin. The BeauGen cushions worked the best but still did not prevent pain. They are also an extra $25 a pair and only last maybe 2 months.
Small, but annoying thing when paying the price you pay for a product like this, is that the OZ labeling on the containers is incorrect. 1oz in an Elvie container is not actually 1 US oz. So if you are trying to accurately track production (as an under producer already, it matters to me) you have to pour your milk into another, more accurate, container to see how much you actually pumped. Also, this negates the validity of the app "insights" because it will say you've pumped 5oz's when in reality you pumped say 3oz's.

 After my first week and a half back at work, I am very frustrated. When both sides work, it's great and makes life much easier (as a $500 beast pump should). However, both sides working at the same time only occurs about 30% of the time. I usually end up having suction issues with one side or the other (does not seem to be specific to the breast or the pump I use).

I have read the instruction manual and watched several videos to help troubleshoot the issues. If the suction disc is moist at all- it will not work. If the silicone valve lip is tucked under the opening on the pump- it will not work. If my nipple is aligned incorrectly with lines on the breast shield- it will not work (and yes- I made sure I am using the correct size shield). After making sure all of these potential issues are addressed- I will still often have problems getting the pump to work. A lot of the time I have good suction at the start and get the pump secured in my bra (and yes, I've used different types of bras/and tight undershirts to ensure the pump stays in place), only to lose suction 5, 10, 15 minutes into a pumping session. I have to start and stop multiple times during a pumping session to replace the pump and get the suction working again. Many times after all of this, I just give up and use my manual pump and then curse about the time I just wasted trying to get the Elvie to work on top of time it takes to just manual pump anyways.

The one positive I will say is that when the suction does work, it stimulates very well (similar to the way an actual baby would) and I end up having a good amount of expressed milk. I found this aspect of the Elvie to be superior to the Medela pump in style that was covered by my insurance.

I am so disappointed this is not working for me consistently because I have read that a lot of women love this product. I think it would be worth the price for me if it worked the majority of time.  And even more stressful than wasting the money, I still don't have a hands-free pumping option for work. I have a very busy medical practice and don't have the time to be tethered to a wall or manually pump for 20-30 minutes 3 times per day. I have spent the past week and half back at work stressed out and running behind schedule for my patients, which is not acceptable and is not going to work for the next 9 months I plan on pumping at work.

I know I am not the first person to leave this type of review, and I am honestly not sure why this works so well for some women and not others. I wish so much that I was in the group of women it works well for, because the concept and overall design of this product are very impressive.

Disappointed, out $500, and searching for another hands-free portable option.

Product Title: Elvie - Double, Wearable Breast Pump w/App - The Smallest & Quietest - Portable - Hands Free & Discreet - Automated with Four Personalized Settings
Review Title: Excellent pump, terrible app required for more than basic controls
Author: Celecia
Review Text:
This would be a 5 star review if not for the app. The app gives you more control over your pump than the buttons on the pump but most of the time it doesn't work. The Bluetooth connection is shaky at best. You also have to make an account and sign in just to get to the pump controls or update the firmware. The app requires location services permission and the phones location MUST be turned on just to control your pump. I'm not sure why since it's a breast pump, not a GPS trying to get me to my destination. One of the pumps has a slight issue that is mildly annoying when charging and I have wanted to try updating the firmware since purchasing the pumps in April but no luck.

That said, otherwise these are excellent pumps. They're not as strong as other pumps that plug into a wall but the tradeoff is being able to move around the house. I've been using the pumps while I get chores done. There's no feeling of being trapped while wearing them. They are quiet and don't wake anyone up even if I have to sneak in to a room to grab something or put something away while someone is asleep. They are also the only pump that has ever managed to pull a decent amount of milk out of my breasts. I don't know why but my body just does not like pumps. The milk containers are small and have to be emptied more often than other pump bottles but that's to be expected considering how portable they are.

If you move around a lot, it's a good idea to occasionally lean forward and let the milk flow into the collection containers from time to time. It is also a good idea to take a damp paper towel and very slightly moisten your breast or the breast shield to create a better seal before you begin pumping(sometimes I use lanolin for this if I'm going to be moving excessively). That extra step can mean the difference between being able to pump while getting things done or having to stay seated because leaning forward breaks the seal between the pump and your breasts.

Unfortunately, you can not use the pumps while they are charging. You have to pay attention to how long it has been since your last charge if you don't want to risk a shorter session or hope the app is willing to stay connected to your device long enough to read the battery charge. While the Elvie does have a red warning light to tell you when the batter is low, it does not last long.

Honestly I wish I could trade the Bluetooth capability for a longer batter life and just use the pump as is while being able to update the firmware via USB connection to a PC. I also wish the pumps could be used while charging. Still, as long as you avoid the app, they are excellent pumps and I would definitely recommend them to anyone willing to spend the extra money for mobility.

I have to stand over my kitchen sink to catch everything that pours out of the device and leaks off my body when I try to remove them. The auto-shutoff will decide not to shut off from time to time, and the only way you’ll know it is when you start to feel something warm and wet, and you’re not holding your baby. Clothes get ruined, so make sure you’re pumping at HOME in sweats, which completely defeats the purpose of all the advertising.

3. It’s not silent, and it gets LOUDER with use. Mine started creaking, yes, creaking with every single pump, so imagine that sound while you’re trying to watch a movie with your baby daddy next you you on the couch. Make sure the volume button is handy, folks.

4. You cannot move - at all - without suffering the wrath of the Elvie. There are times when your baby cries - surprised? Well if you are pumping with a Elvie, there is little you can do about it until you stop pumping. If you try to console baby AND pump, Elvie will know, and she will punish you for it. Usually with one of the above consequences. I got Elvie so I could move more than with the tube type pump. That is not what I got.

5. The charging system is kinda whack. The cords are old micro-usb, which is lame. One of my cords quit working day 2. Just annoying, really, but worth noting in my diatribe. More importantly - you can’t pump while they are charging, and the batteries die after a day of pumping. So if you wake up desperate to pump, beware the dead batteries! You have to plug these up every night, and sometimes more often, or you’ll be literally hurting.

6. The app is annoying! You may think if you constantly check the volume level, you can avoid an over full/leak situation, but you’d be wrong - again. Things the app does all wrong:

a. Does not have an accurate measurement of what’s in the container. It will tell you it’s full when it’s got 3 oz. in it, because you breathed too deeply or, heaven forbid, you tried to hold your baby because he needed to be held. The flip side of this is the above reason #2.

b. When it “decides” it’s full, the app will tell you OVER AND OVER again without stopping, like an evil pop-up that can’t be blocked. You’ll find that it actually makes it difficult to hit the “finish” button because it will not stop: “Bottle Full R” - click Ok, got it. “Bottle Full L” - click Ok, got it. BOTTLE FULL R BOTTLE FULL L BOTTLE FULL R BOTTLE FULL L - forever without end until you tap the Finish button before you even have a chance to check to see if they are, in fact full. (They won’t be, because you probably moved 1 degree in some direction at some point during the session).

c. There are other app issues, but I have to go check to see if my bottles are actually full, so I gotta go.

All of this is said after ordering a second Elvie, thinking the first was the problem. All of this is said even though I do have a Medela pump through my insurance which works just fine except the intense depression that sets in when you have to completely disrobe and put on a special pumping bra just so you can at least have your hands back.

I wanted the freedom promised by a Elvie. That is not what you get.

Product Title: Elvie - Single, Wearable Breast Pump w/App - The Smallest & Quietest - Portable - Hands Free & Discreet - Automated w/Four Personalized Settings - Includes 3 Sets of Breast Shields
Author: Kayla Bartoli
Review Text:
For context, this is my review after 3 months of use with a 3 month old and a 3 year old as a stay at home mom.

I have nothing to compare it to except my Spectra S1, but even that is more portable than these wearables...

Pros:
● Wearable - wireless, tubeless, fits easily into, not only a pumping bra, but even a not-too-tight sports bra
● Output - actually comparable to my Spectra
● Discreet - any time I have pumped in public, no one has had any idea until I took my pumps out of my shirt. They are not overly bulky and they are super quiet.

Cons:
● Leaking - Leaks FAR too easily - I cannot change a diaper or feed or even be barely hunched over or else they will leak, which in my eyes, defeats the purpose of a wearable
● Pump Parts - parts are too fragile - you cannot even put them into a sterlizer or else they will shatter/crack. I dropped one of the sheilds once by accident and it cracked. For a mother of a new baby (and 3 year old), the parts should be far more resilient considering the accidents that could happen.
● Charging - the charging cords it came with were garbage - they have barely worked at all. I would have to move the pumps around and contort the wires in very specific ways every time I charged them just to get the charging light to come on... I almost thought it was the pumps giving me the difficulty until I bought a 2 pack of fast charging wires for $5 on Amazon and they instantly worked; no contorting required. Which is WILD that such expensive pumps didnt come with better cords...
● App - the app does not work well, at least for android. It is supposed to do all kinds of useful things like time your pumps, measure output, records pump times, and maybe more things that I have yet to discover because the app really doesnt work for me... every time I look at the controls to see how long I have been pumping, one of the pumps is always not working/loading, and the other one will allow me to see the timing for a moment and then will randomly stop the timer even though the pumps are still going. The output of milk is also SUPER inaccurate. There are all kinds of functions that the app is supposed to have, but when I press the buttons, nothing happens so it just doesnt work... and I will say. That is not because I am not tech savvy; it is just a garbage app.

To me, the cons far outweigh the pros. I literally only use them at this point because they are easier to put on, as they can go into any bra (even a sports bra that's not too tight) and because they are so expensive. Other than that, I honestly wish I would have bought a different set of wearables and saved my money AND got better functioning pumps.

After an hour of not receiving a callback, I decided to call them again. This time, I spoke to a gentleman and told him about my issue. He checked the system and said, "Yes, I see you ordered the product a week ago, and it's weird it hasn't shipped because it is supposed to ship within 3 days for USA deliveries." I asked him when will the item be shipped out? He said he had no more information than that. I asked to speak with a supervisor again to learn when my product would ship. He told me to hold while he tried to connect me with a supervisor. After about a few minutes, he returned and told me there were none available. They were in a meeting and would call me back within the next two hours.

After 3 hours of waiting and not receiving a call back from the supervisor, I called back again, went through the whole process again, and asked for a supervisor. This time, I told her I would not wait for a callback and would rather wait in line because I'd lied to them twice already by telling me they would call me back within 1 or 2 hours and didn't. She told me to hold while she tried again to locate a supervisor. After about 30 minutes, she said she had a supervisor on the line for me, and her name was Sophie. Oddly, she had the same voice and sounded exactly like the person I spoke to. I explained my issues to her and would like to know why and when my item will ship. She said she had no more information and no communication with the shipping or processing department. She said there was nothing more she could do or tell me at this time. I asked her how it was possible she didn't know and couldn't find out the issue with my order. I asked her for her full name, and she replied Sophie M. Author: Callie
Review Text:
To preface this review I would like to add that I have worked with three different lactation consultant with my Elvie pump, so my review is not based off of poor fit, not using it properly, etc,

While the Elvie Double Breast Pump offers some positives, such as being quiet, discreet when worn, and easy to clean, the negatives unfortunately outweigh these benefits.

One of the most frustrating issues is the design of the suction cup. It lacks a rigid edge, causing a significant amount of breastmilk to leak from the bottom. While the flat suction side may add comfort, it’s hard to justify the milk loss. As any breastfeeding mom knows, every drop counts, and this flaw alone can be discouraging.

The app, which is meant to enhance the experience, falls short. There are no varied modes to simulate a baby’s natural feeding pattern—just a basic stimulation and expression mode, with limited intensity levels for expression. On top of that, the app’s tracking feature is unreliable, often displaying an output that is wildly inaccurate, leading to disappointment, especially for moms working to overcome low supply.

Finally, the battery life is a real letdown. It only lasts through about two pumping sessions, and even by the second session, the intensity noticeably weakens if the battery falls below 50%. This means you’re left recharging after nearly every 20-30 minute session, which adds unnecessary stress to an already busy feeding schedule.

Overall, I would not recommend the Elvie Double Breast Pump. Given its high price, these issues should not be so prevalent, and I found it to be more frustrating than helpful.

Review Title: Learning curve but totally worth every dollar and minute spent
Author: mmoseley
Review Text:
This product was a HUGE game changer for my family and I cannot recommend it enough. I needed to pump in order to give myself more flexibility and freedom without having to give my son formula if it wasn’t necessary. I pump when I’m driving, blow drying my hair, making dinner. Seriously amazing.

There was, however, a learning curve to this. It took me 5 sessions of pumping, reading the guides provided on the app, and adjusting/readjusting to get the suction latched on just right to where I was actually producing a lot.

My advice: read the directions thoroughly! Suction is everything and if you don’t fit it super tightly in your bra, you’re not going to get NEARLY as much milk. I had them loosely in my bra and the suction on the flange wasn’t completely sealed all around my breast and I produced a 1/2 oz from both breasts combined… once I kept at it and figured out the suction and which flange would fit my nipple best, I produced 3 oz between both breasts in half the time! While you can def accomplish a lot of chores and things while pumping, don’t do things that cause you to lean over or have to be bounced around a lot because the suction with release and you’ll be pumping very little if nothing out. Next, create a solid routine/system for how you’re going to clean, dry and store your pump and it’s pieces. I have an amazing pump backpack that came with the pump my insurance provided me and I converted it to have everything I need for this pump so it’s incredibly easy to bring with me.

I feel like a human woman again with this pump because you don’t have tubes going everywhere and your nipple exposed. I hating pumping, I was embarrassed and it took SO much time out of my day. Granted, you still need to clean all the parts but you gain back so much time because you can do things!

Another thing I absolutely love is that for me, this pump helps to stimulate my breasts to produce more milk. You can literally wear these for an hour each day and get so much milk and it’s perfect because it increases your production overall which is something I needed because my son wasn’t getting enough milk at the breast and we had to start supplementing with 4oz of formula a day - which none of us enjoyed.

I’ve only been using this a few days (though I’ve used it like 7 times already haha!) so I’ll try to update as time goes on to be sure this product still stays as top notch as I currently think it is.

I hope this helps any lactating mammas out there to know that this is expensive but absolutely worth the time you gain back from it if you can afford it!

Product Title: Elvie - Single, Wearable Breast Pump w/App - The Smallest & Quietest - Portable - Hands Free & Discreet - Automated w/Four Personalized Settings - Includes 3 Sets of Breast Shields
Author: Anonymous
Review Text:
Third time breastfeeding and I am so happy to find the Elvie.. I used the Medela and it was great, just very tied down to a machine..  I then got the Willow and let me tell you why it sucked!

Elvie vs Willow

- the willow is much louder! You hear the mechanisms moving and have to walk around with a little motor rumbling in your bra.. Elvie has a very faint sound but all you really hear is the liquid hitting the container
- when held side by side the willow and Elvie are about the same size. But when in your bra your breast is much more flush with the Elvie and has a much more discreet look
- while pumping it’s crazy how smooth the Elvie is.. I have to check sometimes to see if it’s even on, but yup it’s working away you can barely even feel it .. the willow was a little more harsh no matter the settings (the Elvie just fits your nipple more natural)
- the functionality is exceptionally better with the Elvie. You can change whether your pumping left or right.. you can switch from expression to stimulation.. you can set a timer!  (willow doesn’t offer any of this) .. and the app is great and so far has been very accurate on volume pumped.
- cleanup! Once again the Elvie is just better!! The willow has parts that are small and can be hard to get into, and if using containers instead of the bag it’s difficult to clean in the small crevices. The Elvie has an awesome container and it easy to clean and pour milk out of.
- a major problem I had with the willow was milk spillage .. after you pump you need to flip this switch to seal it and then turn the pump over and after some time that became faulty and milk would just pour out getting the pump itself all wet. My legs drenched and sticky.. also if all went well with the flip, removing the container always spilled milk again. It’s messy!! The Elvie had me so in love when I realized it’s almost impossible to have a big spill. And with the container being on the bottom, it won’t spill all over the actual pump
- as for the seal… the willow does allow you to move a little more (bending over and such) but if you keep the Elvie compressed nicely to your breast with no gaps at all with a bra you won’t have any spillage!
- the willow only has a 1 year warranty (which I learned the hard way that isn’t enough) .. Elvie has a 2 year which makes me feel they are more confident in the product
- oh almost forgot,, the Elvie comes with extra container AND a different size nipple flange (this cost extra for willow)
- the Elvie uses a usb charger so it can be plugged in almost anywhere.. even the car. The willow uses a standard dc plug and makes it hard to charge on the go

Being I just got the Elvie I can’t comment on the long term durability.. but I can already tell the Elvie is made way better and much higher quality than the willow

Why I went to Elvie
- I used my willow pumps for 4 months, they worked just fine. Stored it for a year.. went to use it again and one never turned back on and the other one worked for a few days after which a pin broke off of the pumping mechanism and is completely useless now. After calling and just being over my year warranty willow basically said TOUGH LUCK.

Review Title: Thought I'd love it, very disappointed.
Author: kirs
Review Text:
Let me say I am VERY disappointed in this product. I have tried on multiple occasions to keep using this product as well as seek support. It seems like there is always an issue. Aside from medical factors this pump leaks, has inconsistent suction, and randomly powers off (not pause, it turns entirely off). The only thing consistent about these pumps is the amount of issues it's causing. Over the last month postpartum, I have probably spent too much time stressing about this product.

Medically these pumps have caused so much pain and trauma to my nipples. After consulting with a lactation specialist, I was sized to the correct flange and STILL had pain. I went as far as seeing the doctor because blisters formed on my nipples, which ended up also causing thrush! Constantly having open sores from these pumps have led both the doctor and lactation consultant advising me to stop the use! Ridiculous that I'm out hundreds of dollars on these pumps and all the accessories I've invested in to try to make these work for me.

This product is promoted as pumping anytime/anywhere, silent, wearable, hassle-free, smart, and responsive. It's really unfortunate that I can find a problem with each of these categories….

How can I pump anytime/anywhere when I have been advised by support to sit still, in an upright position many times? To avoid leaking this is what I was told to fix the issue. NEWSFLASH this item STILL leaks when I do this! Besides the point, the #1 reason to buy this pump is the ability to be portable. When you barely have enough supply for your baby, it's very discouraging and disappointing to have it leak all over. Support also advised me to check all corresponding parts, which I have, and we found no issues there. Just told to sit still…. Which doesn't even fix the issue. What a joke. Makes me wonder how much milk I'm really missing out on, how much my baby is missing out on? What if these didn't leak, could I no longer need to supplement with formula? Really sad I have to stress about this!

A silent pump would be great. I have addressed this issue with support as well. Squeezing and a thumping sound (not how it typically should sound) takes place. While they have replaced the pump before, this issue continually arises! Not only that, but I notice every time it occurs, the pain is even worse! Again, pain which has caused blisters and damage to my nipples leading medical professionals to advise me to stop using the product.

Sure, the product is wearable, BUT why would I want to wear this anywhere when all it does is leak? As mentioned above, I've been advised by support to sit still when using. Either way, the product still leaks! So as far as being wearable, I'll pass since I soak through my bra and shirt anyway!

Hassle-free is a JOKE! While there are only 5 parts to clean, the hassle comes from all the issues which no one can seem to resolve. Continuously saying the same tips (which haven't worked!) and sending new hubs is not fixing these issues that keep occuring. These hubs are a complete hassle and very stressful for a new mom trying to feed her baby.

The smart component would be great if the app didn't glitch every so often, but more importantly if the hub would correctly track pumping. Continuously being told the bottle is full and the hub pausing makes pumping longer and more stressful. Even when the bottle is less than half full I run into this issue. Sometimes instead of pausing, the whole pump powers off! Unacceptable! How can I control the pump remotely if it turns off? In addition to this they are constantly losing connection with the app! What a HASSLE.

Responsiveness is nice when it switches modes, but again, the bottle full detection is far off!

To say the least, I am disappointed, stressed, furious, and unsatisfied. With multiple attempts at searching for help from Elvie customer service with no success and being advised by doctors to stop my use of this product before I cause permanent damage, I find myself out of hundreds of dollars. I have tried many times to make these pumps work, truly. How can I return these and get my money back? I am over the pain and stress. I would simply like to feed my child without pain, discomfort, stress, or permanent damage.

Review Title: Great for busy moms and on the go!
Author: Bailey Nelson
Review Text:
I’m a very busy mom of three juggling distance learning and taking care of all of my SAHM duties. My youngest is 9 month is exclusively breast fed along with actual food just no formula. She constantly attached to me and being busy having to sit down to feed her and then pump for extra time is just in the cards for me. I had a different pump which works great the spectra 2 but I couldn’t do anything but sit, and when you have a million things to do sitting is not an option.
Another reason I decided to try Elvie was I could now allow my husband to help and bond by feeding when I needed a break or  while making dinner or in the evening. I can pump while doing dishes or the laundry. But what I really enjoy is I can still nurse my 9mo old while I’m pumping and she doesn’t even get bothered by the pump. My old pump she would tug on and break suction even while wearing a pumping bra.

Ease of use: assembly is very simple. There are paper instructions or you can use the app. It instructed me you to put it together when I first got it and how to start my session. The app is easy to set up and connect each time you use it.

Features: being able to start the pump manually or through the app is great. I can set a timer change the speed or suction power without having to touch pump if I’m out. It has a sensors that monitors mild output and surprisingly it’s pretty accurate with little to no adjustment when I’m finished pumping. Some people said the light was super noticeable but it doesn’t seem to bother me.
If you tend have longer pump sessions than the pump can get pretty warm when you go to take it out.

Comfort: my first thought was how can this be comfortable? But once you get the hang of placement you barley know it’s there. It’s not super noticeable but since I purchased the single pump my chest looks a little lopsided, but any mom knows we have days where one breast is much bigger when breast feeding.

Cleaning: I read a lot of reviews between Elvie and Willow and this one seem to have better reviews for cleaning. I would have to say that cleaning this one it’s actually easier than cleaning my original pump. I can’t even dry it in the collection container fully before reassembling. You may need a few bottle cleaning tools. I currently use the set of munchkin bottle cleaning tools and a doctor brown brush with a soft scrubbing top. And it is small enough to get into the collection container and clean every little nook and cranny. Since the pump portion cannot be submerged in water you need to make sure to take a wet towel and clean off the seals in the area world the Milk passes into the collection container because it can start to build up there.

Mechanical: my first thought was that it was going to be very loud like my original pump. That is one thing that I really like about this pump it’s very quiet and is actually much more comfortable than a traditional pump. Because it is designed to hug your breast it’s not just sucking in your nipple. There are different shields that you can purchase if you need one that is larger than the one that it comes with the one that it comes with is a 24 mm. Which is The standard size for most breast plan on market.

Overall I would 100% recommend this pump to anyone who is trying to make their life easier or for someone who is going back to work and exclusively pumping. To a mom who’s at home running around dealing with crazy children and a house and looking for a way to pump more effectively and efficiently. The only company I have is if the pump is beginning to get full in the reservoir bending over can sometimes make it leak or spill somehow. I haven’t exactly figured out why it would leak when I would bend over because it is sealed very well. That is my only complaint so far. It charges fully in roughly 2 hours when I took it out of the box. And I just plug it in after every session to make sure that it’s charged up.

Parts: I love that it comes with two shields so I can pump and not have to clean it right away and have a second to use. It also comes with a carry bag so if I’m going to be mobile I can bring a clean one with me. I chose to go with a single pump and I’m glad that Elvie has The option to have a single which is why I ended up landing with them in the end. I had heard good things about the Willow but I also didn’t like how people complain that it was very hard to clean compared to the Elvie who had purchased both pumps.

Overall if you do get the single pump or the double I think you’ll be happy with your purchase.

Review Title: Not good as a primary pump
Author: Brad
Review Text:
There a quite a few pros AND cons to this pump. Overall, I would say it's worth having on hand  (if you can afford it) but it did not live up to the hype and I made the mistake of making it my primary pump which did some damage. It's upsetting that a secondary or back up pump costs almost 3 times as much as a primary pump.

Pros:
 1. The obvious is that is cordless/portable. This in itself makes it worth having on hand. For me personally, my baby would not allow me enough time to pump without having to entertain him or pick him up at some point. My corded pump was not realistic for this reason. So the Elvie really allowed me to continue my breastfeeding/pumping journey. I don’t know that I would have been able to pump during the day without it.
 2. Its also very convenient being able to take it on the go. I don’t know how much I would wear it in public because it is not entirely silent and your boobs look comically huge with the pumps on. However, being able to pump in the car or while hanging out with friends and family was always a nice option.

Cons:
 1. It slowed down my production drastically. I felt like the suction power was good so I still can't figure out why this happened but once I started pumping full time with it my production went down and I would need to pump for 30-40 minutes at a time. Milk was coming out very slowly.
 I felt that the effectiveness of the pump got worse over time. For example, after pumping for 30 minutes i will have 2 ounces of milk. I will then hand express another full ounce. That’s 50% of what i pumped being left in the boob and after 30-40 minutes of pumping.
 I LOVED them when i first started. Maybe this is because over time my nipples got more elastic ruining my production. After having them for almost 3 months now i am buying the spectra to replace this. More money :|
 2. The instructions emphasize that ALL parts need to be perfectly dry in order for the pumps to work properly. Well the membranes (green discs) that are a main component in the suction process end up getting moisture/milk on them during my pumping session. It happens every session and I don’t know how to prevent this.
 3. I also feel like it made my nipples elastic. I had planned that I would use this at work, since my spectra was a pain to lug around. I started using it before I went back to work to see how it compared the spectra, with the hope that it would be the same/similar output. It was consistently lower, about 1-2 ounces. Since I am not an overproducer, and every ounce counts, I knew I couldn’t use this as my primary. I essentially started using it after nursing, if I felt I wasn’t fully drained. I ended up getting sized by an LC and found out that I needed an insert for the correct size since the flanges don’t come smaller than 21 mm (maymom insert fits great). With the correct flange size I was pumping much more, if I had a secured tank top over a bra, although still about 0.75 fewer ounces than my Spectra.

My biggest complaint aside from the output difference (which seems to depend on the person) is that the app and milk estimation is horrible. The Elvie people seem to be aware of this, and considering what this thing costs, hopefully they will fix it one day soon. My pumps constantly turn off because the estimator says they are full when they aren’t. Sometimes I have to hit the start button 20 times in a 30 minutes session. It seems to happen most often if you are moving about, so it could be because the milk is moving around. Last week, one of my pumps stopped connecting to the app altogether which is very frustrating because there is no way to know long it has been pumping otherwise. I haven’t been able to resolve this issue yet, but it’s not the end of the world.

The last straw was the fact that my shields stopped clicking into the pumps. Hence, I collect no milk because the pump doesn’t work properly. The first one happened and then the next day, the same thing happened to the other shield. I use this pump maybe once a day and I’ve only had it for a month. I sterilize it according the instructions, so it shouldn’t have gotten misshapened, but it seems that the only logical issue. I have come to this conclusion bc I can click on the other size shields (the size 28 mm) no problem. Replacement shields are 30 bucks and considering the pump was 500 bucks and a month old, I wouldve I hope wouldn’t have to dump money into it for it to work. I just sent a request to costumer services as they seem to have a 90 day warrantee on shields, but they haven’t responded yet.

Do yourself a favor and don’t get this! The cheaper Elvie stride has better reviews. Yes the unit is discrete but it still looks like you have something odd in your shirt. My LC recommends the baby Buddha for something more equivalent to the spectra/medala.

Update: customer service responded to me and they are excellent! They addressed all of my
Concerns. The shields will be replaced. They provided several suggestions for the app and estimation issues and if I continue to have issues they will replace the hubs under the 2 year warrantee. So there is a lot to be said for great customer service! Changing the stars to 3 for that.

Review Title: Eh. Mind changed after extended use
Author: J Moreno
Review Text:
***The below paragraph is my first review which I posted about 2 weeks after using the Elvie. My updated review is below this one.***

As a working mom I wanted to find a pump that would work for me on several aspects: pretty portable, easy to clean, good suction, not too many parts, comfortable. This pump checks most of the boxes. Its super portable. It has really good suction, way better that I though it would have considering it doesn't have tubes. There aren't too many parts, and its not murder on your nipples. Clean up is where I would dock a star. the pieces are all weirdly shaped and its hard to get them cleaned and dried easily. You definitely can, but it just takes a bit longer and is a little annoying. If you leave them to air dry it would probably be fine, but working I need to clean them after use. Additionally on clean up, transferring is a bit odd too. You have to use the pour spout or the milk drips on the counter. Also with the pour spout there is always some milk left in the bottle part that you cant get out. The last part I don't like is that when you take it off, there is a milk build up. Because of the way the shield is shaped its hard to get it off without dripping milk. Again, not a huge thing, just a minor annoyance. All in all I love it. I get better volume with this pump that I got with either of my Medelas or my Lanisoh. The app tracks it pretty well, but if you get any milk splash on the sensors it doesn't really work until you dry them off again, which is a hinderance while pumping. But if you stay upright and don't bounce around the sensors are fine. It is really small to travel with and the battery life is pretty good. I can pump 3 or 4 20-30 minute sessions before I have to charge, so basically I just charge it every night. Its very comfortable and pretty quiet. Its not silent like it says on the description, but with the light office noise and tv or radio you don't really hear it. The loudest part is the milk dripping into the bottles but there is really nothing you can do about that. It quiet enough that I'm comfortable wearing it and pumping with my coworkers around. All in all if you're on the fence about it id recommend it. I love how much milk it gets out and how portable it is. Its definitely worth the price to me.

***UPDATE***
I've been exclusively pumping with the Elvie for about 3 months now. I am still a fan of the amount that the pump gets. HOWEVER the bottles are not labelled correctly for ounces. What the Elvie bottles say is usually about 1/2 and ounce different than the actual volume. So, if I was bagging milk and the bottles said I have 3.5 in one bottle and 2.5 in the other, I would label that bag for 6 ounces. It is actually only 5 ounces. That makes a big difference when your baby is hungry and eating a specific amount. The battery life is still good. The sensors worked well for the first 2-3 weeks and then not really ever again. They ALWAYS stop the pump telling it the bottle is full, but normally the bottle only has 2.5-3 oz. That really sucks because you have to tell the pump to start again every few minutes and you cant really trust if the bottle is full or not. As for the main problem. LEAKING. Idk what the secret is to get it to not leak. I had the best luck the first few weeks with it not leaking. After that I've had it leak on me about 6 times. It really sucks because by the time you notice your shirt is all wet and its wasted at LEAST an ounce of milk.

It definitely still has its upsides, but its not as great as I first thought. If you're debating between the Willow or the Elvie the leak proof bags of the willow would sell it for me.

Author: Allison
Review Text:
I like this pump, however it does have its pros and cons. (Pros far outweigh the cons)

For starters, I work as a police officer, an EMT and am a student. I purchased this pump to be used while I’m away from home but do not have as much privacy as preferred to be able to pump.

So for the pro’s:
I like that the pump is quiet while working. The first time I ever used it while out and about, was at my mother in laws house. I went to the bathroom to place them in my bra, as I was still learning how to position them correctly and like the privacy of the bathroom to do so. I returned to the kitchen table with everyone else while the Elvie did it’s job. My husband, who knows I use this, never even knew I was pumping. THATS how quiet they are when they work.

The suction is good and I feel I am able to pump as much milk with these pumps as I do my medical-grade Motif Luna. I notice it takes me longer to empty my breasts with these versus the Luna, but I make the same amount. I can empty my breasts completely with the Morif in roughly 6 minutes, it takes between 15-20 minutes with the elvies.

I love the portability of the Elvies as mentioned before. While in class and working on the ambulance the Elvies are nice because they tuck discreetly in my shirt/bra and I can go about my time as usual while they do their work. I sit in class for lectures ans can also drive the ambulance during transport to the hospital while emptying my breasts.

The cons to me are the time it takes to empty my breasts. I’m not sure what’s causing that, however it takes me roughly 3x the amount of time for a pump session with my Elvies than it does my motif pump. For that reason I rarely use the Elvies while working at the PD. I do not get dedicated pumping breaks, so I have to be as quick and efficient as possible and these just aren’t. So that was disappointing.

A second con is that you have to be extremely careful about making sure all pump parts are dry prior to attempting a pumping session. If any of the seals or flanges have any moisture to them the Elvie cannot maintain suction and will pause until the error is corrected.

Overall I really do like the Elvie and the cons are not huge issues for me, as I have a secondary medical grade pump for working at the PD. I have recommended this pump to teacher friends as I feel this will be extremely useful for them.

The Elvies do appear rather bulky while being worn, but I’m rather small stature... 5’0” and 110lbs. So they do look very large on my chest, but that does not bother me enough to be a deal breaker.

Third, I’ve noticed that the pumps themselves have began to look rather dingy and I have not yet found a way to clean them well.

I have been using these pumps for 3 months prior to making this review.

Overall, I do not regret this purchase and would recommend to others.
