Product Title: Elvie - Single, Wearable Breast Pump w/App - The Smallest & Quietest - Portable - Hands Free & Discreet - Automated w/Four Personalized Settings - Includes 3 Sets of Breast Shields
Author: Hannah
Review Text:
So I finally caved and got this after pumping standing up in the bathroom at work every night and then ending up with a clogged milk duct after a crazy 16hr shift where I only got to pump twice. As a rapid response nurse, I never know when I’m going to get called to an emergency and the one pump room is often occupied. The Elvie has made pumping at work and home a dream. And I never thought I’d say that about pumping!!
1. This pump is definitely not for everyone. After extensive research it seems like the effectiveness of this pump largely depends on your breast shape, nipple, let down, etc. For me, it works BETTER than my Spectra!! It’s less uncomfortable and I get twice as much milk pumping with the Elvie. Definitely not what I expected!
2. Super portable! I pop them on in the bathroom and then can go chart at the nurses station, drive to pickup my daughter from daycare, do the dishes, indulge in a 15min skincare routine, the options are endless. I wouldn’t do anything crazy, or anything that requires a lot of bending over since I did read that leaks can happen. I try to minimize walking as well since it sloshes the milk around a lot. I’m definitely not coding a patient while pumping, that’s for sure.
3. It does makes your boobs look massive (this Dolly Parton meet Pam Anderson). Especially since I’m already a 32DDD, the girls look huge with the pumps on. But I wear scrubs at work which are baggy, you could also throw a hoodie or scarf over.
4. It is not completely silent. Someone sitting next to you could hear it, however, I don’t think it would interfere with phone calls, zoom meetings, etc. I don’t really care and am not shy around my coworkers. I usually just tell them I’m pumping lol.
5. It comes with lots of pieces! 4 sets of bottles/parts. The only thing there isn’t 4 of is the flange. There are 2 24mm and I think 2 28mm. You could always buy another set of flanges if you wanted though. It also comes with bra extenders which have enabled me to fit them in every bra I own (wired and wireless).
6. The battery life could be a little longer. I get ~3 20min pumps. But for the size it makes sense that they can’t have a huge/heavy battery. It takes about 2hrs to charge I think, but I can’t say I’ve timed it.
7. I have read that the battery can crap out or the device can be damaged by milk. Also, that parts can warp over time despite following sanitizing instructions. However, I also read that Elvie has excellent customer service and will replace parts, even the device with a warranty.
8. One last point, the pieces are similar to my Spectra and it’s about the same time to wash. It just takes some time for them to dry.
Long story short, it’s a gamble, but if they work for you it’s worth every penny. There are lots available on eBay that are open box or someone is selling bc it didn’t work for them. I chose to buy new to ensure that I got the warranty. My stress levels over pumping have decreased dramatically and I am putting more milk in the freezer for my baby.

Review Title: Does not work consistently, requires a lot of troubleshooting.
Author: Andrea D
Review Text:
I have a love/hate relationship with this pump. I tried a single pump to start with to see if it would work for me before I went back to work. I had occasional issues with the suction not working that I was able to troubleshoot okay, so I decided to buy a second one so I could double pump hands- free at work.

 After my first week and a half back at work, I am very frustrated. When both sides work, it's great and makes life much easier (as a $500 beast pump should). However, both sides working at the same time only occurs about 30% of the time. I usually end up having suction issues with one side or the other (does not seem to be specific to the breast or the pump I use).

I have read the instruction manual and watched several videos to help troubleshoot the issues. If the suction disc is moist at all- it will not work. If the silicone valve lip is tucked under the opening on the pump- it will not work. If my nipple is aligned incorrectly with lines on the breast shield- it will not work (and yes- I made sure I am using the correct size shield). After making sure all of these potential issues are addressed- I will still often have problems getting the pump to work. A lot of the time I have good suction at the start and get the pump secured in my bra (and yes, I've used different types of bras/and tight undershirts to ensure the pump stays in place), only to lose suction 5, 10, 15 minutes into a pumping session. I have to start and stop multiple times during a pumping session to replace the pump and get the suction working again. Many times after all of this, I just give up and use my manual pump and then curse about the time I just wasted trying to get the Elvie to work on top of time it takes to just manual pump anyways.

The one positive I will say is that when the suction does work, it stimulates very well (similar to the way an actual baby would) and I end up having a good amount of expressed milk. I found this aspect of the Elvie to be superior to the Medela pump in style that was covered by my insurance.

I am so disappointed this is not working for me consistently because I have read that a lot of women love this product. I think it would be worth the price for me if it worked the majority of time.  And even more stressful than wasting the money, I still don't have a hands-free pumping option for work. I have a very busy medical practice and don't have the time to be tethered to a wall or manually pump for 20-30 minutes 3 times per day. I have spent the past week and half back at work stressed out and running behind schedule for my patients, which is not acceptable and is not going to work for the next 9 months I plan on pumping at work.

I know I am not the first person to leave this type of review, and I am honestly not sure why this works so well for some women and not others. I wish so much that I was in the group of women it works well for, because the concept and overall design of this product are very impressive.

Disappointed, out $500, and searching for another hands-free portable option.

Review Title: Excellent pump, terrible app required for more than basic controls
Author: Celecia
Review Text:
This would be a 5 star review if not for the app. The app gives you more control over your pump than the buttons on the pump but most of the time it doesn't work. The Bluetooth connection is shaky at best. You also have to make an account and sign in just to get to the pump controls or update the firmware. The app requires location services permission and the phones location MUST be turned on just to control your pump. I'm not sure why since it's a breast pump, not a GPS trying to get me to my destination. One of the pumps has a slight issue that is mildly annoying when charging and I have wanted to try updating the firmware since purchasing the pumps in April but no luck.

That said, otherwise these are excellent pumps. They're not as strong as other pumps that plug into a wall but the tradeoff is being able to move around the house. I've been using the pumps while I get chores done. There's no feeling of being trapped while wearing them. They are quiet and don't wake anyone up even if I have to sneak in to a room to grab something or put something away while someone is asleep. They are also the only pump that has ever managed to pull a decent amount of milk out of my breasts. I don't know why but my body just does not like pumps. The milk containers are small and have to be emptied more often than other pump bottles but that's to be expected considering how portable they are.

If you move around a lot, it's a good idea to occasionally lean forward and let the milk flow into the collection containers from time to time. It is also a good idea to take a damp paper towel and very slightly moisten your breast or the breast shield to create a better seal before you begin pumping(sometimes I use lanolin for this if I'm going to be moving excessively). That extra step can mean the difference between being able to pump while getting things done or having to stay seated because leaning forward breaks the seal between the pump and your breasts.

Unfortunately, you can not use the pumps while they are charging. You have to pay attention to how long it has been since your last charge if you don't want to risk a shorter session or hope the app is willing to stay connected to your device long enough to read the battery charge. While the Elvie does have a red warning light to tell you when the batter is low, it does not last long.

Honestly I wish I could trade the Bluetooth capability for a longer batter life and just use the pump as is while being able to update the firmware via USB connection to a PC. I also wish the pumps could be used while charging. Still, as long as you avoid the app, they are excellent pumps and I would definitely recommend them to anyone willing to spend the extra money for mobility.

Author: Kristina Oates
Review Text:
So I start by saying that yes, I think this is the top of the line breastpump compared to others out there ... but come, with all the tech that is out there today, can't we do better?

Pros:
Compared to the bottles hanging off of your boobs, obviously this is a HUGE step up. It's rechargable, everything can be thrown right into a bag, it makes you look like you have an disturbingly large bust but it fits in most bras and is pretty quiet. (Note: it won't fit in all bras comfortably even with the bra strap expanders that it comes with, but it fits well in looser nursing sports bras. I found that if the sports bra is too tight, it pushes the pumps too close together and doesn't keep the best suction/pumping.) I work in an office with a glass window and can pump at work with full confidence. The other pro is the collection "cups" are wonderful as you just unclip, pour out, wash, and put back rather than having to use bags.

Cons:
1. NOT WORTH THE $! Unfortunately there's not much to do about this as it is still at least better than standard breastpumps, just saying.
2. They link to the app well, but there are serious drawbacks. If you leave the room while pumping and don't take your phone with you, they unlink from the app and you have to pause and possibly restart the app to relink. Along those lines, from what I can see you can't switch back to stimulation mode from expression with the buttons on the devices so you cannot use them without the app.
3. Despite what it advertised, you CANNOT bend over or lay down while pumping. It won't leak necessarily, but it tricks the device to think that the collection thing is full (even if it only has a little) and it'll stop pumping. Then you have to go on the app to tell it that it's not full and unpause.
4. To me they are definitely uncomfortable, but again ... at least better than the alternatives.

I hope this helps. I'd still recommend them if you're pumping regularly, but quality-wise they still have a loonnnggg way to go

Neutral:

1/2 oz: slightly below 20 ml line
1-3 oz: accurate
3.5 oz (105 ml): 95 ml line
4 oz (120 ml) 110 ml line
4.5 oz: 4 oz line

Review Text:
Nothing like as advertised. I have the double pump (had - it’s going back), and it has given me nothing but grief. Sooooo many reasons:

1. If you don’t assemble it perfectly and attach it perfectly, and I mean perfectly, it will not get suction. You will think you assembled it correctly, but 100% guaranteed you will immediately learn that one of the three pieces didn’t go together properly, which means it’s useless. It will drive you mad. Now imagine having to do this 8-10 times a day if you are bottlefeeding what you pump.

2. It leaks - everywhere - every time you use it. It leaks when you inevitably have to remove it to try to get it to work after realizing the above reason has happened. I have to stand over my kitchen sink to catch everything that pours out of the device and leaks off my body when I try to remove them. The auto-shutoff will decide not to shut off from time to time, and the only way you’ll know it is when you start to feel something warm and wet, and you’re not holding your baby. Clothes get ruined, so make sure you’re pumping at HOME in sweats, which completely defeats the purpose of all the advertising.

3. It’s not silent, and it gets LOUDER with use. Mine started creaking, yes, creaking with every single pump, so imagine that sound while you’re trying to watch a movie with your baby daddy next you you on the couch. Make sure the volume button is handy, folks.

4. You cannot move - at all - without suffering the wrath of the Elvie. There are times when your baby cries - surprised? Well if you are pumping with a Elvie, there is little you can do about it until you stop pumping. If you try to console baby AND pump, Elvie will know, and she will punish you for it. Usually with one of the above consequences. I got Elvie so I could move more than with the tube type pump. That is not what I got.

5. The charging system is kinda whack. The cords are old micro-usb, which is lame. One of my cords quit working day 2. Just annoying, really, but worth noting in my diatribe. More importantly - you can’t pump while they are charging, and the batteries die after a day of pumping. So if you wake up desperate to pump, beware the dead batteries! You have to plug these up every night, and sometimes more often, or you’ll be literally hurting.

6. The app is annoying! You may think if you constantly check the volume level, you can avoid an over full/leak situation, but you’d be wrong - again. Things the app does all wrong:

a. Does not have an accurate measurement of what’s in the container. It will tell you it’s full when it’s got 3 oz. in it, because you breathed too deeply or, heaven forbid, you tried to hold your baby because he needed to be held. The flip side of this is the above reason #2.

b. When it “decides” it’s full, the app will tell you OVER AND OVER again without stopping, like an evil pop-up that can’t be blocked. You’ll find that it actually makes it difficult to hit the “finish” button because it will not stop: “Bottle Full R” - click Ok, got it. “Bottle Full L” - click Ok, got it. BOTTLE FULL R BOTTLE FULL L BOTTLE FULL R BOTTLE FULL L - forever without end until you tap the Finish button before you even have a chance to check to see if they are, in fact full. (They won’t be, because you probably moved 1 degree in some direction at some point during the session).

c. There are other app issues, but I have to go check to see if my bottles are actually full, so I gotta go.

All of this is said after ordering a second Elvie, thinking the first was the problem. All of this is said even though I do have a Medela pump through my insurance which works just fine except the intense depression that sets in when you have to completely disrobe and put on a special pumping bra just so you can at least have your hands back.

I wanted the freedom promised by a Elvie. That is not what you get.

Another significant drawback is the subpar battery life, which undermines the pump's purported portability. Instead of offering the freedom to pump on the go, I find myself tethered to power sources, constantly monitoring battery levels to avoid interruption during pumping sessions.

Regrettably, my experience with the Elvie portable breast pump has been far from satisfactory. Despite its promising features, the product's fundamental flaws overshadow any perceived benefits. As a result, I've been forced to supplement with formula due to milk leakage and unreliable battery performance.

While I acknowledge the potential of the Elvie pump and appreciate its innovative design, the current iteration falls short of delivering on its promises. As a consumer, I urge the manufacturer to address these issues promptly and prioritize functionality over aesthetics. Until significant improvements are made, I cannot recommend this product to fellow mothers seeking a reliable breastfeeding solution.

In conclusion, while the Elvie portable breast pump may appeal to the modern mom seeking convenience, its performance fails to live up to expectations. As a new mom navigating the challenges of breastfeeding, I hope that my feedback will spur the necessary improvements to make this product truly worthy of its price tag.

I also feel like it loses connection to the pumps constantly, so I just don't really use the app that often.
And careful with the little one, too. Your baby can pause them when picked up or bump her head on them if you don't pad between her and the pump. Otherwise, once you figure out how to maneuver, you lose way less time interacting with your LO than you would with a more traditional pump.
They are also WAY more portable than many pumps out there and just as quiet as the top ones covered by insurance. I also find the shields way more comfortable than others.
With these, not only do I miss fewer pumping sessions, but I also don't miss out on so much of my life tied down to a large motor or an outlet.
There is also less to clean (no tubes), but the cost of replacement parts is higher than other brands. Convenience has a price, but it's well worth it.

Review Text:
This pump was worth the price. I had to choose between breastfeeding and being a FT working mom, until I discovered this pump. At first I was skeptical, but I figured I’ll try it since I was at the end of the line with sustainability of pumping at work. I have had it for two days, and it is worth every dime.

I have used both Medela and Spectra pumps, and this one is best for busy moms like myself. I’ve been able to type at my desk, to hold my baby, and also to drive while pumping. Review Text:

I have been able to pump so much more using this pump as I don’t need to be connected to a bulky pump, and can use it while I’m up and moving around.

It did take me a few tries to figure out how to get the suction to work (make sure all parts are assembled correctly, that none of the rubber parts are bent in any way, and that your nipple is well aligned in the shield), but once I got it figured out, I’ve had no issues. It empties my breasts in about the same amount of time as the Spectra most of the time.

The only drawbacks I have found so far is that the pump will leak if you bend over (only had this happen once), and you can only pump about 4 ounces at a time. It is fairly quiet, although not silent. If I am in a very quiet room, my husband can hear me pumping if he is within 10 feet of me. I’m planning on using it at work, so we will see if anyone notices then. It does make you look more busty, but isn’t anything that looks unnatural.

Overall this has been one of my best purchases, and I wish I would have had it with my other babies. My freezer stash is already way over what it has ever been in the past, just because I can pop one of these on and go about my day instead of having to sit down and pump.

Mind you, these factors such as suction, power, and use may be different for everyone but for me personally, the suction is a bit strong for me so I have to put it on the lowest setting (for reference, I place the suction on 3 expression mode on my Spectra for about 25-30 minutes and I'm squeezing aggressively).  I use the Elvie for 20 minutes and I swear, I pump more than on my Spectra.  Overall, I am so happy with the Elvie and the price is worth it for the convenience.  I believe that since this is a relatively newer product, their technology and quality will only increase in the next few years.  Their customer service is amazing also (it's a 2 year warranty).  One of my pumps was not charging or turning on and they replied extremely fast and had it shipped to me within a day.  Super happy customer!

**Update**
The one con to this is that I wasn't able to figure out how to fix the settings to where it will keep a constant suction level the same. I would sit there and all would be fine and then all of a sudden the suction level would crank up and geez it would be so painful. I would have this on for about 20-25 minutes and it does this religiously twice. So basically I have to sit there and watch it and when it cranks up, I have to lower the suction level.

Product Title: Elvie - Single, Wearable Breast Pump w/App - The Smallest & Quietest - Portable - Hands Free & Discreet - Automated w/Four Personalized Settings - Includes 3 Sets of Breast Shields
Author: Veronica
Review Text:
After 5 months of use I have lots of thoughts on this pump. At first I hated this pump because I didn’t know how to properly use it. I was getting minimal milk output. But just like any pump, you have to play around with the settings to see what works for you. I now use this more often AND get more milk output than my plug in pump.

Pros:
-Hands free, on the go pumping. This is by far the biggest positive about this device. For a working and on the go mom, this has been a life saver. There have been times I would have missed pumping if not for this device.
-Has great suction/pumping power ONCE YOU DETERMINE WHAT SETTING WORKS BEST FOR YOU. I urge you to try different sucking strengths to see what works best. Also, in my experience, wearing a tight fitting sports bra while pumping got the highest milk output.  I now get more output from this than from my plug in pump and this only occurred after I found what setting worked best for me.
-Charges quickly. I get about 2.5 20 minute pumps out of a charge but it’s easy to throw on the charger between pumps. Would recommend purchasing a double charging cube and cord so you just plug one cube in to charge both devices.
-It’a quiet. This thing is much more quiet than my plug in pump. You can hear it if you listen closely but cannot hear it on a phone call, etc. It’s very quiet.

Cons:
-You cannot bend over while wearing these. I repeat DO NOT BEND OVER WHILE WEARING. Milk will spill. I have heard of hacks to get milk to not spill if you bend over but have not tried them.

Product Title: Elvie - Single, Wearable Breast Pump w/App - The Smallest & Quietest - Portable - Hands Free & Discreet - Automated w/Four Personalized Settings - Includes 3 Sets of Breast Shields
Author: Michelle K.
Review Text:
My youngest needs fortified breastmilk, which involves some pumping on my end in addition to nursing. I also have a very busy two and a half year old, which makes being tied to a wall VERY challenging. Additionally, I plan on pumping when I return to work as a teacher in the fall. I needed something that would allow me to multi-task. I have used the Freemie cups in the past, but the idea of being handsfree and cordless was especially appealing. I have been using these for about a week and I absolutely love them. The suction is just as good as my Spectra and I get plenty of milk from them. They are easy to clean as long as you don’t have a leak (see below). Some reviewers have said there is a learning curve with aligning them on your nipples. I am use to Freemies and so I had no issue with that. It also comes with a lot of helpful directions. The best part is I am free to empty the dishwasher, cook dinner or play with my toddler. Time is precious!

The only negatives I have found are with the app and some leakage. You have to be really careful not to bend forward with these. Otherwise milk will leak out the release button. When they do leak, it’s a little challenging to clean and I worry that I am doing a thorough job. The app is also useless. It takes some time to setup each session and I find it’s just as easy to control things on the actual pumps. So I don’t bother connecting it when I am pumping.

Overall, these are worth every penny! I highly recommend for the busy, working mom!

Review Text:

Huge Cons-

LEAK CITY! So all and all you still have to lay down.

PROS-

Review Text:

I would never attempt to use this during a meeting with colleagues for example which I have seen mentioned in other reviews. It is quiet but certainly not silent. I have had multiple visitors ask, “What’s that noise?” You very much still need to utilize a nursing bra to wear this pump properly. Estimate of how much milk you have pumped is never accurate. This wouldn’t be so bad if the pump didn’t automatically shut off once you’ve pumped 4oz. Whenever i have pumped 3 it thinks it’s 4 so I have to empty the bottle a whole oz early taking up even more time. If you lean too far forward it leaks so no emptying the dishwasher with this on like i had hoped. And for me milk runs down the plate and everywhere when i remove this (even if i tilt my body slightly forward.) My biggest complaint is I have ruined two sets of the breast shields (I’ve only owned this for 3 weeks) during sterilization. I have followed their EXACT sterilization instructions provided both times. They claim this can be sterilized in the microwave but recommend doing so for no more than 5 min. I did 3 min and they are warped which renders them unable to be used. Customer service was willing to replace them. In their email to me they said that they are running into issues and perhaps microwave sterilization isn’t the best for their product. I WOULD NEVER HAVE SPENT $500 ON A PUMP WITH PARTS THAT CANT BE STERILIZED IN THE MICROWAVE. No new
mom had time to be boiling pots of water!! But alas that is what they recommended I do. SO I used the boiling water method with the next set and  guess what? Yup, another shield warped, ruined and can’t be used. Haven’t heard back from customer service yet. Hoping they get back to me ASAP bc I exclusively pump and being without this is a huge set back and time suck. Not sure I would buy this again. I still use my Spectra half the time bc I know it’s going to work strong and fast without any time wasted messing with an app etc.

7. Mobile/hands free - could not type- awkward with spectra - I forget the elvie cups are on when typing/working.

Review Text:
I’ve had enough!! So much so, I am willing to waste my time with an infant by my side and write a review so other new moms don’t suffer like I have.

I have purchased this piece of garbage twice!! Yes twice. Because when it works, which is 10% of the time, it works great. The suction is better than my spectra s1. It’s also convenient to care for a newborn and infant with low profile cups.

With that said, only because I’m a complete fool did I continue to purchase parts for this garbage every single time it stopped working on me. Sometimes when a part fails mid-pump, suction messes up and milk goes into the tubes, and into the motor. This happened to me at least 4 times now in 6 months. If you’re lucky, you catch it before the pump breaks. I wasn’t so lucky once and had to repurchase the entire pump kit. When I received the new pump, the tubes were kinked, brand new out of the box. I reached out to the company and they sent replacement tubes right away. So their customer service wasn’t bad, at least from my experience.

As I sit here for the third day, suffering because I can’t get a decent pump, I decided to finally write a review and warn about this thing. I’m currently using just one cup, one breast at a time, because this thing failed on me once again and I can’t tell which piece of rubber is the culprit. I’ve changed out several parts, waiting on the final piece with the gasket to see if that will fix it. Product Title: Elvie Stride Hospital-Grade, App-Controlled Breast Pump - Hands-Free, Wearable, Ultra-Quiet & Electric with 2-Modes, 10-Settings & 5oz Capacity per Cup

This has definitely improved my pumping experience and I would recommend it to anyone who needs a hands-free pump! It comes with a 24mm size shield. You can purchase 21mm or 28mm separately, so if you know you need one of those sizes, go ahead and buy that at the same time because it does not include different size options. Its discreet design means I can pump at work, while running errands, or even during a Zoom call without anyone noticing. However, getting the placement right is key to avoiding leaks, which can be a bit tricky at first.

In terms of cost, the Elvie Stride is on the pricier side, which might make it less accessible for some. However, for the convenience and freedom it offers, I believe it’s worth the investment if it fits your budget. The Spectra S2 is more affordable and offers excellent performance but lacks the portability and flexibility of the Elvie Stride.

When compared to my spectra, another popular hospital-grade pump, the Elvie Stride excels in convenience and mobility. The Spectra requires you to be stationary since it's a plug in pump. It’s also way bulkier, like carrying carrying a bowling ball

For me, the Elvie Stride’s hands-free functionality outweighs its slightly lower suction strength. It’s a perfect choice for moms with an active lifestyle who need flexibility while pumping. If you’re looking for a more traditional, stronger stationary pump, the Spectra S2 might be your go-to. Both pumps have their pros and cons, but the Elvie Stride has given me the freedom to pump on my own terms, and that’s been a game-changer!

Product Title: Elvie Stride Hospital-Grade, App-Controlled Breast Pump - Hands-Free, Wearable, Ultra-Quiet & Electric with 2-Modes, 10-Settings & 5oz Capacity per Cup
Author: Kim
Review Text:
Update: I've been using my Elvie Stride almost exclusively for 5 months. I'm an exclusive pumper and have more than 10 pumps to compare with. I removed stars, because it's time to replace parts and customer service responses.

Replacement parts:
Boy howdy is it pricey and a little ridiculous. Just replacing valves and diaphragms will set you back $50 which is bad enough, but it's the seal that dropped this pump from a 5 * review. You have to buy a completely new container to get the seal. I'm not the greatest environmentalist, but even I balked at the waste created by partnering a silicone part that should probably be replaced every 3 months with a hard plastic which probably could last a year or longer (but if you listen to most bottle manufacturers that use the same material, 6 months) and not making that silicone part available.

Cup pop issue and response:
Another annoyance is that the cups pop apart when cold, even brand new. I brought this up to Elvie and though they replaced a set of cups (those pop apart when cold too), they said this was likely caused by sterilization. Their advice was to not boil the cups (bring water to a simmer only) and to keep the seal on the cup for washing. Boiling sterilization is what's in the manual, so why say you shouldn't? They said UVC was not tested so was not recommended. I'm just wondering how a pump manufacturer can get FDA approval for their pump that can't handle sterilization. Regardless, I use a rubber band when transporting my cups to work and at work so they don't pop and ruin my day.

Previous review:
I was looking for a handsfree option so I could get things done while pumping. I have a Spectra S1 and it's great, don't get me wrong, but to make it handsfree is a challenge requiring a lot of extras. This translates to more money and more things to setup just to pump. Even so, there was always some obstacle to getting things done.

Not with the Elvie Stride. Slide the cups in, attach the caps, clip the hub and turn it on.  Laundry, dishes and other chores are within reach. Need to run around the house, no problem. Better yet, it works better than my Spectra at emptying me which was surprising given Spectra's reputation. The pour spout is great for getting milk into a storage container.

Now, the Elvie Stride doesn't come without some drawbacks:
1) I find it hard to hold baby like normal. Also, he can't lay on my chest as he prefers when the cups are in.
2) I am busty, so when I put the cups in, I'm smashed together in my bra. When routing the tubes between and down, the tubes get squeezed, which causes a reduction in or no suction. To solve this, I route the tube over the cup and down.
3) It doesn't automatically tell you how much you've pumped in a session on the app and I'm not a fan of their markers on the cup. There is no flat edge to set the cup down to accurately see how much you pumped, you have to either pour into another container to get your volume or attempt to hold the rounded cup straight.
4) The lack of flange sizes! I need a 17 mm flange, but they only have 21, 24, and 28. Even a 21 reduces the volume I pump. I had to get an insert from another company which works great, but it adds 2 more parts that need cleaned. It would have been better to have a properly fitting flange.

Product Title: Elvie Stride Hospital-Grade, App-Controlled Breast Pump - Hands-Free, Wearable, Ultra-Quiet & Electric with 2-Modes, 10-Settings & 5oz Capacity per Cup
Review Title: Took some getting used to but I love it now!
Author: Gigi Rose
Review Text:
I bought this pump after being tired of stationary pumping. I was worried that it wouldn’t empty me very well, but it performed just as good as my medela pump - I know because I tried to manual pump after using the Stride a couple of times to check if there was more to give, and there were just drops.

I also read some reviews where people couldn’t get all the pumped milk out, so I do have a tip for this below.

PROS:
- love being mobile, I can get other things done like eating, washing dishes, etc
- relatively quiet, like a phone vibration
- battery lasts all day for me, I pump 5x 18-20 min a session, then charge at end of day
- pretty easy to clean, only 4 parts (I use the nanobebe electric brush and it makes it quick)

CONS:
- some things are still difficult but not impossible to do, like holding & feeding baby, and bending over can cause potential leakage
- placement on breasts takes some getting used to because it’s difficult to see in the little placement hole (I found this much easier with a bra that has a clip to come down so there’s more light coming through the sides over a sport bra)
- takes some practice pouring and getting all the milk out
- parts need to be completely dry when assembling which can be difficult washing & pumping every 3-4 hours
- when pump switches from stimulation mode to expression mode automatically, it goes back to the middle suction setting, even if you’ve turned it up during expression. I believe this can be changed in the app but it’s pretty annoying there’s no manual way to set this

TIPS:
- I use the fridge hack and keep the pump parts (assembled but obvs without the motor) in a covered container in the fridge between pumps, then wash my pump at the end of the day. Expressed milk can technically be left out 4 hours, and my 5x pumping at 20 minutes brings me to around 2 hours of the milk being at room temp, so I’m satisfied with that. Not everyone is comfortable doing this (it’s recommended to wash after each use) and I wouldn’t do this if baby were sick and only started doing this after our baby turned 4 months. It does mean that I put on the cups cold, which is not that pleasant, but I prefer it to washing.
- To get all the milk out, Elvie has a video taking the pump apart and pouring the remaining milk out that was stuck in the diaphragm. Since I do the fridge hack, I am not taking the pump apart. Instead after doing the initial pour, I make a pumping motion on the diaphragm (basically the same motion the pump makes - see image) to get the milk to come out, then I pour out the rest.

Product Title: Elvie Stride Hospital-Grade, App-Controlled Breast Pump - Hands-Free, Wearable, Ultra-Quiet & Electric with 2-Modes, 10-Settings & 5oz Capacity per Cup

Shortly after it lost suction and was pulling almost nothing. I have supply issues anyway, but could tell the pump wasn’t coming close to emptying me. So I took it ALL the way apart. I hadn’t been removing the green silicone around the cups and that was the issue - a fine layer of milk residue had made its way under and was compromising the seal. I used the dapple baby soap and a wash cloth and scrubbed everything super clean and let it dry. Immediately after, it pulled way more than it had in awhile. I use the fridge hack and clean it once a day, and do a quick clean daily… and DEEP clean once a week.

I absolutely prefer my Spectra with Pumpables Liquid Kits as I have elastic nipples, but Elvie Stride has been a great secondary piece. My only issue with it is that it’s “wired” with tubes. I’m planning on getting wearables that are much more independent soon.

Review Text:
These are amazing. Got one from my registry and found it worked so well for me I bought a second. They are easy to throw on before a car trip or a feed session and collect a bottle worth (55 early on, up to 120 on boob 3 weeks into baby). I can even be lying down (as long as in bra and sit up to remove).

I assume electric pump will be more efficient but I generally find it comparable to my Medela hand pump and I don't have to be bent forward pumping the whole time. Single silicone part makes it easier to clean too. My ICBLC friend found that these or Hakaa did not work for her because she has very elastic boobs and large nipples. Another friend never uses her Hakaas because she forgets; honestly I would never use them because you still have to be sitting fairly still and I do most chores with the Curve in (secured in bra).

My one comment is that the opening (flange equivalent) is an odd shape/size and my right nipple gets sore if I use it too often on it. I assume my nipples are just slightly different sizes because the left has never had a problem. To get the best suction too I will add - press the release valve to open presure and then squeeze the bottom and reseal the release to get the most suction. All in all great product would recommend to anyone (even full price, though got my second ina Mother's Day sale). Elvie's whole line look like great products and their website is SO EASY to navigate. I'm looking at the stride for my electric pump.

Product Title: Elvie Curve - Manual Wearable Breast Pump - Hands-Free, Kick-Proof, Portable Silicone Pump That Can Be Worn in-Bra for Gentle, Natural Milk Expression - Breast Feeding Essentials
Author: Kate
Review Text:
I tried a haaka with my first child and even if I could get the suction right, the moment I moved (let alone the moment she moved) it lost suction. I could never get more than a half ounce.

It took a few tries to master but I'm able to attach the Curve with one hand - it helps that I can suction it on and then adjust my nursing bra. This is perfect for midnight nursings for me - the baby usually only takes one side per session and I can get almost a full pumping amount on the left over side if I use the Curve.

I'm not a fan of pumping both sides at the same time, I find it really uncomfortable. Again I can stick this on the side I'm not pumping and get almost a full pump sessions worth. If I really want to drain that side, I'll just pump for five minutes at the end of the session.

Granted I've maxed out at about 4.5 ounces a side. So if you regularly pump more than that it might not have the capacity you need.

The little valve can be challenging when you pour out the milk - until you get the hang of it.
Cleaning is pretty easy if you have a bottle brush.

Product Title: Elvie Curve - Manual Wearable Breast Pump - Hands-Free, Kick-Proof, Portable Silicone Pump That Can Be Worn in-Bra for Gentle, Natural Milk Expression - Breast Feeding Essentials
Author: Sam J
Review Text:
Purchased for road trip to use on one side while nursing on the other. Baby is 7 months. Left on during and for 1 hour after feed and had 5-6 drops of milk in total. Sitting in the car, I had to readjust and reattach multiple times, but easy to use. Used around house a few times while nursing other side and had less than half an ounce.

For $50 I wanted to love this thing. Compared to the cost of the Haakaa, this thing is significantly overpriced for what it is . Its much more discreet and not as bulky, which was why I stopped using the Haakaa. Would have been more useful at the earlier months when milk supply is ample. For me, I never had an oversupply and never leaked or had a significant letdown on the other side while nursing. An electric pump with stronger suction works better.

If you have an oversupply, or letdown easily, I'd go with a cheaper silicone brand and save the $. You don't need the name brand and fancy packaging, which is what you're paying for. Plus they never go on sale. Its easy to clean, however when drying, water pools into the "release" button and can never fully dry. I had to shake out multiple times while on drying rack to shake out water that accumulated inside and spend an extra 15 seconds balancing it to drain properly. Author: SSDD
Review Text:
The Freemie is AMAZING!!  I would never have been able to keep pumping after I went back to work (9 months ago!) without it. I swear by this thing every day!

I have an industrial strength traditional one that I started off with at home (that I not-so-affectionately call the "Tit Tugger 2000") that I have to crank up to 10 as my boobs tend to be very reluctant to part with their hard earned treasure.  (it literally makes funny noises when it pumps at the suction setting I need)  The Freemie does great and still has a couple higher suction settings I could use if needed. I HIGHLY recommend.

A couple suggestions:

Use lube. Lube is as important at this end of the journey as in what got you in this mess to begin with! I use Nursing Butter and just put a tad bit on the inside of the funnel.  Works great!

Make sure you put the triangle shaped "barrier device" on the plastic outer piece and make sure it's seated well before putting the valve base on.  I've found that's usually what's wrong if I'm not getting adequate suction.

DO NOT BEND OVER. I repeat DO NOT BEND OVER.  You will be wearing boob juice, the floor will be wearing boob juice, the nearby dog will be wearing boob juice...  you have lots of maneuverability with the Freemie and I do many chores and activities while wearing it,  just not bending over more than about 45 degrees.

Cons:
Can be a little hard to totally clean, especially at the beginning when your milk fat content is the highest. I found taking a Q-tip to it every few washes gets all the little cracks and crevices clean.  That and the "don't bend over" thing are really the only cons I can think of.

Good luck on your pumping adventure!
Date: Reviewed in the United States on February 14, 2022

Product Title: Evenflo Manual Breast Pump
Review Title: Good portable option, a little painful...and save that little elastic thingy!
Author: IMHO...
Review Text:
I've owned two of these breast pumps so far. They are really very useful because they are small enough to throw in a diaper bag, yet powerful enough to pump when you are away from an electric breast pump. In several situations, including on an airplane and during a long work day, they have really been a lifesaver when you need to drain breastmilk. This convenience comes with a few problems, in this order:
1) The suction on the pump is pretty harsh on your anatomy. Until you get used to the pressure, it's downright painful. Best advice I can give is not to squeeze the handle all the way. Squeeze it part way only until you get to the right amount of suction for yourself.
2) Like most pumps, it's a PITA to clean. You have to open up the top and take out this gasket, and there's a little cup shaped apparatus on the bottom of the pump that you also have to remove and get into. The silicone piece around the horn (which helps to make it a little softer) is hard to get out, but then once you try to put it back on it has a tendency to want to pop off.
3) There's no way to seal the bottle once you are finished pumping. Therefore, if you accidentally tip the bottle over, the milk will spill out. I find it's best to just bring a breastmilk storage bag at all times and empty the breastmilk out right away.
4) Over time, the little elastic that keeps the pump handle going will get slack. They include an extra one in the package, but seriously by the time the first one wears out---being a new mom, you have already lost that little elastic thingy in some drawer with all the other little doodads that you've put away to avoid your little one chewing on then, and you won't be able to find it.
But, of course this is all in the context...A portable pump, very handy in some situations, but not a perfect product.
Date: Reviewed in the United States on July 25, 2016

Product Title: Evenflo Manual Breast Pump

Review Text:

Personally, I found manual pumping to be faster and as a working Mom we need all the time we can get back. So I know longer use the electric pump. When I firstr went looking into Manual Pumps I struggled between the Lansinoh and Medela. Mainly bc these are two well known names in BPs and assumed like many if its expensive it must be good. I opted for the Lansinoh which in all honestly does the job.  I've had the Lansinoh for about 3 months and it just stopped working well. It takes me about 30-40 mins to pump 5 ounces. The suction isn't what it once was and I can only guess is maybe there is a microscopic hole that is lessening the pressure. That being said, I didn't want to drop another $30-$40 on a new pump so I opted to give the Evenflo a try.  I recieved it yesterday and to my surprise I pumped 6 oz COMFORTABLY (you know what i mean) in 13 mins. I pulled more milk from each than I have in weeks with the Lansinoh.
At first, i t hought it was a cheap version of BP. The pumps are very shallow so I didn't think it was going to work but to my surprise its the best pump I've had.

I suggest to anyone for the $15.00 to give it a try.

I like having a milk collector (I use medela, but I assume haaka and others are the same) on one breast while I pump with this on the other. This Philips pump is very comfy for my breasts and flat nipples. I love the control I can assert and not having 2 different "strengths" like other manual pumps is surprisingly better for me, so I'm going based off instinct. That helps with my milk let downs.

For me and my lifestyle, this Philips works better for me than the purple Lansinoh manual one I got from Walmart to hold me over when my baby came early. This Philips one is also better for me than the yellow gimmick Medela pump with a spinning top that I keep almost dropping because it's hard to hold one-handed. Though the silicone collector the medela came with has done well for me alongside this Philips manual pump.

I also have an Elvie Stride 2 and don't get me started. That thing was a nightmare for me. It's harder silicone, I got rugburn on my areola and had my skin peeling from it. I started slathering on lanolin. It doesn't drain all my milk, I got a milk bleb, and mastitis. Every time I nursed, it felt like electricity going through me. My doctor said I may have an exposed nerve. I went to the hospital to see a lactation consultant and she confirmed my flange size. I had to wear a nipple shield for a few days while my nipple healed but still needed my baby feeding on it to drain the milk or I'd get more issues. Even after I confirmed I had the right flange, I still had to use the Lanolin, and it still wouldn't drain my breasts. I wear Lanolin with it just so I don't get  I got that through my insurance and I regret it. I really love this Philips manual pump by comparison. Author: Candice
Review Text:
I have been exclusively pumping for about 6 months now and I've used 4 different pumps. In general, I think I speak for a lot of women when I say the pumping experience is an unpleasant one, but some of these companies have got to be pulling some kind of prank on mothers.

For this pump in particular, I actually like it quite a bit. The parts are the easiest to clean of all the pumping parts I've used. The flanges are silicon and among the most comfortable for my nipples. The suction is good and my settings are remembered. I like all of that, but it has a few flaws. The flanges don't screw on tight. They are either screwed on 100% of the way, or they're loose. If you nudge them slightly, they come loose. That makes it a little more difficult to wear them while doing other things. The bottles have a ledge on the inside that collects milk that I'd rather give to my baby. It also makes it more awkward to pour milk if you're actually trying to empty the bottle where you might spill some if you aren't careful. The tubes are made of a silicon that every single piece of dust CLINGS to. They need washed constantly, just because of the dust that sticks to them. These flaws aren't even dealbreakers though. Like I said, the experience in general isn't a pleasant one, so some problems are to be expected.

What makes me extremely angry and disappointed with this product is that they actually expect you to pay about $160 for an extra set of parts through their website. That has to be a joke. Thats almost the price of the pump itself. The only thing I can think is that they are pricing their products for insurance companies or something because that is absolutely insane. There is no way it costs enough to manufacture those parts to justify that price point. It blows my mind.

I'm not buying the extra parts. When these ones wear out, I'll find something else.

Product Title: Philips Avent Single Electric Breast Pump Advanced, with Natural Motion Technology, SCF391/62
Author: Candice
Review Text:
I have been exclusively pumping for about 6 months now and I've used 4 different pumps. In general, I think I speak for a lot of women when I say the pumping experience is an unpleasant one, but some of these companies have got to be pulling some kind of prank on mothers.

For this pump in particular, I actually like it quite a bit. The parts are the easiest to clean of all the pumping parts I've used. The flanges are silicon and among the most comfortable for my nipples. The suction is good and my settings are remembered. I like all of that, but it has a few flaws. The flanges don't screw on tight. They are either screwed on 100% of the way, or they're loose. If you nudge them slightly, they come loose. That makes it a little more difficult to wear them while doing other things. The bottles have a ledge on the inside that collects milk that I'd rather give to my baby. It also makes it more awkward to pour milk if you're actually trying to empty the bottle where you might spill some if you aren't careful. The tubes are made of a silicon that every single piece of dust CLINGS to. They need washed constantly, just because of the dust that sticks to them. These flaws aren't even dealbreakers though. Like I said, the experience in general isn't a pleasant one, so some problems are to be expected.

What makes me extremely angry and disappointed with this product is that they actually expect you to pay about $160 for an extra set of parts through their website. That has to be a joke. Thats almost the price of the pump itself. The only thing I can think is that they are pricing their products for insurance companies or something because that is absolutely insane. There is no way it costs enough to manufacture those parts to justify that price point. It blows my mind.

I'm not buying the extra parts. When these ones wear out, I'll find something else.

I haven't had any issues with strange noises or it being too loud. No pump is completely silent but this one is very quiet. The cushioned flange is comfortable, too. More so than my Ameda pump.  I would be happy enough just having this manual pump, since I don't need one for multiple times each day.

Product Title: Philips Avent Manual Comfort Breast Pump
Review Title: Manual pump comparisons from three major companies
Author: J. Michelle
Review Text:
Having two kids and currently expecting a third child, I’ve come to possess multiple double electric and manual breast pumps. I currently own and Ameda, Medela and Avent manual breast pump. Between the three manual pumps I have noticed several differences.

Ameda
• Cost: 60USD when ordered as a single item direct or from a third party retailer. It can be acquired for free from various hospitals after birth or if one ordered an Ameda Purely Yours carry-all be included with the pump.
• Handle: This pump’s handle is connected directly to the piston and is the most taxing on the hands. It connects directly to the breast flange. The piston connecting to the handle at the top has a major flaw in that it is very thin and if one is not careful, can easily be broken. I have responded pretty okay to the pump, relieving engorgement with out the need for hand expression after in about 30 or so minutes.
• Screw Base: Like Medela pumps the pump is narrow based allowing for any standard sized bottleneck to be pumped into. With the use of adapters one can pump into wide based bottles available from various bottle manufactures.
• Parts: Replacement valves and flanges can be purchased at any major retailer online and in store. The breast flange is one piece having no body it connects to. The flange is a hard plastic item that can be uncomfortable to use. However the flange is angled well, allowing for milk to flow without the need for mom to lean forward to get all milk in the bottle. The flange can be easily converted out for use with the Purely Yours by removing the handle that snaps onto the flange and taking out the piston. The pump uses a full valve that gets pretty good suction and is very sturdy.
• Cleaning: This manual pump has the least amount of parts that need to be cleaned after use. There is the flange and valve only that needs a clean. Normally if home I would use the bottle I’ve pumped into for storage, eliminating transfers into disposable bags and the need to wash the bottle I’ve pumped into. (Side note: I’m lazy so I’d stick the bottle in the fridge for later use and do a batch washing of bottles at a later time.)
• Weight: Due to the nature of the handle/piston this manual is the lightest of all three I currently own.
• Response to the pump: I’ve responded to this pump fairly well. It did relieve engorgement easily and the amount of time needed to express was about 30 or so minutes when ever my hands wasn’t being taxed.

Medela
• Cost: 40 USD plus. The pump can be found at major retailers in store and online. It can also be included with the PISA or another Medela double electric that comes with all accessories if one orders it.
• Handle: The handle on this pump is far more comfortable to use than the Ameda. I never had any pain in the hands while using this pump. On the handle there is the symbol for two phase expression although one would need to turn the handle to access it.
• Screw Base: The pump is narrow based allowing for any standard sized bottleneck to be pumped into. With the use of adapters one can pump into wide based bottles available from various bottle manufactures.
• Parts: The pump has more parts than the Ameda. The flange is a separate piece from the breast flange body and doesn’t allow for milk to flow freely thus having me lean forward. The pump comes with a two part valve that comes with a very flimsy membrane that can be detached and washed downed the drain if one isn’t careful. (There are aftermarket companies that sell full valves that work far better than the standard valve/membrane jazz Medela puts out.)
• Cleaning: The flange, body and valve are an easy clean. Do take precautions when washing the valve/membrane as the membrane is fragile and can be easily lost or washed down the drain.
• Weight: The pump is much heavier than the Ameda however it’s not wearing on me when in use. It is heavier than my Avent also, as the flange is longer and separate from the body.
• Response to the pump: I believe this pump is one the lower end of my responding. With use I’ve always had to lean into the flange to get all of my milk in to the bottle. The membrane never provided adequate suction. (I do understand that it’s a manual pump but the membrane/valve combination is far too flimsy to provide any reasonable suction the way Ameda’s and Philips Avent pumps can.) After a pump session, I found myself consistently having to hand express pulling an extra 0.50-1.00 ounce expressed.

Avent
• Cost: 30 USD plus but no more than 50USD as seen on the manufacture’s website. The pump is a single item only. It can only be acquired via an direct purchase from the manufacturer or a third party seller. The pump will not be included with Philip’s double electric pump.
• Handle: The handle is a similar model to Medela’s pump and easy to hold when using the pump. It doesn’t cause pain to the hands while in use.
• Screw Base: The pump uses a standard wide screw neck. If you are a user of the classic Avent bottles you can pump into the bottle with their manual, however the anti-colic ring must be in use to prevent leaking. I have pumped into standard wide neck bottles not Philip’s with this pump.
• Parts: The pump has more parts than the Ameda and Medela’s pump. The flange is one piece as it doesn’t remove from the body. The comfort cushion and its cap make for the most parts in total. The pump has a full valve that provided me with excellent suction. (CON: Replacement parts for the pump can only be ordered online or direct from customer service if called.) Pump can be converted out for use with Philip’s double electric pump if one owns it. I have it in my procession and the flange is the same as the electric though the electric has different parts at the top. If a replacement stem or handle is needed it can be ordered from Philip’s replacement website. They do carry parts there for all of their products including discontinued products.
• Cleaning: The pump is easy to clean as the flange is the widest of all my manual pumps when the comfort cushion has been removed.
• Weight: Avent is lighter than Medela but slightly heavier than Ameda. It’s not heavy when in use.
• Response to the pump: Time span to use this manual is shorter than Ameda. It’s a very effective pump, even more effective than some double electric pumps. The comfort cushion also makes for one of the most comfortable pumping experiences I’ve had to date.
Note: With all of my pumps I do not use the standard 24/25mm breast flange. I use a 30/30.50mm breast flange. None of these pumps come with a flange size other than the standard. All pumps come with a bottle to pump into, use for storage and or feed baby from. (Ameda does not include a bottle nipple but any standard nipple can be used on their bottle. )

Overall I rate each pump as follows on a 1-5 Scale
• Ameda: 3.5
• Medela: 2.75
• Avent: 4
Date: Reviewed in the United States on April 1, 2017

Product Title: Philips Avent Manual Comfort Breast Pump
Review Title: I thought it might be a good idea to buy a more portable pump since we ...
Author: darbisonlewis
Review Text: This pump is a game changer for me.  I exclusively pump for my 2 month old twins who never quite got the hang of nursing.  With the holidays coming up, I thought it might be a good idea to buy a more portable pump since we will be traveling and back-and-forth to family gatherings.  As it stands with my twins eating every 3 hours, my daily routine is to feed the babies (an hour commitment when my husband is at work), pump with my Medela Pump in Style Advanced (about 30-45 minutes), try to hurry and clean a bit/grab a few moments of sleep/eat a meal/run an errand, then start all over again.  Needless to say, I've been accomplishing next to nothing and barely sleeping.  I got this manual pump 2 days ago, and it has changed my life.  Not only can I pump on the run if need be, but I'm getting more milk in less time.  With my Medela, I was getting on average about 6-7oz in a 45 minute pump.  Sure, with my hands-free bra I could eat or read while pumping, but how much can you really accomplish when you have to stay within tubing-length of a breast pump.  With the Avent Manual Comfort Pump, I'm averaging about 8-10oz in about 10 minutes of pumping.  I'm also able to keep my supply up (it was starting to peter off) because pumping is no longer as much of a planning/time commitment, so I can do it more often.  Previously, if I had a long errand to run, I would have had to skip pumping because I couldn't spare the 45 minutes.  With this pump, even if I can't pump until empty, I can quickly pull off a few ounces (I can usually get 4oz in the first 3 minutes) and be on my way.  I was really worried about losing my supply during the holidays when I wouldn't have as much time to pump, but I may skip bringing my double electric pump on our travels altogether.

Review Title: Comfortable but too many other negatives....
Author: Catra121
Review Text:
After two months of using a Medela Pump in Style, I decided to get a manual pump to make pumping more convenient when out of the house or when visitors were over (the electric pump is loud and set up in the room we use most...which is where our guests are when they come over). I bought two manual pumps...the Philips Avent Manual Comfort Breast Pump and the Medela Harmony. After a week of use...I have to say that I prefer the Harmony.

There are some positives to this pump...particularly that it is more comfortable to use. This is the result of the comfort petals and also the shape/design of the pump. I find that is really what this pump has going for...and not much else (though admittedly this is a BIG thing).

The things that I don't like about this pump...well...there are three big negatives for me.

First, this pump is VERY loud and squeaky. Sometimes if you pump the handle in just the right way it doesn't squeak...and sometimes it does anyway. It's quite annoying and not remotely discreet...I cannot imagine using this "on the go" because I would just be too embarrassed (and not by the pumping but by the ridiculous squeaking noises this thing makes).

Second, I can't see what is going on in there. I have no idea how much milk is flowing (or if it still is) while using this. I have a fairly low supply so sometimes it takes a while for the milk to add up...but with this pump I can't tell if I should keep going or not. That's a little frustrating. The collection container also has a very wide base and since I sometimes don't get a lot of milk...it's very discouraging seeing so little in the base of this container. Also hard to tell in the large size if it actually is adding up or not.

Which leads me to the last thing that I dislike about the pump...the collection container itself. If I had a bigger supply then this would probably be a positive thing. I like that you can pump right into the AVENT bottles and then all you need to do is screw on the nipple and you are good to go. Unfortunately...that's not the case and with this pump I constantly have to transfer what is pumped into another container. With the harmony I can pump right into the storage containers (which are not Medela but are a more universal size I guess that the Medela accommodates).

I won't be returning this pump as it is really comfortable AND I have found that when I have the time to do so...a combination of pumping with the AVENT and then an hour later pumping with the Medela Harmony actually produces the most milk. So I usually do this in the morning when baby is still asleep to get an extra boost in my milk supply.

Product Title: Philips Avent Manual Comfort Breast Pump
Review Title: Every breastfeeding mom should have one
Author: Kay J
Review Text:
This pump impressed me so much that I felt compelled to write my first product review. I'm a First time and pumping only mom. I had been using an Ameda Purely Yours double electric breast pump, an expensive and time consuming machine with rigid hard plastic and varying efficiency. It would take an average of 20-30 minutes to express 4oz. A friend recommended that I get a manual pump for times when I have to be away from home for more than 3 hours or for in case of emergencies or power outages. I picked the Comfort manual pump because,
1. The gel pad looked squishy and comfy and lord knows my aching breasts needed some comfort.
2. The price was more than reasonable, as a new mom and a grad student I need to be really careful how much money I spend.
3. It's portable and comes with everything you need to feed your baby on the go. It comes with a nipple attachment and covers for the flange and nipple.
4. It is far from taxing on my hands. It requires very little effort to express large quantities of milk rapidly. I can express 4oz from one breast in 4.5 minutes. (Yes I timed it)

In short, since I received this pump I haven't touched my electric pump and likely wont be using it again unless something happens to my Comfort Manual pump. It has replaced my main electric pump. One of the best purchases I've made for my daughter and myself.

Product Title: Philips Avent Manual Comfort Breast Pump

Review Text:

Product Title: Philips Avent Manual Comfort Breast Pump
Author: Liz
Review Text: The Philips Avent Manual Pump was a lifesaver for my first business trip upon returning to work. I traveled for 3 days when my son was 3.5 months old and used my manual pump exclusively - no cords or wires to deal with and my output was great! I was able to carry the pump in my carry on luggage (because it was so small - it also fits great in a purse) and to pump in some very inconvenient locations with ease - a baseball stadium bathroom, a family bathroom at the airport, etc.). I agree with the other reviewers that this pump works nearly as well as my double electric work horse pumps (Spectra S2 and PJ's Comfort), allowing me to pump on each side for 7-8 minutes, for a total of 15 minutes, and to express 4-6 oz depending on the time of day, which matches my double electric pump performance. The pump is comfortable (due to the silicone insert) and I did not experience any hand cramps or other hand issues, even while expressing breast milk 7 to 8 times a day for 3 straight days. At the end of my business trip, I returned home with ~96 oz pumped milk, which will go a long way towards meeting my personal goal of exclusively breastfeeding for one year. I will concede that the pump can become loud/squeaky if the membrane has water in it. Repositioning the membrane often helps in a pinch. I still highly recommend this pump despite this issue.

Product Title: Philips Avent Manual Comfort Breast Pump
Author: Ashley
Review Text:
I'm on my second child and my third manual pump.  I exclusively pumped with my first and used the original style Lansinoh pump (it worked better than my electric at the time), so it got a workout and I spent a ton of time with it! I swapped valves and eventually bought a second one since I loved and used it so much.  Now 6 months into my next baby the valve is giving out and the pump has been discontinued.  I figured I'd try this because it got good reviews and we use the Avent bottles, so yay, I can pump straight into her bottle.  Unfortunately, this is not nearly as nice as my old pump.  It's like they didn't test it with real women.  Here are my issues:

1. The flange is very short, so it has to be held close to the body, which is annoying and hard to do while keeping suction, especially if you're in a fixed position in a car, or wearing a sweater that's bulky.
2. This also means that you can't see the milk flow and your nipple.  It's easy to make adjustments to get more milk out, but when you can't see what's going on, that's not possible.
3. The diaphragm is placed directly over the very short flange neck, so with the way milk can spray and with the diaphragm pulling air up, your milk goes up into the diaphragm.  By the time I have a full bottle the diaphragm is covered in milk.  Annoying to clean and wasteful!  Maybe my milk sprays out more than others, but it still seems illogical to place the opening for the diaphragm directly above this area.
4. Again, with the short neck there's little room for your thumb to go around, so I always end up with a red spot and a sore knuckle.

All in all, it serves it's purpose and the suction is good, but I would have tried a different pump.  I'm disappointed Lansinoh changed their design, but I think I still would have tried the newer model that seems less liked over this Avent had I known there were inherent design flaws.

Product Title: Philips Avent Manual Comfort Breast Pump
Review Title: Not as good as Medela, but fine in a bind
Author: E. Manninger
Review Text:
I have the Avent and the Medela manual hand pumps.  I prefer the Medela, hands down.  I started out with Medela, but had to purchase an Avent pump when I was traveling and in a bind.

I'll compare the two here:

Aesthetics:
Avent wins out.  It's a much sleeker-looking pump, and I like that it's not smothered in colors.  Medela has more of an 80s look to it.

Suction:
Avent's suction is too weak when the soft-fit rubberized shield is in place.  When it's removed, the suction is too strong.  I pumped for 18 months for both of my kids, so I am not sensitive AT ALL in this regard.  In the end, it served its purpose, but each pumping required too many mid-pump comfort adjustments.
Medela has the 2-phase system, which I really liked.  The suction could also be modified based on the speed of pumping.

Cleaning:
Avent has almost twice the parts that Medela has, and is a little more complicated to figure out at first.  But, the parts wash easily enough.  I never tested them in the dishwasher or a steam bag; I washed them by hand.
Medela: The plastic ended up getting a filmy appearance despite my absolute diligence in cleaning with soap AND steam cleaning after every single use.  However, none of the parts warped in dishwasher baskets, and held up very well in Medela's matching microwave steam sanitizing bags.

Bottle Matchup:
Avent: If you use the Avent feeding system, you'll like how the bottles are interchangeable with your pump.
Medela: Medela's pump bottles match up with the Dr. Brown's feeding system (which I used with my first child, switching to Avent for my second).

Other features:
Avent's pump comes with a shield cover, which was nice.  It kept the inside of the pump sanitary while in storage.  Medela's doesn't have one of these.

Bottom line: The Medela pump is a better product.

Review Text:

League as the best one.

Product Title: Philips Avent Manual Comfort Breast Pump

Product Title: Philips Avent Manual Comfort Breast Pump
Author: Roxy
Review Text:
I purchased this manual pump for two reasons: (1) it's compatible with the bottles we use, and (2) I wanted an easy to use pump in case I need to pump in the car or in the middle of the night. I also liked the fact that it had a massage cushion. After reading other reviews I figured I'd give it a try. Unfortunately, I'm not a fan. Although I like the fact that you don't have to lean forward in order to collect your expressed milk, it's about the only thing that I do like.

What I don't like:

- Being that it's a manual pump, it's to be expected that it'll take longer than an electric pump. However despite being able to control the speed it takes 20-25 minutes to pump one side with this manual pump versus 10 minutes with my electric.

- After about 5 minutes my hand gets tired and starts to hurt. The instructions say to switch hands if this happens but then I end up having two sore hands and don't want to pump the other side.

- I can't seem to use the pump without holding it with one hand and pumping with the other. This isn't very convenient.

- I can't use the massage cushion since my boobs are too big. Being this was one of the reasons I wanted this pump, it kind of defeats the purpose.

- It's hard to know when I've emptied my boob since I can't really look down and see if anything is still dripping and then the part where the milk is being pumped ends up foggy up/getting covered with milk.

Overall, this manual pump isn't for me.

Product Title: Lansinoh Signature Pro Double Electric Breast Pump, Portable with LCD Display, 3 Power Options, Includes 25mm Flanges, 2 Baby Bottles with 1 Slow Flow Bottle Nipple, and Carry Bag
Author: OrangeCatKevin
Review Text:
I have never written a review on an item before, but I really felt this product warranted one!  I bought this pump when I was still pregnant with my 2nd child.  I had used the Avent manual pump with my 1st, and I was so disappointed.  I ended up giving up on it very shortly after my daughter was born, and I knew this time around I wanted an electric one.  Only thing was, I didn't want to spend $200-$300.  So I settled on this.

Well, let me tell you, I hadn't "settled" at all!  I can't say enough good things about this breast pump.  Some pros:

1. This pump gives you the option of using one flange or two.  Most often I only do one at a time, but it's nice to know you can do either way.

2. It offers different cycles (speed of "sucking") and vacuum strength (how hard it's "sucking").  To me, this is a wonderful feature because you can find a setting you're comfortable with.

3. You can switch the power source from DC plug to batteries.  This is great if you plan on travelling.

4. The price can't be beat.  You get much more than you pay for - I would consider this pump right up there with the best of the best Medela's - which easily cost you $100 more.  And the going rate to rent a pump around here is $35 a month, so if you plan to pump for more than 4 months, it's worth it to just buy this one!  With a Medela, you'd have to pump for 8 months or more to make it more economical to buy rather than rent.

5. The Lansinoh brand really is good.  They make, in my opinion, one of the best nipple creams around.  It is also fairly easy to find replacement parts and accessories in stores (I've seen them at Walmart and Babies-R-Us).  It is also pretty easy to wash, as the apparatus for each breast is made of only 4 pieces (not including the tubing).

6. This set comes with extra pieces, bottles with caps, and a few sample freezer bags.

Only a couple of cons (but not enough to make it a bad review in any way):

1. It doesn't come with any sort of travel bag.  But everything you'd need to bring with you would fit in an extra purse, or even your diaper bag, so I don't really see the need.

2. It is a bit awkward to pump both breasts at the same time.  It is uncomfortable to hold them as directed with one arm and hand.  I feel like I lose suction on the breast nearest my elbow.  I don't know if this is all double pumps - this is my 1st experience with one - but it really leaves you with no hands free.  And for a mom with an infant, that doesn't really work out!

All in all - I would recommend this breast pump 100%.  You get so much for an amazing price.

Product Title: Lansinoh Signature Pro Double Electric Breast Pump, Portable with LCD Display, 3 Power Options, Includes 25mm Flanges, 2 Baby Bottles with 1 Slow Flow Bottle Nipple, and Carry Bag
Author: OceanDreams
Review Text:
This pump is a lifesaver, even though there are some minor issues to consider.

Pros:
-The Lansinoh electric pump is small and very light, which makes it easy to transport between work and home, if you walk or use public transportation
-It has excellent suction power and automatically transitions between a letdown and expression phase. You can also adjust the settings to accommodate your specific needs. I struggled to get one 3 oz bottle after pumping with the Spectra S1 for 20 minutes. I’ve gotten 5+ oz while pumping with the Lansinoh for 13-15 minutes.
-The Lansinoh is affordable when compared to some pumps that cost more than $200 without insurance. I’m not sure if insurance covers the Lansinoh, though.
-I highly recommend the Lansinoh if you are a beginner when it comes to pumping and you’re not sure which settings will work for your body. The Spectra is pretty manual and you may not know what works best until you try a pump, like the Lansinoh, which demonstrates how much time you need for the letdown and expression phases and how strong the vacuum should be for you.

Cons:
-This pump is loud, while the Spectra is quiet and discreet. If you wanted to pump while on a phone call or while your child is sleeping, the Lansinoh ain’t gonna cut it.
-The Lansinoh doesn’t have a night light, while the Spectra does; therefore, again, it would be difficult to use this pump at night, while your baby is sleeping in the same room.
-The Lansinoh pump parts come apart easily and sometimes while I’m in the middle of pumping. I’ll find milk on my pants occasionally and have to tighten the parts.
-The Spectra S1 has a rechargeable battery, while you have to purchase AA batteries for the Lansinoh, if you want to use it when you don’t have access to an outlet

Despite the cons I mentioned, the Lansinoh is my go-to pump because it allows me to easily pump the 4 oz my baby needs for each of her feedings. I was in tears using the Spectra S1 because my baby’s caregiver (while I’m at work) was suggesting that I might have to supplement with formula because she was screaming after finishing her 3 oz bottles. Overall, this pump has been a lifesaver and I’m grateful I purchased it as a backup pump.

Review Text:
This is the second pump I have used in my time since breastfeeding so this will be comparing my experience with this pump to my experience using the Medela pump. The first thing that drew me to this pump was the price. I received the Medela pump through insurance. I didn't have a positive experience with the Medela- it broke after about 9 months of use. It would still turn on but I'd turn the knob to the highest setting and sometimes it worked, other times it didn't. 1. Reliability: So far, it has not malfunctioned once! Very reliable.
2. Ease of use: I like how there are only a couple of buttons on the screen. One button to turn it on. Then another button to change which type of setting- this basically just means do you want it to pump fast, slow, or somewhere in the middle. There's also a button to increase the intensity of each setting. What I found interesting about this is if you're on the fast setting and you push this button, it doesn't make it go faster it actually prolongs the length of the pull.
3. Size: I love how compact this pump is. It's lightweight and easy to transport. This particular pump came with the black bag which has been good but not the best. Imagine Mary Poppins type of bag. 4. Effectiveness: When I was looking for this pump this is was probably my most important criteria. Was it going to get the job done? The answer is yes! It's efficient. I can get a full bottle in twenty minutes or less, depending on how full my breasts are at the time.

Only con that I would say is that it isn't the easiest to clean. The bottle and pump attachment have quite a few parts so you have to disassemble it before washing. Still not a big deal, as you can wash everything in a dish washer.
