Review Text:
***Editing this now to note that the review was for the original Lansinoh, NOT the Affinity, which I have not used, and which was either not available, or not commonly available in 2008.  It looks like the listing was changed to point to a different product.***

Most of it's been said already, so I'll try to keep this fairly brief.  This is the same as the Ameda Purely Yours, so make sure to check reviews on it as well.

I use this pump about three times a day in an effort to build up a frozen milk stash before returning to work.  While the power adapter is large and heavy, the pump and horns are surprisingly light and small.  The whole thing fits nicely in the diaper bag we were given in the hospital, with room to spare.  The parts that come into contact with milk (horns, rubber valves, silicone membranes) wash up easily with a bottle brush and unscented dish soap, and fit on any standard sized bottle you'd like to use.  I figure that the milk's in the horns only briefly, so BPA contact is minimal, and using third-party bottles lets you avoid contact there.

It's no louder than the Medela swing, which I started with, but it's a double pump, and the horns feel comfier to me.

Just a few hints I haven't seen yet:

-If you cut slits down the front of a sturdy bra, you can insert the horns, and pump hands-free.  If said bra has a lace or fabric overlay, push that back rather than cutting through it, and use it to cover the slits when wearing the bra normally.  There are instructions online on using hair elastics to suspend pumps from a nursing bra, also.

-Alternating between high speed/low suction, and low speed/high suction got the most milk for me.  Just switch when it stops flowing.  It's more comfortable than consistent high speed and/or suction, too.  I love that the pump has separate controls which makes this possible.

-The sample Lansinoh milk bags that came with this pump fit in Playtex drop-in bottles.  Didn't see that noted on the package, but it's good to know.

-If you pump as much as you can, and then feed your baby, he or she will still get enough to eat.  The best pump is no match for an infant, who will be able to get milk the pump couldn't, so if you're trying to increase your supply, this may help.

Review Title: Great pump, but what's with the beeping???
Author: LD
Review Text:
When I first started pumping, I used a hospital grade pump and purchased the Medela parts that went with it (shields and bottles).  When I returned that pump, I needed to purchase my own pump.  After reading the reviews, I decided that this one would be my best bet (and you can't beat the price).

Pros: This pump works just as well as my hospital grade pump did, and you can adjust the speed and suction, which is nice.  It's relatively easy to clean, too.  It's small, so it's easy to find a bag to carry it around in, along with all the extras you'll need if you're planning to pump at work, or anywhere other than at home.  It fits standard-size bottles, which is nice.

Cons: You hear the suction noise with this pump (which isn't bad), but it also beeps along with the suction.  I have NO IDEA why the beeping is necessary, but I find it a little aggravating (especially when I'm pumping at night, or at work).  It's not discreet, that's for sure.  Also, the parts aren't BPA free, so I don't use the bottles.  I actually use the Medela bottles that I purchased for my other pump, because they're a standard size, BPA free, and can be sterilized in the microwave (which is MUCH easier when I'm pumping at work.)  The shields have to be washed by hand, or they can be put in the dishwasher.  It's a little bit harder to find replacement parts for this pump (I've found you generally have to order them from the Lansinoh website--do yourself a favor and figure out which parts you will need duplicates of after you've received the pump--order them all at once because the shipping isn't cheap).

Overall, I'd recommend this pump because it's very effective, and is a great deal.

Author: MM
Review Text:
Some background:
Bought the Lansinoh Double Electric in November 2009.
Used it till January 2010.
Currently using the Medela PISA (since January 2010).

I thought I had done extensive research before buying a breast pump, and a few reviews favorably compared the Lansinoh with the Medela Pump in Style. I remember reading a review that said that the Lansinoh was just a 'little' slower. I used my Lansinoh for about two months, and was pumping till my breasts ran dry. It used to take me over an HOUR to do so (and I did this about 4-5 times a day). Needless to say, I was not particularly happy with the time spent pumping (time when I could have caught up on some sleep considering I began using the Lansinoh about a week after my son was born).

For quite a while I thought I must have very poor milk supply with very slow let down. Hence I continued with my pumping schedule very diligently. However, once I got back to work, it became very difficult trying to find time to pump. I finally caved in a bought the Medela PISA. I was very skeptical on the decision since I didn't want to end up with a more expensive pump but still be stuck pumping so long (since I thought the problem was with my let down). Anyway, I am SO glad I bought the Medela PISA. I was able to completely drain my breasts in 10-15 minutes!!! I have been using the PISA for the last two and a half months, and am so much happier. I am able to continue giving my son breast milk; he is almost six months old now, and I am hoping to pump till he is one--I seriously doubt if I would have been able to pump with the Lansinoh while working.

Also, this is not really such a big deal, but the Lansinoh bottle markings get rubbed off pretty soon. And thats tough  if you use the bottle markings as a guide to measure how much you have pumped (The Medela bottles have not had this problem).

In my opinion, the Lansinoh might be alright if you plan on being an occasional pumper; however if you plan to pump regularly and/or need to pump at work, then the Lansinoh might not be your best bet. While it is much cheaper than the Medela (almost a third of the price), having used the Lansinoh and the Medela, I can confidently say that you get what you pay for! I just wish I hadn't sunk money on the Lansinoh, and had gone with the Medela right from the beginning...

Review Text:

Also, it's lightweight, has very few parts (easy to wash), and is easy to carry.  Because it's so affordable, I'm trying to order a second one for work so I don't have to carry back and forth from home to work.

NOTE:  If you order from AmericaRX (one of Amazon's preferred sellers), beware--they will send you the Lansinoh AFFINITY pump, which is different from the original double electric pump.  The parts of both pumps are not interchangeable.  Because I was ordering a second pump for work and I already own the double electric breast pump, I ended up with two different products, and it is a tough to process a return, even though it's the wrong product.  ("The picture on Amazon is just a representation, Ma'am."  It's AN ENTIRELY DIFFERENT PUMP!)  I'm still in the process of finding out whether I'll have to file a claim with Amazon to get my money back, and then I'm going to hunt for the original pump elsewhere.

Product Title: Lansinoh Manual Breast Pump, Hand Pump with Comfortable Flange, Includes 5oz Baby Bottle with Slow Flow Nipple, Breastfeeding Essentials
Review Title: Suctioned Bottom is nice feature, other brands are better though
Author: BTV
Review Text:
I have this one as well as the older generation NatureBond one. In comparison, I prefer the NatureBond, however this one has some very nice upgrades that are worth mentioning.
If you've never used a haakaa, they are miracle milk collectors that any leaky, breastfeeding mom should have (hence the still decent review despite the cons listed). I used these with both my babies and never had to use the awful hand or electric pump. I would also suggest buying a second haakaa if you like it and leak in between feedings or hate pumping as much as I did.

Pros:
- HANDS FREE! I cannot stress this enough to anyone that has never used one and is still stuck in a tiny, windowless room trying to pump. Pop it on, forget about it, get some stuff done. Put it on the other side while breastfeeding and double your freezer stash.
- The lanyard is actually quite nice. I didn't think I'd really use it, but it's a great hands-free option when you're trying to collect your things (and baby!) and move to a different room. It's also saved me once or twice when the suction came loose and it fell off. I still lost some milk in the fall, but the whole thing didn't dump out since it only fell about 2in. Note: the newer NatureBond model has this upgrade as well.
- the suction cup bottom is an amazing addition! I wish all of the haakaa brands would add this feature. Even if its not suctioned well (see "cons") the base is still wider than other brands and less likely to spill. Pro tip: You can suction the bottom to the included lid for a wider base if you're using it on a soft surface (couch, bed, etc) and can't suction it to anything.

Cons:
- the aforementioned suction bottom doesn't stick forever. I've still dumped it a few times thinking it was suctioned onto a hard surface, only to find the bottom had popped off in a manner of minutes.
- the milk suction power is too strong. It's actually quite painful in comparison to the NatureBond brand that I have. There's a very small suction power window in between "this will pop of in a few seconds when you least expect it" and "I feel like I put my boobs in a vacuum sealer".
- I don't really understand the lid feature on any of the haakaa brands... this one doesn't even fit that well and still leaks. The other brands at least come with a silicone stopper that works much, much better. Therefore, your only protection from accidently dumping your haakaa is the suction bottom that has a tendency to pop off spontaneously from certain surfaces.

TL,DR: The NatureBond brand is better, but the suctioned bottom is a nice feature.
Date: Reviewed in the United States on May 19, 2021

Product Title: Lansinoh Manual Breast Pump, Hand Pump with Comfortable Flange, Includes 5oz Baby Bottle with Slow Flow Nipple, Breastfeeding Essentials
Review Title: Does a better job than an electronic pump, but short-lived
Author: Psychotic Parakeet
Review Text:
UPDATE OCTOBER 2019:

So after nearly four months of using this multiple times a day every day, it pretty much died.  The suction power diminished, and in-turn, so did my milk production because I was not able to get a good volume out before I noticed it was the pump itself going bad.  I switched to a Bellababy manual pump recently, and I am able to get a large volume of milk out now.  While this product helped me in the initial stages of pumping, its longevity was short-lived.  Three stars for it helping me when I needed it the most, but it is definitely not a five star product that could not stand up for long-term pumping.

------------------------
I just had my first baby via c-section a week ago, and I was discharged from the hospital with a one-week rental of a Medela electronic pump that I was using there during recovery.  This hand-held pump supersedes the electric one by far when it comes to comfort and increasing milk output.  I was producing about 30ml with each pumping on mid-level with the electric pump, and I was able to do double that amount with less time using this pump.  I'm on my second day of use with this, and I am able to output 4 ounces (120ml) to satisfy my baby's tremendous appetite.  Not bad as a first-time mom.

You can ease into the suction gradually to avoid flying into the ceiling, which is nice because the electronic pump makes it feel like things are getting sucked into a wind tunnel.  The nice protective purple edges around the suction cups add so much comfort.  The parts to the machine are basic and easy-to-clean, but my only gripe is the pump handle assembly that tends to trap water, so you have to really shake it around to get all the water out.  Otherwise, this is a fantastic product and I am glad it did not make me completely shy away from offering breastmilk like the Medela electric pump did.

Product Title: Lansinoh Manual Breast Pump, Hand Pump with Comfortable Flange, Includes 5oz Baby Bottle with Slow Flow Nipple, Breastfeeding Essentials
Review Title: Very effective and comparable to elvie
Author: Kai
Review Text:
I have used the original elvie pumps, the elvie stride and this manual lansiloh pump. I am very impressed with this pump. I normally pump 6oz in 40minutes (per side) using the elvie or elvie stride. I get the same output using the lansiloh manual pump in 20minutes (per side)

Elvie pumps have a gentle suction that some people (like me) respond to really well. I have 2 kids and so the elvie is useful to pump while doing chores where I can remain upright like cooking, laundry, tidying up etc. However when both kids are awake it is not very practical to have the elvies in because I can't bend down to pick up my infant or perform other tasks that require bending over or leaning back.  I find the lansiloh pump useful during this time because I can easily remove the pump to take care of a task and then return to pumping. Sounds silly but this pump helps me stick to my pumping schedule. Of course pumping hands free with no manual effort (elvie) is ideal but because of the bending/leaning issue I can't use it all the time.

Its also great to have a manual back up pump just in case your electric one decides to stop working randomly.

Pros:
Suction is as strong or as gentle as you want.
The pump is silent.
Easy to put together.
Just as effective as elvie in terms of output.

Cons
Wet duckbill falls off and into the bottle. Make sure the duckbill and the part of the pump where the duckbill will be placed is dry.

You need a straw cleaner to clean the small parts of the flange.

Would definitely recommend.

Review Title: This is a breast milk collector, NOT a pump; PERFECT for catching drips while nursing
Author: Sekhmet
Review Text:
Pretty handy!  Especially for new mothers with leaky breasts.  The title is a tad misleading, as it says "manual breast pump" but this is in fact NOT a breast pump.  This is a collector.

Basically, you use suction to collect the drips on the opposing breast when baby nurses (which would ordinarily otherwise be wasted by being soaked into a breast pad) that comes out with a milk "let down" when feeding your baby.  The suction helps draw the drips out so you collect a bit more than you would if the breast were just sitting there leaking.

Pros:
*It has a very strong suction, and you just squeeze the whole thing to "activate" it
*It's easy to pop it on there right after you put baby on the other side
*it stays put due to suction and I can sort of prop it on baby's leg or hold it, etc.
*I haven't needed the strap but it's handy to have around your neck JIC it were to lose suction, it would just hang off your neck instead of falling and spilling milk all over.
*It's inexpensive
*easy to clean: you pretty much just rinse it after use and let it air dry upside down.  The entire unit is one continuous piece of soft silicone.
*comes with a covering lid so you can keep the inside lint free if it's in a bag, or cover it if milk is in and you're setting it on the counter to come back to later.
*has a suction cup base so you can adhere it to a countertop or other smooth surface so it won't tip over; and there's a little pull tab at the base to release the suction cup easily with no risk of spilling or sloshing the contents.
*easy to remove from breast, and doesn't spill/slosh when doing so.

Cons:
*it takes practice to get the nipple positioned in the center of the suction area (however it seems to work just fine even if my nipple is pressed against the side).
*the suction can pinch a little if it's not on there just right and you may need to pop it off and adjust a few times before it's comfortable.

All in all very handy and well made and SUPER useful for collecting otherwise potentially wasted milk; esp when breasts are leaky in the first few weeks after delivery of baby.  In one sitting, I collect an once or more of milk, simply from drips!  Definitely get one even if you aren't sure you'll need it.  It's cost efficient enough to be worth trying if you plan to bottle feed breast milk, or have a freezer stash.

Review Text:

This may seem like a "duh" scenario but coming from sitting at the kitchen table to set up the electric pump and sit there on let-down for 6min before giving up or manually expressing into the flange/bottle with a warm compress.. the Lansinoh being this easy to use was kind of crazy. Cleaning instructions say parts are dishwasher safe too- whereas the "fancier" one says to boil every day- exhausting to try and deal with when you're a new (and in my case first time) mom.

Review Text:

Review Title: It works but it has its glitches
Author: Marie Grace Alban
Review Text:
I though getting these two options was the best to have but there are so many issues. Below are my pros and cons.
Pros: the package arrives with the flange option and the hands free cup option.
Cons:
1) The charger is extremely bulky and does not fit in a regular pocket size. I have to wear pajama pants to make it fit and it is heavy that my pants fall off. The charger doesn’t last long, I have to pump for like 25-30 min because I have a low supply so I have to constantly charge it after two maybe three sessions.
2) The flange option only comes in 24mm, I had to buy the extra 27mm size and pay extra for those parts.
3) The cups have the same story, only 24mm arrives with the package and I had to buy the 27mm. Also, it is so specific that if you don’t attach the parts perfectly, the cups do not work. I have spent a lot of time disassembling and assembling it before starting my pump session that gets so frustrating.

Overall, the product is okay, it pumps and it works but it has so many issues it is frustrating to use and most of all having a newborn, I should not have to deal with getting extra parts, charging issues and cups not working.
I’m already past the return date so I have to use it but my son is just one month old and I think I’m going to get another brand because I can’t keep pumping with this product, otherwise I’m going to loose my mind.

Review Text:

For starters, this pump is super easy to clean. Only three parts that are easy to take apart and put back together. It also comes with a 21mm flange, which doesn’t seem to be a common size amongst portable pumps.
The stimulation and flow settings are vast enough for the comfort of your choosing, and gives you a powerful 30 minute pump, equivalent to my hospital grade plug-in pump. I am able to pump my normal 6-9oz a session, without needing an additional session or repositioning.
Some tips for usage: make sure you wear a tight enough bra. You may also want to invest in lanyard for full portability. (I have worn a hoodie over the pumps and put the battery/vacuum in the front pocket)
Overall, great pump and I am extremely happy with this purchase!

Author: McKenna
Review Text:
**UPDATED SECTION AT END**
This pump is absolutely amazing and I love it! I've really relied on this pump as I have been unable to breastfeed my baby like I wanted to. I don't want to feed her formula, I'd rather her be getting breast milk, but because I have flat nipples it has been a struggle to get her to latch properly.

It is super portable and everything you might need to feed your baby fits in the provided backpack. I keep all the pump parts in there, as well as extra bottles, extra nursing pads, and my baby's vitamin supplements.

This pump the super intuitive to use, and the suction power is enough to mimic the stimulation you need to keep producing. In just 20 mins of pumping I can get a good 10 oz from both breasts combined.

All the pieces disassemble for easy cleaning, although there is one small space that is somewhat difficult to clean out.
I'm pleased with the battery life on this thing. I can get 5 or so pumping sessions out of it before it starts to die, and that lasts me a whole day.

**UPDATE**
After 6 months of consistent, daily use (as I was fully reliant on this pump to get milk for my baby), the pump practically died. It started by having a shorter and shorter battery life, and it eventually got to the point where I had to have it plugged in to make it through a pumping session. Eventually it became so dysfunctional that it would pulse two or three times and then die, even while plugged in. Maybe it was just a malfunction with the one I received, but it made everything that much more frustrating and stressful.

So if you need to fully rely on pumping to get your baby that amazing breast milk, I don't know if I can recommend this as your daily pump. It's good for on the go and supplemental pumps, but you might need something a little more heavy duty for constant use.

Product Title: Medela Breast Pump | Swing Maxi Double Electric | Portable Breast Pump | USB-C Rechargeable | Bluetooth | Closed System | with Carry Bag
Review Title: Pump works well! No plugged ducts yet!
Author: Amazon Customer
Review Text:
I was given this pump as part of a Friends and Family Program with Medela by a friend of mine who works for the company. In return, I am to provide an honest review of the product.
With my first child I had a different brand of pump and I had plugged ducts ALL THE TIME and mastitis twice. I produce A LOT of extra milk so it was hard to get it all out. So I was excited to try this pump since they stated that you could extract more milk with the pump + the Medela name, I figured it would be a good one to try. I have not had a plugged duct yet and feel like my breasts are draining well.
This pump works FAST! I can pump 14 ounces total in 10 minutes and feel like my breasts are drained completely. It's quiet, which is always a huge plus, it's super portable - the small pump has a loop on it that you can easily put a lancet on and hook it on you and get chores done while you pump.
The only thing worse than cleaning a juicer is cleaning a breast pump 5 billion times a day. But as far as pumps go, this one is easy to clean, no hidden nooks and crannies to get into. So that's nice.
The one draw back is that the tubing did get water in it. I think because the pump wasn't 100% dry when I put it back together and had to use it again. This was a bummer as it says in the literature that the tubing will stay dry. Pump number 2 and the tubing had water in it. So I will have to replace that as to avoid mold in the tubing. Overall, I am super happy with this pump and will continue to use it for the duration of my time breastfeeding my second child, which I plan to do for 2 years.

Product Title: Medela Breast Pump | Swing Maxi Double Electric | Portable Breast Pump | USB-C Rechargeable | Bluetooth | Closed System | with Carry Bag
Author: Erin
Review Text:
I received the pump from Medela at no charge in order to try it and provide an honest review. Initially I expected a lot from this pump, it's #4 in my pumping journey.

Initially I had issues with it, because it didn't look like it fit together -- but an email to support helped me figure out my issues. The pieces looked like they were supposed to fit flush together, but didn't. After talking to support, I understood that as long as there was suction it would be fine.

As far as this pump goes, it is great for travel. The suction is effective and the bag makes the pump very easy to tote around. The flanges come in 21mm and 24mm which was great to help me figure out what size i needed (all my other pumps had 25mm and 28mm options). I really appreciated the rubber edges to the flanges, too, as they made the pump more comfortable to hold against my breasts. I have used this on road trips and the size and portability have made pumping in the car so easy. It was also quiet.

My biggest complaint is that if you don't have the Medela family app, you cannot check on how the battery level is. If you're at home that isn't an issue, but on the road it can be harder to keep track of. Another point against it is that if you press a button while pumping, to change the suction for example, it restarts the 30-minute countdown to shutoff.

Overall, though, this is a good pump. Very easy to clean and use, even without the app.
Date: Reviewed in the United States on November 5, 2021

Product Title: Medela Breast Pump | Swing Maxi Double Electric | Portable Breast Pump | USB-C Rechargeable | Bluetooth | Closed System | with Carry Bag
Review Title: Perfect for Mom’s On the Go - Lifestyle Change
Author: Paolo Latrofa
Review Text:
I absolutely love the new Maxi Swing portable pump. I have 3 children and have breastfed/pumped with all of them. As a busy mom, I am always on the go, go, go. This pump was life changing.

I am able to plug it in during car rides and pump while I drive since it is hands free. Once I get to my destination, I just pour the milk into a bottle and I am ready to feed the baby.

Around the house, I use a Fanny pack and place the pump in it so that I can do laundry, wash dishes, change diapers and even eat meals while pumping. It’s working out great.

I only wish that Medela provided a Fanny pack for the pump that fit it perfectly. They do provide you with a backpack, but you can’t wear the backpack while pumping.

The backpack is very sleek, lightweight, small and portable. It is very cute and stylish. I love how the side pocket opens and has the cooler. That is a very cool feature. There are also stands that hold the pumped milk so that they don’t fall over and spill.

This would be my favorite backpack/carrying case and pump out of all 3 Medela pumps that I have used over the years!

As far as battery life, it gives about 10 hours I would say before it needs to be charged again. I can charge it at home or in the car.

As for suction, it does a really good job on my right side, but does not do the best job on my left.  In the beginning, I wondered if it was even working on the left side. My right side will get 4-5 oz and the left side 1-2. This can also be normal as the baby nurses mainly on my dominant right side.

Overall, I give this pump a 10/10. I highly recommend for busy moms. Anything to make life a little bit easier. And not having to be tied down to a machine is wonderful.

Author: Stacy N.
Review Text:
I love these as much as one can love a breast pump. Pumping is probably the bane of my existence, but here we are. So here it is:

So about what I do like:
1. How these have their own little pump. It’s perfect for an over supplier that almost only needs one breast per feeding. So this works great to empty out the other side too.
2. Super easy to just pop on and go.
3. Easy to assemble, once you get the hang of it. But you have to make sure everything clicks into place.
4. I generally find pumping to be super uncomfortable, but this one isn’t terrible. I just have to start slow and low on stimulation mode, then work my way up to the mixed mode, then I finally end on level 5-6 in expression mode.
5. I used the Elvie Stride with my first baby and it was difficult to put together, the parts warped in a sterilizer machine and it was 100% hard plastic. It HURT. This one is softer silicone and way more comfortable, and no hard plastic.

What I don’t like:
1. As an oversupplier, each breast will easily put out more than the 6oz capacity, so the reservoir is not enough for me.
2. Speaking of capacity, you can get to 6.5oz before it just stops allowing more milk to go into the reservoir and you end up with it all over you. And the measurement notches are impossible to see while you are wearing the pump, so you kinda have to guess.
3. There are 5 parts, (6 if you need a flange size other than 24mm).
4. It is a bizarre feeling when the pumps are on and aren’t synced up, and it’s difficult to get them synced.
5. Definitely don’t bend over to any side with these on, it will leak out of the top.

All in all, for my use, it’s perfect (except that I wish it had a larger capacity). I have the V1 pro that I will take to work once I go back, which addresses some of my “don’t likes” but it has tubes and an external pump. These will continue to be the ones I use during breastfeeding sessions, and the V1 Pro is my go to when I need to empty both breasts through pumping.

P.S. Both Momcozy pumps I have do a waaaayyyy better job at emptying me out than my Elvie Stride ever did. It now takes 15-25 minutes vs 45 minutes.
P.P.S. Whatever pump you use, be sure to use pump spray to moisturize and make pumping waaay more comfortable.

Update 4/5/25: I think the leak was because I didn’t put the pump together properly? Because I have since pumped more than 6.5 oz with no leaks. I think the highest at one time is 7.25 oz.

Product Title: Momcozy Breast Pump Hands Free M5, Wearable Breast Pump of Baby Mouth Double-Sealed Flange with 3 Modes & 9 Levels, Electric Breast Pump Portable - 24mm, 2 Pack Mint
Author: Kate
Review Text:
I LOVE my M5! It’s the only portable pump I have tried but it works really well. It’s not as good as my spectra wall-plug pump, but I don’t think any portable pump is going to be as good as a heavy duty pump.

I will say I had a little bit of a harder time finding the right size and since you can’t see where your nipple is going once it’s on it’s hard to tell if it’s properly aligned. It took a bit of trial and error figuring out the right placement and I still will frequently need to readjust to get it right. It doesn’t hurt while pumping, and shouldn’t. However, if I use the M5 several sessions in a row, my nipples will eventually start getting sore by the end of the day whereas with my spectre I don’t have that issue.

As far as the convenience and easy of use goes- 10/10. I’ve never had a spilling issue while wearing it. Except one occasion where I had to suddenly bend over to stop the dog from getting into something, and it only spilled because I inverted the pumps for a moment. If you stay more or less upright you can move around and do every day tasks with no issues. You don’t have to be too careful or pay too close attention other than not completely bending forward.

They’re not too loud while pumping and sound a little bit like a soothing bullfrog croaking. If I’m in a completely silent room or with just a couple people conversing you can definitely hear them. If the tv is on, music is playing, or there’s several people in the room talking, then it’s barely noticeable. I have larger boobs already, but the pumps are very discreet, they just make your boobs look even bigger. I am very comfortable using these in public.

The battery will last me several pumping sessions. They will run for 30 minutes before shutting off automatically and you have several different options for suction power and modes. I can only stand a level 2-4 suction on these whereas with my spectra I can typically go much higher. I don’t know if they just measure strength differently or if I am more sensitive with the M5 because of the nipple alignment issue.

When I compare milk output with the M5 vs the standard spectre wall plug in pump, I don’t notice a big difference. I’ll usually use a combination of both throughout the day since the spectre doesn’t hurt my nipples as much, but it’s so much more convenient to be able to get up and walk around while pumping.

After reading a bunch of reviews comparing the M5 and different portable pumps, this one definitely seemed like the best option for a decent price point. I still stand by my choice! If someone were to gift me a different portable pump I would try it, but I wouldn’t go buy a pump other than this one on my own!

Product Title: Motif Medical Luna Double Electric Pump for Breastfeeding - Portable - Hospital Grade Pump w/LED Light - Hands-Free Breast Pump, Quiet Motor Baby Breast Pump
Author: Mishele
Review Text:
I wanted to try a new pump after good experiences with spectra in the past: this pump is compatible with spectra parts so it wasn’t too risky of a change.
Good: The pump is strong; I don’t need that much suction, but if you do this is a solid choice.  The profile is also slim, which makes it easier to travel with or take to work. I also like how many sizes they have available for flanges so you don’t need to go look for custom sizes on your own if 24 mm isn’t for you.
Bad: The parts are crap. My backflow protectors didn’t work right out of the box, so I immediately had to replace those with some extra spectra pieces right off the bat. My worst experience has been with the duckbill valves. I ordered a set and one arrived with a gap—the exact type of gap you’d see after hours of pump usage, and a sign the valve needed replacing soon. I reached out to the company and they said it was fine like that. After several exchanges with customer service, it was clear they wouldn’t replace the defective valve or refund my money. Eventually I had to use it and sure enough, I pumped over an ounce less on that side— it really is defective, as it appears. So as much as I want to support a company that isn’t Medela or Spectra, the parts are too low quality and the customer service too disingenuous to give my money to. I will say that if you get the non-duckbill valves, they are great; they are easier to remove for cleaning, and seem to be more durable as a result. But if you order replacements, you’re more likely to get the junk duckbills because it seems like that’s what motif is transitioning to. If you go with this pump, save yourself some heartache and buy replacement pieces from third parties on Amazon or spectra.
Date: Reviewed in the United States on January 17, 2023

So I've been an exclusively pumping mom for both of my boys for medical reasons so I know how hard it is to decide on the right pump.

With my first son, I had the medela freestyle pump. I loved its portability but that's it. It hurt so much to pump and I loathed every second of it. I realize now, I had too big of shields so I sized down this time to have a portable option and it's still super painful.

The motif luna I received was a lemon. I called customer service and they got me a new one and it arrived within two days. They were amazing to deal with! Anyway, the pump is rather large to what I was thinking it would be for a portable. But I just put it into a smaller purse to carry it around. The pump is nice. I've seen people say they get more milk in less time. I don't think that's true in my case. My spectra is amazing at getting milk out. But this pump is comfortable, especially if you have more sensitive breasts. The suction on the highest setting isn't quite as powerful as my spectra but it does the job well. I also love that I can use my spectra parts!

Author: Tookzac
Review Text:
PSA, I didn't buy my pump through Amazon I got it through my insurance for free, but I always look at reviews on Amazon prior to purchasing something even if it isn't from Amazon, so I wanted to share my thoughts on this pump.

1. I have used the hospital supplied Medela pump, Spectra S2 and this pump.

2. I love my Spectra S2 pump but it's bulky and not super portable.

3. I had read several reviews on this pump, here on Amazon and through blogs, and there were so many mixed reviews.  I'm glad I got this pump, it's been fantastic now that I know my settings and how to use it.

4. If you are using the supplied valves, don't they suck!  Purchase new ones and purchase Spectra ones, you will notice an improvement in your suction.

5. I read some reviews that the suction isn't good on this pump.  I believe they have done vast improvements to the suction.  I ended up getting a used one from ebay as well to leave at work, on the back it says in was manufactured in 2019 and I notice the suction is not as good as the new one I got through insurance that was manufactured in 2021.

6. I love the memory function on this pump!  Once you figure out what levels of massage and suction work for you program the memory it will save you so much time!  I started with the suggested settings in the manual and they worked perfectly for me.

Review Title: This is my “primary” pump and I love it!!
Author: Geneva Martin
Review Text:
Sharing my breast pump journey and reviews to hopefully help a few people 🤗

I’ve tried the Willow, Elvies, Spectra S1, and Motif Duo. I’ve also used the Avent manual pump, Medela manual pump, Haaka, haaka breast shields and medela breast shields.

Tl;dr: I’m keeping the Motif Duo as my primary pump, and using the elvies for my mid day pumps and any time I leave the house. The Willow was painful and problematic , and the S1 was great but huge. I swear by my Haaka for establishing a supply, and the medela shields for when my nipples are sore. The haaka shields were uncomfortable and didn’t do anything for me.

Pictured is the Motif duo with the Maymom S1 kt

The haaka is the best thing for increasing supply while nursing no matter what pumps you’re using! I wore this on the opposite breast for every feed over several weeks until I had enough oversupply to start freezing. It was a huge relief when I was engorged and starting to get backed up and way better at relieving my clogged ducts than any other pump. My biggest word of advice is to keep an empty bottle next to you while you’re using it and pour off every half ounce you express so if it falls off or gets kicked by baby, you’re not drenched and don’t lose much. Plus while you’re establishing your supply, you’ll have a bottle ready to go if baby is still hungry after nursing!

The Spectra S1 and Motif Duo are almost exactly the same pump! They both have a “vibration” feel to the pump which helps get more output in a shorter time than the elvie. The huge advantage of the motif is the size! The S1 is almost the size of a bowling ball, and the Motif is the size of a walkie talkie. They both have different suction settings and you can switch between expression and massage mode for different speeds. The S1 has one more speed adjustment, but it’s only available in expression mode and didn’t make the size worthwhile for me. Both use the same tubing as almost every other pump on the market, so if you prefer the spectra or medela valves and flanges you can easily swap them out. I usually throw the motif in my sling while baby wearing, and I ordered a Fanny pack to carry it if and when he ever lets me set him down!

The Elvies were a huge improvement on the Willow. I’ve pumped at Target, the car dealership, Costco, and the post office! They’re the quietest electric pump I’ve used, and actually as quiet as the manual ones. The suction power has a better range, so “low” is actually low but high is still pretty high. They’re lighter and smaller, so my bra holds them pretty well (although be sure you have a good fitting bra!), and I can pick up baby while wearing them. Pausing a session to feed is easier with the elvie than any other pump which happens a lot with a newborn! The bottom is flat so it sits nicely on a table when you’re putting your breasts away or taking the pump apart. The parts can be easily cleaned in a microwave sterilizer and assembly is really fast! They’ll charge with a USB charger and I now keep a reusable USB battery in my bag for it. The only reason I have another pump is because it takes longer to fully express with these (about 30-60 minutes vs 15-20), but they do eventually drain me and they’re less hands-on than the spectra or the motif duo. They do have issues leaking from the button area. You need to stay fully upright and can’t lean forward for any reason or you’ll get milk all over your shirt. If they leak, you need to remove the button mechanism and clean it up, otherwise milk will dry in there and cause more issues with leaks. A lot of people recommend the “plastic bag trick” to help with this. I wear a breast pad between the button and my shirt and it catches the small leaks really well. I’ve had a couple sessions where I had suction issues, but it was always an assembly error and easy to resolve. One issue was the membrane was wet, and I resolved it with a paper towel. Another was the valve was deteriorating, and removing it from my rotation fixed it (on all pumps they have a lifespan of 1-3 months). Another time I simply had my bra in the way and didn’t realize it at first! I’ve had just as many issues with the spectra and motif, but I could never use those in a public place!

The Willow: This was my must have registry item. I was so excited about it and really wanted it to work! I even ordered a second set of flex tubes and the reusable containers because I was fully committed to it. The lowest suction level was way too intense for me. I checked my flanges and tried a different size, and still had raw, bloody nipples and ended up covered in blebs. I got a bad case of clogged ducts as well, but learned about the haaka before it became mastitis. The reusable containers had issues about 1/4 of the time, where the hub was giving me error messages but my husband and I tried checking all the gaskets and walked through assembly without resolution. I reached out to customer service but the process was slow. They said the containers should be replaced, but it was faster to order another set from Amazon (when you’re a nursing mom time is critical and I don’t have three days for them to decide to help me!) The new set was having the same issues, and again we tried multiple times to eliminate human error as the cause. The bags worked reliably, but as I’m pumping 4-5x a day right now, I just can’t justify spending $1 per session! They were also filling with more air than milk, so I couldn’t even try to use one bag on both breasts to conserve resources. They are also huge! I couldn’t it into most of my shirts with them on because they stuck out so much like giant robotitties, and they were so heavy my bra struggled to hold them in. Their shape makes it hard to set down if you need to for a second because it would try to end the session too early and then leak everywhere. They have a setting called “flip to finish” where you rotate the pump at the end of your session to catch the leaks, but half the time it would leave 1/4oz in the flex tubes that you couldn’t see, and then it would run everywhere when you tried putting things away.  I couldn’t hold my baby while wearing both of them at all, and when I tried one would get bumped and try relatching painfully to the side of my breast. Additionally, the flanges use magnets to set alignment, so they can only be sterilized in boiling water, not the microwave. That’s a relatively minor inconvenience if you’re not sterilizing things constantly, but it’s not an issue at all with the other pumps and was just added incentive to return them (which, thankfully Amazon helped me out with, given the failures of the reusable containers and the concerns to my health)

Review Text: I got mine through Aeroflow not Amazon, but I hope to help others with my review. First of all, yes it is small & portable. I have to have extra tubing to make it longer for me because I use the Freemie Next Generation collection cups with this pump as I do not have time to sit around with my shirt open & dangling bottles or storage bags showing. I absolutely require hands free & discreet so a pumping bra wouldn’t have been enough for me. It’s very easy to fit in some of the pockets of my clothing, otherwise I wear my tote bag & just slip it in the bag while I am pumping. The suction is great most of the time. The con? Battery life is only 2.5 hours which isn’t sufficient enough for my busy lifestyle anyway. However I do not even get that! After only 10 minutes of pumping I have two bars left. After 45 which means restarting my pump after the auto shutoff at 30 minutes I have one bar left. That’s not 2.5 hours of use. I have 3 hours of travel to the children’s hospital for specialists for my special needs children multiple times a year. I would have to stick my pump back on the charger every time I am done with it to keep it sufficiently charged. Thankfully I don’t do the driving on the trips to the hospital, but it’s still highly inconvenient. I might as well carry my Medela Harmony manual as a backup when the battery craps out or buy a second portable electric pump as a backup for when one needs to charge. Just too much money to invest. If you’re looking for a pump that is discreet, portable, has a decent battery life & you don’t have to spend all this extra money on collection cups & pumping bras & all these extras to make it “more discreet” I suggest the Willow pump. They are rechargeable, but the motor & all is in the pump so the whole thing hides in your bra. The up side compared to using Freemie cups or a pumping bra with the flanges is you can bend over & lay down with the Willow. Using the Duo with Freemie cups or flanges & pumping bra you STILL need to sit upright or you will be covered in a milky mess. The con to the Willow is it is a $500 pump. The pro to it being that much is all the money you will have spent on the Duo plus all the accessories to make using it more convenient & discreet you could have easily bought the Willow with that cost. I suggest saving your money & making a better investment, but don’t ditch your Medela hand pump. It’s a great backup either way.

Review Text:
I don’t like to write long reviews but I want to be thorough.
I have a two month old (my second child)that I exclusively breastfeed. As with my first, I work at an office and have to pump during the day. With my first, I used the medela pump in style advance (PISA) and was very successful in exclusively breast feeding for 11 months until my daughter decided to no longer latch. I have used the same pump this time (for 7 weeks) therefore my comparison is related to that pump as  I have not used any other pump. I thought about getting the medela freestyle but since it is significantly more expensive I decided to try this pump instead (after researching its features and watching a couple of you tube reviews)

Lightweight and compact- The difference is huge! It weights a little more than a pound and it’s so compact that it fits within my itsy ritzy wet bag (medium) including the tubing, flanges and bottles with plenty of extra space (although the pump does include a tote bag). It also fit within the compartments of my itsy ritzy diaper bag and It does not feel heavy at all.  It can easily fit on your purse and avoid the extra bag.

Performance- With the PISA I can set it in a lower setting (barely moving the dial after the stimulation  setting) and I am able to extract at least 3 ounces up to 5 ounces per session. When I used this, I got worried since it does not feel as powerful as the Medela. I played with the strengths and extracted the same amount of milk using the higher settings (7 to 10 which is the max strength). It was really comfortable and even at the highest levels the noise and vibration was less noticeable than the PISA.  It also has 3 frequencies for extraction meaning that you may be at a 7 strength but the “suckling” frequency can be faster or Slower. In a 30 minute session, and experimenting with the strength and frequency  I had 2 let downs and pumped 4 ounces on each breast (comparable to PISA). That being said, I am not sure that it may work efficiently for someone that has to use the higher settings on their PISA.

Battery- it has a rechargeable integrated battery and that is a super convenient plus for me as I can be brain scattered and would probably forget to bring additional batteries Also I can charge it at whatever point and know I have a full charge again. It is worth mentioning that you can use the pump while charging therefore even if you had used all its battery as long as you are plugged you can pump. I am yet to test the 2.5hour battery life but a 30 minutes session reduces one of the four bars on the battery display, therefore I would assume  a 2hr life to be on the safe side.

Auto shut off after 30 Minutes- It helps save battery life as I tend to get distracted and could easily leave the pump turned on and drain its battery.

Other perks-
LCD screen- does make a ton of difference specially when extracting at night.
Memory- It has a memory feature that allows you to set a customized sequence based on your session preference ( this helps a lot when you are time constrained  pumping at work).
Timer- The timer is a really well though idea and eliminates the need of separate tracking and organizing.
Variety of sizes-  It also includes 3 sizes (21 mm/24mm/27mm) for you to determine the best flange based on nipple size.

My only con at this moment is that the system uses wider parts and bottles than the medela and since the company is relatively new , there isn’t a large array of options for buying  replacement parts.

That being said I really like the product , would definitely recommend it and am glad to have chosen this pump. If you have low supply or require a higher setting on your pump it may not be as efficient as it is for me.

Product Title: Tommee Tippee Made for Me Double Electric Breast Pump, USB Rechargeable | Quiet, Portable, Lightweight
Author: Celena Motes
Review Text:
I found this pump for a good deal at TGMaxx and was very excited to try it out.
It’s drained me faster then any pump I’ve ever used, and the flow settings are very unique. It’s also small and pretty quiet, so pretty portable when charged.
But, there’s a lot of issues too.
The pump has a million parts that are hard to take apart and reassemble, and the worst to clean. They also take forever to air dry, Because all the crevices.
I use a size 19 flange on my spectra pump, this one works for me but I don’t believe one size fits all and feel like larger nipples would definitely have issues.
It’s a very cloudy type of plastic that makes up the pump flange, so it’s impossible to see if you’re still producing/ actually empty. I exclusively pump, so it’s important to me to pump until empty to keep my supply up, but it’s hard to tell when I’m actually finished.
The burgundy cap melted in the dishwasher, top rack, the second time I washed it. I definitely would say only hand wash this pump. I will say, customer service was great- I wrote them in their chat on their website about getting a replacement cap, they did not have it in stock so they sent me a single pump to use the cap off of.
Not having different flange sizes or a way to purchase replacement parts is definitely a bummer. Like they rushed the launch without launching the parts that will eventually need to be replaced. (It did come with two sets of duckbills atleast).
Overall I am keeping the pump, but it’s definitely not a primary pump. I plan on using it as a backup or as a “my husbands family is in town and I need to hide to pump but don’t have a outlet spot to hide in” pump.

Review Title: Very "tippy", wish I had bought a different pump.
Author: Katalina Pfeil
Review Text:
I encountered many problems:
1. First pump quit working after 2 days of use (very stressful with a newborn); new one got here quickly and had to send back original. (Keep your packaging just in case...)
2. Plastic is cloudy color so you can't easily check for positioning or flow.
3. Design makes it tip over ALL. THE. TIME. And the silicone is a hair magnet!
4. Poor seal from pump to bottle, will spill milk if it tips over.
5. Purple top (where suction hose attaches) pops off ALL. THE. TIME. It barely screws on, so any gentle touch and it'll pop off.
6. Pump controls are on touch screen; time/pump power display lights up, but the controls don't! In other words, you will be blindly pressing around the display at night to guess where the controls are.
7. Invisible pump controls will make you hit them all the time, especially when trying to transport. Every time I pick it up to move, I happen to unintentionally turn it on.
8. Only comes with 2 bottles, so expect to be holding at least one cold bottle to your legs while pumping.... and don't lose one!
9. Other Tippee bottles have different threads and do not fit the pump.... I have the 9 oz glass bottles, they are a very poor fit to the pump and lids are not transferable between bottle types.
10. Pump is small enough to fit in diaper bag, but definitely not your pocket... and forget about the pump handsets... just count on bringing another bag along to transport your pump setup.

Product Title: Tommee Tippee Made for Me Single Manual Breast Pump | Soft, Cushioned Silicone Cup | Reduced Hand Strain
Review Title: Too much effort needed to use and clean
Author: BBP
Review Text:
My wife didn't like this Tommee Tippee breast pump. Being parents to twin newborns and a 3 year old in the middle of a pandemic, we need all the help we can get. We're trying out different baby products to see what works best for us and is the most efficient in terms of time and or effort. She pumps and I (dad) help bottle feed. While it is convenient to pump directly into a bottle, that does not make up for some severe shortcomings.

Her first complaint is that the pump stroke is very short. The pump does not suck in the breast deeply enough. so many strokes are needed. Comparing the drive shaft of the TT to a MAM pump, I see that the TT is about half as tall, This translates directly to increased effort on the part of the user.  Secondly, the pump has numerous parts to clean, but that comes with the territory -- other manual pumps are equally so. As for the odd bottle shape, yes, the indentations do make the bottle easier and more comfortable to hold versus a traditional round bottle. But, it comes with an unacceptable cost. Notice that the shoulder of the bottle bulges out like a donut and the area has no taper to the neck. When cleaning, this area traps in liquids, requiring extra shaking to remove residual soap and water. Every other bottle I've used for food or babies has a curvature for this very reason -- to avoiding trapped materials.

I do like that the nipple is ridged for better latching by baby. Some of our bottles are completely smooth at the tip and they often slip in baby's mouth as he tries to get a good latch going. However, it's just too much effort overall to use this product. She's sticking to the Haaka manual breast pump and traditional cylindrical bottles.

This is the third or fourth Tommee Tippee product we've tried and all of them have been disappointing, including a bottle warmer and a Haakaa imitation. The brand has not worked well for us and I feel like the people designing their products aren't parents.

Product Title: Tommee Tippee Made for Me Single Manual Breast Pump | Soft, Cushioned Silicone Cup | Reduced Hand Strain
Author: Jessica
Review Text:
I was hoping I’d like this pump over my old clunky manual pump but sadly that’s not the case

This pump is easy to put together. It’s also easy enough to wash.

Using the pump hurt my hands. It wasn’t nearly as ergonomic as it looks or claims. By the time i finished pumping both sides, my palms we’re sore and cramping. It also feels like it unscrews a bit then longer you pump, causing you to have to stop and retighten the bottle.

I hate that the plastic isn’t clear enough to see proper nipple placement. If any part of your nipple touches the side, it can drastically impede milk flow (and comfort) and this isn’t always something you can obviously feel. I’ve never had a breast pump that wasn’t clear in this regard. It’s not fun making it a guessing game.

The shape of the system is also frustrating. It’s shaped in a way that makes it so you have to lean forward to create a good seal and allow the milk to drop into the bottle. If you sit up straight or try to lean back, it becomes awkward to hold on yourself and some of that precious milk can leak out if you aren’t vigilant on the seal

The suction isn’t too powerful either. I was able to get about 2 ounces after a long pump session and I could feel that I have a lot more to give.

Overall this pump is better than nothing. It’ll relieve pressure and it is possible to get a bottles worth out, obviously the better your milk supply, the easier this will be. It’s too bad that the design makes it awkward and inconvenient.

Pros
-easy to clean
-easy to put together
-quiet

Cons
-hard to see how nipple fits
-pumping causes hand pain quickly
-not great suction
-awkward shape requiring a lean forward to use

The expense is crazy! Not only are the reusable milk containers sold separately, you’re supposed to replace them every 3 months, along with the flex tubes. And the bags are crazy expensive too.

Author: Mina
Review Text:
First of all I want to say that the idea of this technology is what drew me to purchase these pumps. I liked the idea of being able to walk around and take care of things while pumping.

Pros
Wireless, tubeless, portable, not being tethered to an outlet was the best feature it has to offer.
Strong suction, but it's a different kind of latch than most other brands.
That said, the cons outweighed the pros

Cons
App SUCKS
They are extremely loud. I wouldn't want to work in an office and expect to be able to pump discretely.
Customer service people are nice but their process is a bit annoying to navigate to get some help.
The pumps profile/silhouette are ridiculously huge. I'm Talking Dolly Parton huge lol
The output is lacking, my breasts never feel emptied after a session.
I don't like that you cannot control the different modes (they have 2: stimulation and expression) you have to wait for the pumps to determine that you've pumped enough milk (0.5oz) before it enters into stimulation mode. Even then, the mechanism for measuring your output isn't always accurate which means sometimes you get stuck in stimulation mode for 20 minutes!! Which also means you don't have access to any level higher than 3 (there are 9 levels). On the flip side, sometimes it will say you've pumped 4 oz and need to empty your container or replace your bag when there's only an ounce in the darn thing. So needless to say, my frustration only grew when dealing with these pumps.

The battery life could be better, they don't seem to last as long as you'd like and it only comes with 1 charger which is less than ideal if you have to wait to charge the other pump before a session. You also cannot use the pumps while they charge.

For as much money you spend on these, you'd expect better support from the company, better app and for it to actually do a decent job of emptying your breasts.

You have to replace certain parts on a monthly basis ($$$)
This product and company seems like nothing more than a revolving door of money spent.

I know it works for some mamas but the sad news is it just simply ain't working out for me. Now I'm stuck with a pair of $500 worth of equipment that is just useless and taking up space.

The juice ain't worth the squeeze. Especially if you're battling a low milk supply and your goal is to improve it by pumping more frequently.

I get a better output of milk with my Madela Hands free and the Madela pump in style. I do hope to find a truly hands free pump that will get the job done.

Product Title: Willow 3.0 Wearable Breast Pump, Double Electric Breast Pump, Cordless, Hands Free Breast Pump with 9 Levels of Smart, Hospital Grade Suction Strength, 100% Leak Proof & Fits Fully In Bra, 24mm Flange
Author: Grace K.
Review Text:
I really want to love the Willow 3.0 pump, but I have mixed feelings about it.

Bottom line, TLDR:
Pros:
- Hands-wireless pumping offers freedom to do other things while pumping, e.g. bottle feeding baby, changing baby, laundry etc.
- Strong/different suction that could help with clogged ducts in some instances

Cons:
- the pump itself is expensive, and all the extra pump parts are also expensive
- Pump parts not easy to maintain
- Not practical for exclusive pumping
- Not practical for pumping larger amounts each session unless you have multiple sets of pump parts
- Not practical for using in car or outside of home

Long story:
I am exclusively pumping since my baby’s birth (14 weeks old at the time of this review), starting with 8 pumps per day (ppd) and have gone down to 7 ppd then now 6 ppd. For the past 10 weeks or so, I have been using willow pump for 1-2 sessions per day and use another pump (Spectra S2) for the rest of the sessions.

I did not use the Willow pump right from the start, because 1) I was too tired to figure out the complicated steps required to use it, 2) at the time I was pumping small amounts of colostrum and it didn’t make sense for me to use these bags for such small amounts.

Hands free and wireless
For me, biggest draw and selling point of this pump was being able to multitask while pumping, which is absolutely a big win here. However, note that these pumps are not very discreet (unless you want to look like Pamela Anderson, quoting my friend who is also trying this out) and they are not very quiet. I would not use this out and about, or even in front of my in-laws while they are in the house.

Suction
For me, the suction felt different from my regular pump. It seemed uncomfortable at first and it took some time getting used to, eventually after a few sessions. However, I often have clogged ducts and I did find that in several instances, the strong and different suction did seem to help clear the clogs.

Volume limit
The max volume of the containers and bags is only 4 oz each side.
For me, personally, that limit is okay for 8 ppd and once I got to 6-7 ppd, it is not enough to empty my breasts sometimes, I can only use it for sessions when I know volumes are lower.
The pump will automatically stop pumping once you reach that 4 oz limit, it would require switching out a new bag or container to continue. The process is cumbersome, since it would require you to unlatch, take out the pumps and “flip to finish” and re-latch. With other pumps you might have the option to use larger containers, or simply swap out containers while still latched.

Learning curve
There definitely is a learning curve. It took me a few sessions to master the “flip to finish” required to get all the milk into the bags or reusable containers so that there is no milk left in the flex tubes. I think new users probably should expect to lose some milk from leaks and mishap in the beginning. The quick start guide and the videos in the Willow app are very helpful and clear but the steps to use it effectively are complicated.

Issue 1 (occurred more than once a week )
It is awkward to double pump on both sides. You cannot latch on both sides at once. You have to initiate latch on one side first, once you have one side latched, you have to quickly latch on the other. I have a quick letdown, so if I don’t quickly latch on the second side, often times I get a mess, and the second side becomes hard to latch on as it is wet, often triggering one of those orange blinking light warnings and it would not let you proceed unless you can reattach the flex tube and/or flush the valve with warm water (impossible to do in a car or away from home). I often end up using a 2nd container to continue, crossing my fingers and hoping that I would not run into the same issue with the 2nd one.

Issue 2 (occurred at least 4-5 times)
I occasionally get the issue with the milk containers not filling to 4 oz but the pump/app says it is. 3-4 minutes into the session, with 1-2 oz in the container, it would say it is full and stop and would not let you continue with same container. Again, I would use a 2nd container to continue, hoping I would not run into the same issues.

Cost of parts
The pump does not come with the reusable milk containers. They cost another extra $49.99 a pair at the time of this review. In practicality you would need at least two sets. The pump only comes with one pair of flex tubes, so one would need at least one extra pair for practical purposes.
Also one of my milk containers already cracked after about 2-3 months of use.

Conclusion
While innovative and the freedom it offers delightful, the willow pump does not fulfill all my needs as an exclusive pumper who wants to consolidate pumps to fewer pump sessions per day (thus more volume per session), also not as someone who occasionally like to pump on the go in the car. It is hard to justify the costs of the pump and all its parts. The issues I encountered make it unreliable to be used on the go.

It seems to have a lot of potential but much is still left to be improved.
