Product Title: Spectra - S2 Plus Electric Breast Milk Pump for Baby Feeding - Convenient Breast Feeding Support
Review Title: Spectra Baby S2 is professional grade!!
Author: Old school Lycan
Review Text:
First of all, thank you to all the people who took the time out of their busy lives to share very helpful reviews!  Special thanks to reviewers Michelle Jang and K. Barnett for helping my wife and I make an informed decision with the Spectra Baby S2.  I'm not going to delve or rehash anything they have already mentioned but I will like to contribute our experience with the S2 for others who are trying to decide which breast pump to purchase in this daunting sea of baby related products.  So here goes:

Our daughter was born 7 weeks prematurely.  As a result, my wife was going to 100% breastfeed if her body allowed it.  Whether you are a first time parent or a seasoned vet, it's rather scary to see your child so small and so frail with many unknowns.  Unfortunately, our little angel had trouble latching on.  My wife's team of lactation consultants tried many different angles and attempts to get her to latch, but at the end- our precious little preemie was one that preferred the instant gratification of a bottle.  Luckily, my wife was able to express and we are taking it as a blessing.  Our insurance company provided us with the Ameda Purely Yours Double Breast Pump.  My wife is a planner; so within 3 months of her pregnancy we received the Ameda Purely Yours Pump.  We checked online to compare prices and found that Ameda Purely Yours was going for $150.  My wife was quite excited about the prospect of using a breast pump and entering the world of motherhood....I on the other hand was ecstatic that we just saved $150 for a pump that looked promising on paper.

Fast forward to 33 weeks after the delivery....my wife had her initial consultation with the lactation consultant.  I was a bit agitated with the consultant at first because whenever she mentioned breast pump....she was constantly pushing for my wife to rent a "hospital" grade Medela Symphony unit.  When my wife mentioned that we brought our own breast pump from home, the consultant asked to see it.  She took one glance at the Ameda and shrugged it off.  So naturally, my wife and I were completely turned off by her attitude towards the Ameda.  She never really gave us an explanation to why the "hospital" grade pump was better than the "consumer" grade pump.  Because my wife also has a condition called PCOS, the probability of my wife's chances to express is a lot lower than women without PCOS.  For one week, at $20, we told ourselves let's give it a shot and record data on her milk yield.  As scientists, we are obsessed with recording data and have been quantifying our daughters milk intake on a daily basis and still to this day my wife has been recording her milk yield.  Although one week's data is not as good as a month's or two months of data, my wife's recorded yield between the Ameda and the Medela suggested a large discrepancy between the two units.  If my memory serves me correctly, she told me that the average difference in yield was by 15-25 mL.  A mother's breast milk is often referred by both healthcare professionals and moms alike as "liquid gold."  A difference of 25 mL was enough to convince us that there was merit in renting a Medela unit.

Renting a Medela unit from our hospital is currently priced at $85 plus tax per month.  The other alternative was to switch to formula...which we did not want to unless we had to.  Again, we wanted to give our daughter the maximum benefit of breast milk for as long as my wife could express.  According to medical professionals, milk is beneficial to infants due to the passing of mom's antibodies to child.  Studies have shown that infants who are fed breast milk tend to be leaner, less likely to get sick, less likely to develop autoimmune diseases as adults, and are less likely to be obese as adults.  However, at $85 a month....this was going to get rather expensive really quickly.  We already have various bills coming from every direction and the last thing we needed was another bill.  Obviously, we would've continued to rent the Medela if we had no other choice.

The last time I checked, the Medela Symphony is priced at $1500 and is marketed to hospitals and lactation consultants.  There are a couple of vendors out there that will sell to the public but according to Medela....the Symphony is not meant to be sold to the public but rather rented.  Medela does offer a "consumer" grade called the Medela Pump In-Style.  The Pump In-Style received much better reviews than it's predecessor the Medela Personal Double Pump but we have never owned either so I can't really say one way or the other if they are just as good as the Symphony.  Many people have sworn by these consumer grade pumps....but many negative reviews have suggested that the pumps lose suction over time.

With only a week left on our Medela rental, I was determined to find an alternative for my wife to help us save more money.  Enter the Spectra Baby.  I stumbled on the wonderful reviews by Michelle Jang and K. Barnett and decided to take a chance.  At $142...now at $128.....why the heck not?  For one week, my wife compared her yield between the Spectra S2 and the Symphony.  The results were virtually identical!  The first thing my wife noticed was that the suction power was just as powerful as the Symphony.  The other cool thing is that we were able to use all of her Medela parts with the Spectra with just minor tube modifications shown by Michelle Jang and we were in business!!  The Spectra Baby is the best kept secret!  Some insurance companies in several states have started to adopt the Spectra systems as they are gaining momentum in popularity.  So how is the Spectra better the Medela Symphony?

1.  Cost
2.  Weighs significantly less at 3.3 lbs
3.  Has a night time light
4.  Can still use existing Medela flanges, pump parts, and various accessories

My wife has been using the Spectra S2 since the end of April 2015 to this present day of July 14th, 2015 without any hiccups or degradation in suction.

We can't be any happier with the Spectra S2 and I hope this review helps other parents with the decisions.  Special thanks to the many people that leave very informative reviews....without your reviews we would've never have known about great products such as this one.  I hope to pay it forward with this contribution of a review.  Good luck to you all.

Product Title: Spectra - S2 Plus Electric Breast Milk Pump for Baby Feeding - Convenient Breast Feeding Support
Review Title: Great pump! Better than Medela (except for the tubing/attachments)
Author: Amazon Customer
Review Text:
This is my fourth pump in two babies - I blew through the motor on my Medela Freestyle twice, bought a (used) Symphony for home use, and then got a Medela PISA from my insurance company. My Medelas have been very effective - I pumped at work for over a year with my first baby and was well started on pumping with my current one with my Medelas. Then I decided to try the Spectra because of rave reviews from other people.

The Spectra is incredibly quiet - about the same as the Medela Symphony. Both of those pumps are much much quieter than the Medela Freestyle or PISA. Like the Symphony, it has adjustments for both pumping speed and suction strength, and a "letdown mode" toggle button. It's as quick or quicker than the Symphony. I can fully empty out within 10-15 minutes. The adjustment of speed and suction allows me to stimulate multiple letdowns in one quick session. Most importantly - it doesn't hurt like the Medela pumps. I usually have to work myself up to stronger suction of the Medela pumps over the first five minutes of a session because the pulling motion really hurts. However, with the Spectra, it uses a gentler pull-and-vibrate motion which is just as effective as the Medela pumps, but doesn't hurt. Although the shape of this pump isn't as easily packable as the practical brick shape of the PISA (the basic one that comes from your insurance, not built into a bag/backpack), and is slightly larger than the PISA, it's light - probably about the same as the Medela portable pumps, and smaller than the Symphony.

One star off because the attachments are annoying. The wide-neck bottles are leaky, and difficult to pour out of (first time I tried to pour out of the wide-neck bottle, I spilled half an ounce of breastmilk and almost cried). The breast cone comes attached to the adapter, which makes it impossible to use the hands-free pumping bustiers that only have two small holes in front. It's also annoying because the size you get may not be  yours. I got the 24mm with my shipment (small), but they also come in large or medium. Since parts are not as available as Medela, it's expensive to get new adapters in the appropriate size. I think the older version of this pump probably had detachable parts, based on the reviews, but the one I got in the beginning of 2015 (ordered from Amazon) shipped with one adapter piece, including both the cone that goes over the breast, and the adapter that screws onto the bottle.

The backflow protector is nice, to keep the pump closed. However, I've never had issues with backflow of milk into the tubes in any of my pumps. While there are ways of cutting apart the Medela PISA tubing to fit into the front-side of the Spectra tubing, the Medela tubes (without backflow protector) also fit when plugged directly into the Spectra pump. The fit is fine, and allows for use of Medela adaptors and narrow-neck bottles with the Spectra pump (though without the backflow protector).

Also annoying: no car adaptor. They make a version of this pump with a battery, but I don't really like battery-operated pumps (I had a Freestyle) because I oftentimes find myself for a full day in a place without a plug, and since I have long days, the battery doesn't always last for the third pumping session of the day, especially after a few months of regular use. This is probably solvable with an inverter for the car, but I have yet to try that - assume it would be just as good that way.

All in all - a great pump! I have yet to try or experience one I like more!

Product Title: Spectra - S2 Plus Electric Breast Milk Pump for Baby Feeding - Convenient Breast Feeding Support
Author: Sarine Thomas
Review Text:
I have been an amazon customer for many years but this is my first review. The Spectra S2 has really impressed me.

I had my first baby a couple months ago and was determined to breastfeed her. I was gifted the madela freestyle pump and was really excited about using it to start my own milk stash because I really wanted to provide my child with breast milk for a year or more. Unfortunately my baby would fall asleep at the breast a few minutes after latching on so though I kept waking her up and feeding her for more than an hour and half each session, she never emptied either breast. I thought the Medela pump would help me to at least pump and bottle-feed her the milk but every time I pumped, I got less and less milk each session. I never once got more than an ounce from both breasts together. Even getting an ounce (per DAY - not session) was almost impossible. Half an ounce TOTAL from both breasts in one DAY was the norm for me with the pump. (There was nothing wrong with the pump or tubes and the flanges were the proper size.) I talked to LCs but their suggestions didn't help. I took fenugreek in copious amounts, drank a lot of mothers milk tea, even consumed some south-indian home remedies my mother and grandmother prepared for me to no avail. My milk supply began to decrease because my breasts weren't being emptied. Within 5 weeks of my baby's birth my milk supply was just about gone. I was devastated.

I began using the madela harmony manual pump with the hopes of somehow increasing my supply again. When I began using it, my supply was just a mL in an entire 40 minute session with 20 minutes per breast. Sometimes I didn't get more than a couple drops. But I used it every few hours  round the clock and saw my supply come up to a total of one ounce per day within two weeks. From there though it leveled off (hand pumping for 40 minutes at a time HURTS so I couldn't effectively increase the frequency of my sessions). Fortunately, once my daughter hit about the 2 month mark, she was breastfeeding much better, staying awake and emptying the breast each time. I was still using the hand pump however and I considered renting the madela symphony but it was simply way too expensive.

My husband happened to find this pump in a cursory search on amazon and told me it was a hospital grade pump for a fraction of the cost of madela. I read most of the reviews and was so excited to hear stories similar to my own from other moms. Almost all of the ones who had trouble with madela pumps and switched to the spectra S2 saw an increase in their output. So I ordered it, hoping the same would be the case for me.
As soon as I received it, I went to my room to pump. I didn't have much hope of seeing an output since my daughter had just fed a minutes before and emptied both breasts but this pump still drew out an extra 8mL in 15 minutes! That's more than how much I get in 40 minutes of hand pumping in some sessions. The second session was also a little bit after a feeding and I still got 9mL. I love this pump and I am so glad I purchased it. It is worth every single penny. Now I can pump more frequently and I have every hope of building up to produce more than an ounce from each breast each session.

Product Title: Spectra - S2 Plus Electric Breast Milk Pump for Baby Feeding - Convenient Breast Feeding Support

Product Title: Spectra - S2 Plus Electric Breast Milk Pump for Baby Feeding - Convenient Breast Feeding Support
Review Title: Comfortable but not the answer I'd hoped for
Author: ams13
Review Text:
I bought this to replace a Pump in Style Advanced that I'd bought for my first child, as it was taking me 3-4 45-min sessions a day to pump enough milk to leave my baby for 7-8 hours. The PISA was also quite uncomfortable, even with the larger personal fit breastshields that I use.  While I am not an "overproducer", my baby certainly doesn't nurse for 45 min at a time, and I was hoping to find a pump that could cut down on time.  I was excited to see affordable hospital grade pumps from Spectra, and I was wavering between the S2 and the Dew 350. I went with the s2 because of the letdown/massage mode.

First of all, the pump is really comfortable, especially with the adjustable cycle length and vacuum.  So it is a great improvement over the PISA in that.  But it is not a magic bullet: in 4 days of use it has not resulted in either an increase in milk quantity or a decrease in pumping time for me, which I found disappointing.  It is not too heavy or too large to carry back and forth to work.  I use a tote to carry the pump and parts and an insulated lunch box to store the milk. It seems well designed and sturdy. I don't see the point of the nightlight, but I don't pump at night.

I think there are two problems (for me) with the pump.  The letdown mode - which was my primary reason for purchasing the pump - doesn't work well for me, as the suction cannot be turned up high enough during this mode.  It truly is more of a feathery "massage" mode than letdown mode.  The PISA letdown mode worked for me in about 10-20 seconds; the s2 takes long enough (minutes) that I usually just switch to the quickest setting on the regular cycle instead.

Second -and this is the biggest problem, for me- is the pattern of cycling.  The pump cycles really gently through pump, release, pump, release.  You can adjust the number of times it cycles per minute for 30 to 46, so the lower numbered settings have a longer suction time.  However, the release phase does not speed up, and the release phase is too long.  On the fastest settings, only about half of each minute is spent in suction, and the rest is release.  In the slower settings, a proportionally longer time is spent in suction, but the release time between cycles is still the same (too long) length of time.  The suction is powerful enough, though, and I did not find a significant difference in milk collection between the highest and intermediate settings.

the breast shields: the breast shields that come with the pump are comparable in size to the ones that come standard with the Medela, but I found that the shape of the Spectra shields makes them more comfortable to me.  I can use the small S2 shields if I need to, but I cannot comfortably use the standard Medela.  Unfortunately they are not big enough for me.  I use a larger size Medela shield, and with the standard S2 shields I could feel that some ducts did not empty.

Before I purchased the pump I did email the company to ask about the size of the shields, among other things.  They wrote back and said there are larger shields available, but that some women have made the Medela shields work with this pump.  Another reviewer on Amazon has posted a diagram for how to make the Medela shields work, and I suppose this is at least unofficially sanctioned by the company if they mention it in emails!  I did try the Medela shields using this method and found it worked fine.  (I cut the Medela tubing, not the Spectra tubing.) This is also relevant because it means that in an emergency you could buy Medela replacement parts at a local store rather than needing to find Spectra parts.

The collection kit: eh. It works fine.  The threads are compatible with the Medela kits, as well as the Playtex pump and store kits.  The bottles and nipples are adequate.  My daycare provider used the Spectra bottle and nipple and my baby slurped it down just fine.  They're not pretty, and probably won't hold up forever, but they're okay.

On the whole, this is a modest improvement over the PISA.  Given that the Medela kits are compatible, and comparing the price of the two, I would go with the S2 but plan to purchase extra Medela parts and/or collection kits.  However, given the price and the general uselessness of the letdown mode, The Dew350 might be a better option.

I had been using a PISA that was covered through my insurance and it was okay for the first 3 weeks when all of a sudden, a few days ago my nipples began to hurt so bad even something brushing up against them softly made me want to scream and cry. Yesterday was the most painful yet, all I got all day was drops from my PISA and even my first try with the spectra.  I decided to take a rest from pumping all together for a few hours and tried again around 11 with the Spectra.  I normally get anywhere from .5 oz to an ounce but I got 2 oz out of my right breast right off the bat.  This morning, I decided to try my left breast while baby was latched on the right, I normally don't get very much if any at all from my left breast using a pump but I already have more milk from my left than I got from my right last night.....and we're still going!! My daughter is only 4 weeks old so I feel like this is a huge accomplishment considering I was in so much pain and getting little output with the PISA. Oh yes, and this does NOT hurt my nips like the Medela does.  They're still sore but they need to heal as I think I just had the Medela settings set way to high. Product Title: Spectra - S2 Plus Electric Breast Milk Pump for Baby Feeding - Convenient Breast Feeding Support
Review Title: I could kiss the engineers that designed this
Author: briget
Review Text:
Update: my S2 did develop an issue and started shorting out after 5 months of constant (8 times a day for 30 minutes eac pumping session) use. When I called spectra they immediately processed the claim and overnighted me a new pump, plus gave me a 15% off coupon for some new accessories. I could not be more thrilled with this company. Well done spectra baby USA!
For the last 15 weeks I have struggled at every pumping session with a medela PISA (more like POS). I'm exclusively pumping so this was 8-12 times a day of absolute misery. Well my Medela stopped working and they wouldn't replace it so I bought this pump instead. It is so, so much better in every way I can't even begin. First, this pump has an actual display and buttons that adjust the suction as well as the cycle length.  There is a nightlight to be able to see what you are doing when you stumble around at 3am to get up and pump. There is a timer on the display (extremely important at first when you are trying to get your supply established). This is quiet enough that you can sit right next to your sleeping baby and they will stay asleep, and it doesn't sound like the pump is talking to you. The valves that allow the milk to pass through to the bottles are a single piece of soft silicone instead of hard plastic with a thin membrane over it that is constantly tearing like the medela. There is also a backflow membrane that keeps milk out of the tubes and the pump, and it also seems to be keeping moisture out of the tubing (this was always a huge problem with the PISA.) The best part of all though? No more pain! The PISA and it's horrible spastic action have DESTROYED my nipples even with the correct flange size. This pump on the other hand has a much more gentle rhythm that isn't pulling and twisting my nipples up against the flange wall. The milk blisters that I have developed are actually healing. It's overall very clear that someone put a lot of time, and attention to detail into designing this pump and the manufacturer is following good quality control. Product Title: Spectra - S2 Plus Electric Breast Milk Pump for Baby Feeding - Convenient Breast Feeding Support
Author: Amaris
Review Text:

Pros
--The massage setting really helps flow and stimulates let down
--Very customizable settings allow you to change rate and vacuum strength
--It remembers your settings after it has been turned off and on
--The nipples and bottles included are great for newborns (slow flow nipples)
--It can be easily moved between rooms
--You can use it on one or both sides as needed
--Has a light that illuminates settings when pumping in the dark

Cons

Look closely at the details listed for bottles -- unfortunately none of the bottles I purchased fit the third party or spectra flanges so I am constantly washing bottles. I purchased the kiinde twist bags and adapter package which has helped a bit. I am the only person in my house who knows what plastic bit goes with what other plastic bit! Product Title: Spectra - S2 Plus Electric Breast Milk Pump for Baby Feeding - Convenient Breast Feeding Support
Review Title: Best decision I ever made is to buy this pump!
Author: Sarah Wilbourn
Review Text:
This is an extremely important piece of equipment for me, I exclusively pump since my daughter is in the NICU and receives her milk through a tube. I have to rely on my pump to provide my baby with milk, so if it’s not reliable, I would be very honest. I did a crazy of research picking a pump, and I was not disappointed!

Things I love:
1. This is so easy to use. The digital controls make it extremely simple to chose a comfortable suction level. The timer helps me keep track of how long I’m pumping. The light is very useful at nighttime, I don’t have to wake my husband with my lamp. I used a Medela Symphony in the hospital for 3 days after birth, and was way more impressed with my Spectra as far as ease goes.

5. Has a letdown phase feature that is very easy to use. It started out in letdown mode, then you just press the expression button and it changes over. It saves your settings from the last session, so you don’t have to reset it each time.

Product Title: Spectra - S2 Plus Electric Breast Milk Pump for Baby Feeding - Convenient Breast Feeding Support
Review Title: So glad I decided to purchase
Author: AJRICH
Review Text: I'm so glad I purchased this pump. With my first babe, I got the Hygeia through insurance and literally could not produce a drop, so I rented a Symphony for the duration of my pumping career. With my second child, I ordered the Medela PISA thinking it was a sure bet. I know some pp have great success with that pump but it felt incredibly rough on my nipples and I still wasn't pumping much at all. So, back to the rental Symphony, which was by far the best of the three but I STILL wasn't producing much and my nipples still felt slightly abused in the process. At the recommendation of a lactation consultant and after much deliberation, I ended up buying the Spectra. After spending a few hundred on consultants, an ungodly sum on donor milk from a milk bank, and then some for the rental pump, I decided the Spectra would be worth it if it was as great as all the reviews suggested. And it is! For me, it's easily superior to even the Symphony. It's light, it's quiet, it's GENTLE and it's very effective. The "suckling" makes it so much easier for me to have a let down, and the timer and nightlight are cherries on top. As others note, the accessories kind of suck--the bottles barely stay closed when attached to the pump for some reason (they have a way of almost unscrewing themselves), the back flow protectors don't stay put incredibly well either, and because they are a little sticky/grabby (for lack of a better word), the tubes tend to pick up lint on the outside. But all of those complaints are a small price to pay for an overall excellent pumping experience (words I thought I'd never say). I am not back at work yet but I am already feeling so much more confident about my ability to continue go of my baby breast milk for as long as I'd like (with my first, I stopped at 6 months because my measly .5 to 1 oz marathon pumping sessions were so time consuming and demoralizing). I know pump preference is a personal thing, but if you've had no luck with the more popular models, I would definitely urge you to give this a try. If you don't prefer it, you can always sell, donate or give to a friend.

Product Title: Spectra - S2 Plus Electric Breast Milk Pump for Baby Feeding - Convenient Breast Feeding Support
Author: Esmeralda Salamone
Review Text:
This pump is a game changer. I got this because our 3mo old is super easily distracted and was dropping percentiles so our pediatrician and lactation consultant wanted us to try pumping a few oz each day to give her a bottle in the morning and at night.

I started with a secondhand Ameda- when it did work, which was only half of the time, I could only ever get .5-1.0 oz out of it, and that was after 15 minutes of struggling and discomfort. I ended up hand expressing for several days in addition to the pump because it just wasn't emptying the breast efficiently. I finally reached a breaking point and fortunately was able to get this thing delivered to our door on Christmas Eve with Prime same day shipping.

I was so nervous putting it together - it had come highly recommended on a parenting forum I am on but I couldn't help but worry that perhaps it wasn't the PUMP that was the problem, it was ME.

Set up was a breeze - the standard boil some wash some procedure for any pump. I love that it automatically has a slower setting it begins with to get your milk going (I did hand express a bit before I started as it indicates to do so in the instructions) and then you only have to press one button to switch to "Expression" mode. The suction is insane, I had it on the second lowest setting and managed to get 2oz on one side in under ten minutes. And the best part was - it didn't hurt! The Ameda was so uncomfortable I was seriously considering supplementing with formula.

To be honest, I don't see how the other brands stay in business. This bad boy comes in at near $50 cheaper than the cheapest competition (Ameda, Phillips Advent) and seems to outperform them. I skipped out on the S1 that has a battery to save money, but the charge on it lasts 3 hours which is also incredible - it would be an amazing machine if you need to bring it to work and pump!

Our hospital pumps cost $90 to rent with a $50 fee for the parts so this was the best AND most economical choice - a real winner all around.

Product Title: Spectra - S2 Plus Electric Breast Milk Pump for Baby Feeding - Convenient Breast Feeding Support

Author: J&R.coop
Review Text: So I bought this Spectra s2 back in March 2017 to see if it could replace my PISA (pump in style advance by Medela)and used it on and off maybe a total of  45 to 50 hrs total until July 2017. With my supply being stable I decided to stop pumping. I've always been a "just enough" mom when it came to providing breast milk for my baby but would pump to donate to mothers and preemie infants at our local hospital to increase the overall milk demand so I could keep my supply a little higher then my daughter's demands. Initially pre spectra s2 I used my PISA daily 8 times (20 minutes each session) for 6 months before it started to lose suction. Cost wise the spectra on Amazon is much more affordable however I'm curious if the cost on the spectra site would have been worth it now due to the 2 year warranty... Honestly if I would have known that my health insurance would have covered the spectra s2 like I learned after receiving my PISA I would have choose the spectra instead thus ensuring I was covered by the 2 year warranty. So if you're here in search of reviews for breast pumps and have a baby on the way check if your insurance provider will cover a breastpump, more specifically the spectra s2. Then order it from the spectra site where you'll recieve the 2 year warranty so if you lose suction as quickly as I have you'll be covered.

Product Title: Spectra - 9 Plus Portable Electric Breast Milk Pump for Baby Feeding
Review Title: Does what I need it to do so far.
Author: TL
Review Text:
I'm not using this day in and day out since I'm mostly breastfeeding, but I got this because the pump my insurance gave me, the Medela Pumping In Style, which would've never been my choice (if I had been given a choice), was a piece of garbage that I now only use if I'm willing to accept that I might end up just sitting down and having it be a noise-maker with no pumping and no style.

Anyway, I can't compare this to any other pumps that seem popular, but probably the main thing that I like about Medela's Pumping In Style over this is that this starts on the same setting that you left off on rather than starting on the massage setting when you turn it on. That took me by surprise when I first used this. I also wouldn't say I'm a huge fan of the tubing for either pump, but I think Medela's was slightly less aggravating.

They both seem about the same level of noisy.

I probably like everything else about this pump more than Medela's Pumping In Style.
I like being able to see which setting I'm on rather than guessing.
I like that this is lighter weight.
I like that this is rechargeable.
I like the flanges being clear so that I can easily see if milk is even coming out. Medela's flanges are clear but the other plastic parts that they slot into aren't. Can't see the milk coming out unless I get a mirror or something and try to see if milk is dripping into the bottle.
I like the placement of the air hole more on the Spectra flange than on Medela's flange setup. On Spectra's flanges, the air hole is towards you, the person pumping, so it doesn't spill out as easily if you lean forward a bit. On Medela's, the air hole is away from you, which means you can go F yourself if you need to bend over a little to give your baby attention. I spilled at least 2 ounces with Medela's stupid flange setup really early on in my baby's life before I had any supply built up because I tried to do this thing called bending over to give my baby attention. I was already having a hard time because I didn't heal properly after giving birth, was in a lot of pain, and family members who wanted to help more were unavailable/had very limited availability, so I was on my own a lot and barely sleeping. Losing 2 ounces may not sound like a lot to some people, but when your baby is still at a point where 2 ounces is still enough to fill your baby's belly, you want those 2 ounces that you feel like you just barely produced to not end up on the floor.

I wish it came with it's own way of clipping on or a bag made for it. I display is bright and easy to understand. The pump in general is easy to use. However I dont know how people are driving and using this. The "horn" (part that goes on the breast) is the same as on a standard pump and sticks out several inches off the chest. You could not wear a shirt over yourself while pumping. I do wish the pump came with a vessel that could be worn under your shirt to collect milk, had it's own way of being carried or clipped, and that the pump was about 10 times quieter than it is.It is WAYYYYY too loud.

Product Title: Spectra - 9 Plus Portable Electric Breast Milk Pump for Baby Feeding
Author: Frances Garcia
Review Text: This is my fourth breastfed baby/using a breastpump - I've owned the Medela PISA (hate) and the full-size Spectra pump (love and prefer) and actually didn't mind lugging it around. I travel quite a bit for work and was curious if it might make packing a bit more efficient. I wish I had bought it sooner. It fits in my back jean pocket and standard a car cup holder... I have even used it during many commutes. It is quiet and powerful, and fits with all of the other standard Spectra pump parts. Now, I prefer to use the full-size Spectra pump at home and the Spectra 9 at work and for travel. Note that the speed and vacuum settings are preset (vacuum setting will not go higher than 5 in massage mode, and the higher the vacuum setting, the lower the frequency of the expression mode). If you need a custom setting, this pump isn't for you. I am personally very happy with the 9 and do not see this as a con because it takes the guesswork out of the settings. Very cost-effective, small pump... highly recommend!

Product Title: Spectra - 9 Plus Portable Electric Breast Milk Pump for Baby Feeding
Author: Nicole in CA
Review Text:
I bought this little Spectra pump for a business trip.  I didn't want to lug my giant Medela Symphony all over in my carry-on.  It took me a little getting used to, but now I love it.  My first pump (first baby) was a Spectra S2.  I loved it!  If you've used and liked Spectra pumps before, I think you'll like this one.  I wouldn't recommend it for a full-time pumper, but it's great for travel and part-time pumping. I've had mine about two months and use it about 8-12 times a week.
Pros:
The battery life is great.  I can usually pump about 6 times for 15 minutes at level 7 or 8 before I need to charge again.
It has 5 "massage" settings (for let-down) and 10 "expression" settings.  At first it seemed a little weak (I was accustomed to my Medela) but the more I use it the better my body responds to it.
It is really small and light.  About the size of an iPhone.
The operation is quiet compared to others.  It's not silent by any means, but I pumped in my seat while on the plane and the cabin noise was enough to conceal the pump noise.
The display is a good size, bright, and easy to read.
It's very simple to use.  If you've used a Spectra pump before, it's the same overall feel.
Cons:
The power switch is easy to accidentally press while carrying the pump in a purse or tote.  A couple of times I've found it running inside my work tote, which drains the battery.
I'm not a fan of the pump flanges and diaphragms, but there are kits out there that replace the bottle and flange setup.  I don't dislike them that much that I feel like I need to buy different ones.

Product Title: Spectra - 9 Plus Portable Electric Breast Milk Pump for Baby Feeding

Review Text:

The downside to it is that I do not get the full suction that I do on my spectra 2. The spectra 9 plus, at its max (L10) sucks at the level of the spectra 2, L7 or L8. This might be perfectly fine for some people, but I usually pump on the spectra 2 at L10 to L12, so the spectra 9 plus does not empty my breasts as well.

I still use the spectra 9 plus when getting ready in the morning, I hook it up and go do my hair and eat breakfast and all that. I also use it at work to pump as it’s easy and light to carry back and forth.

The spectra 9 plus is ideal for travel, on a plane or at work, but I will save it for those occasions and still mainly use my spectra 2 to maintain my supply.

Product Title: Spectra - 9 Plus Portable Electric Breast Milk Pump for Baby Feeding
Author: Emma L
Review Text:
UPDATE: One star. Useless
Today I tried to use this at a conference that was across town from my office.  I'm currently sitting in my office, instead of at the conference, using my S2 instead of this little 9plus. I love that the 9 plus is small and portable and it was easy to throw in a small lunch bag and not take a huge pump bag with me.  I love that it holds a charge and that when I put it on the charger last night, it was still fully charged. But it DID NOT WORK for pumping (the main point of owning this).  I got into the lactation room at the conference, got myself all set up, turned it on, and waited two minutes on the "massage mode." Nothing. Which was pretty remarkable, since I had missed one of my morning pumping sessions, so I was in the "don't think about baby or my shirt will get wet" stage of needing to pump.  I absolutely cannot recommend this.  If I had to rely on this as my main pump, my kid would be getting nothing but formula, because I would get no milk.  I am pretty disappointed about it.  I wish I could take it to conferences instead of lugging around the bigger S2 and finding an outlet.  But the most important thing is expressing milk, and this was not going to cut it. I don't think I can return it, since its technically used, but I won't be trying to use it anymore.

I admit, I have not given this a full test. I purchased this to use instead of my bigger S2 when I’m traveling for work. I imagined throwing it in my purse and not feeling like I needed the bigger one. I’ve started using this one for two pumping sessions. The strength of it is noticeably weaker than the S2.  After 4 minutes I felt like it was slow or less effective than the S2, or otherwise wasting my time. So I quickly switched to the S2 which I was sitting next to.  I’ve put it in my purse a few times when I was out of the office and felt like I may need to pump, but I have not actually needed it. Bottom line: I think it’s probably comparable to the medela products, but not in the same league as the S2. I would not recommend as your sole pump, because your supply may suffer. But as a short-term, on the go pump, it fills a nice niche. In case you did not guess, I love my S2 (as much as you can love a pump). I have one for work, one for Home (cheaper and quicker than a $150 pump bag) and am using both for my second kid. They’re both still going strong.

Product Title: Spectra - Synergy Gold Dual Adjustable Electric Breast Pump - Breastfeeding Essential
Review Title: Long lasting, great suction, the BEST
Author: Carrie
Review Text:
I have 3 kids all of which I have pumped for.  I have used Medela, EvenFlo, MomCozy Wearable pump, the Spectra S2 (also a great pump), and variety of hand pumps.  Nothing has been as impressive as this pump.  The price tags is a bit of an ouch but I will say that I have had this pump for three years and I've pumped for 18 months on it and it is still going and the suction is still great.

I am also an over producer.  In the first 9 months I produce over 70 ounces in a day and this pump can handle it and does a great job of emptying breasts.  It's also going for women with largers breasts because the pump has the power to help get all that milk out.  With other pumps I would still feel like there was milk left after pumping.  The dual settings are great for individual adjustments so you can adjust for comfort or to try to kick the slacker-boob into gear.

It is very easy to find pump parts and replacement parts such as tubes, duckbills, large bottles or different flanges that work with the spectra.  It is a closed system pump so the milk stays in the bottle area and never goes anywhere near the tubing making it last so much longer

It's not the quietest pump but I've honestly never had an issue with baby or hubs waking up in the middle of the night because I'm pumping.  Is easy to see the settings in the dark so you're not guessing if you've got the right button.

It is not the lightest pump in the world so if you're taking it to work regularly it will get heavy but there are bags that fit in and honestly, if rather carry this around and be comfortable and know I'm getting a good pumping session in than use something more portable.

I highly recommend this pump.  I tell all my soon-to-be mom friends about it!  Way to go Spectra!  Keep up the good work!

Product Title: Spectra - Synergy Gold Dual Adjustable Electric Breast Pump - Breastfeeding Essential
Author: EZE
Review Text:
PROS:
Reliable, doesn't need charging. Will have to sit for pump session which I see as a mandatory break :)
Parts easy to clean.
Parts easy to assemble, quick start.
Two sizes of breast shields provided with device.
Easy to adjust suction from very low to higher level.
Can adjust suction on each side separately, can start or stop each side separately.
Remembers previous session settings
Quiet but still audible
Night light and back light touch panel
Sleek design
Very fast international shipping from seller.

CONS
hooked to electricity, not portable
No space to hold bottles like previous models
Switching from simulation to expression mode cannot be done separately for each side.
Need to manually dial down settings of previous session if you want to start on lower suction.
Automatic shut off at 30 minutes (normal for most pumps)
Breast shields not so comfortable but not bad either (can connect to pumpables liquid shield set- see pic)
Must handle pumped milk carefully, bottles not very stable, also capacity only 160 ml
Somewhat large and heavy.
Minimal accessories provided with purchase.
Milk collection bottles dont come with a cap (rather a teet and disc).
Customer service not excellent. Claimed the one I bought off amazon was not genuine. I'm pretty sure its genuine.
American plug. Will need adaptor. Voltage compatible with international.
Soft pump parts need to be boiled for 2 minutes (standard sterilizer will take longer. I add boiling water to a mug and remove after 2 minutes)
Valves and membranes will need replacement (standard for most pumps)
I still have to manually massage to get maximum volume. I had higher expectations from a spectra pump, but that could just be my personal anatomy.

Overall:
I feel it was a valuable purchase and I use it more than my other 2 portable pumps, but I cannot say that it feels very superior. The milk output is about the same range, maybe slightly more.
The main reason I stick to is that the pump parts are easier to clean and assemble.
You would still need a portable pump if you need to pump at work.

Review Text:
This pump is incredible. As an exclusive pumper this has improved my life!

2. A bit noisy - it’s definitely louder than my Spectra especially if you put it down on a table but well worth it.

The only thing I regret is that I spent so much time going back and forth on whether to buy this or not. This pump is definitely worth it and is solidly my primary pump as an exclusive pumper.

Product Title: BabyBuddha Breast Pump 2.0, Wearable Electric Breastfeeding Pump with Soft Stimulation Mode, Portable, Hands-Free Milk Extractor, Hospital Grade, 3 Modes, 21 Suction Levels, 22 to 24mm Flange
Author: Amazon Customer
Review Text:
I previously was an exclusive pumper with low supply and used medela and spectra pumps. I opted for the spectra pump again with my insurance and probably should’ve went with a newer pump with better technology.

I was in search of a pump that might work better than the spectra so I opted to try this pump out. As far as output goes, it is similar to the spectra, I maybe get a little more out and empty faster but not enough difference to warrant switching pumps. It comes down to preference when I decide which pump I’ll use.

Pros: portable, lightweight. Easy to take on the go with you or move around the house. Has 3 different modes. Out of the 3 pumps I have, the suction on this one is the most comfortable. Empties my breast the fastest which comes in handy when you’re in a rush.

Not necessarily cons but things I didn’t like about it, but is not a deal breaker:

As an exclusive pumper, on a full charge I get about 3 30 min pumps before the battery dies. I have the s1 spectra and I get more pumps off of it in a full charge. (It is smaller in size)

I loathe the toggle button or whatever it is called to switch the modes and levels. Maybe I have fat fingers but it’s not easy to simply press the button to switch between modes. As I’m switching throughout my session to get more let downs this is annoying. Then there is a delay when you are switching modes and levels. So say if you press it wrong or to many times u have to press again to get which mode you want and there is a delay from suction.  The spectra and a cheap knock off wearable I have can switch modes with no delay.

The biggest thing I’m most annoyed at with this brand is the flange sizes. It does not work for us small flange size girlies. Yes I can use an insert but I found that I can produce more with the actual flange size in comparison to using an insert. When you are an under producer, every drop matters. I would love to utilize this brand’s technology and use the flange, bottle, etc but I can’t since they don’t have smaller flanges. I did try using an insert but I found I got better output with a different set up.

So I only utilize the pump itself and I have my spectra bottle attached to it with my flange size when I pump. I wish these companies would come out with smaller flange size.

The motor is loud. It is by no means quiet and it does vibrate as well.

All in all, I do prefer this over my spectra s1 and a momcozy wearable knock off that I have. I have been using this for almost two weeks now and it is what I reach for.  Easy to set up and learn how to use the modes.
Date: Reviewed in the United States on December 4, 2024

Product Title: BabyBuddha Breast Pump 2.0, Wearable Electric Breastfeeding Pump with Soft Stimulation Mode, Portable, Hands-Free Milk Extractor, Hospital Grade, 3 Modes, 21 Suction Levels, 22 to 24mm Flange
Review Title: Amazing portable pump that beats all other pumps!
Author: NaturalLuver
Review Text:
I received it several days ago and sterilized all parts that night. I used it twice yesterday and was so impressed, I am thinking about purchasing another to keep at work. My daughter is almost 4 mos old and pumping is the part I dislike about breastfeeding. This pump makes me think I could do it longer than 6 months. I would love to go a year, but it is difficult with work and I am a low producer so my daughter only nurses in the early morning and then wants to drink from a bottle.

The initial simulation mode is interesting - all the women who said watch out for the long pull weren’t joking. I wasn’t quite prepared for it and to be honest, it hurts when it happens. My nipple seems to get pinched right at the end. However, I can see how that can really help get things going and contribute to proper emptying.

I had missed a pump session at the end of my workday and was a little engorged when I got home so I was eager to try it for the first time. In 30 minutes, it sufficiently emptied my breasts and produced a much higher output than usual - maybe double. I thought that may just be due to engorgement. However, I had a shorter period between that and my (next) last pump of the night and I got just as much as I normally do at my last session, which would not typically happen with my pump sessions being that close together with my spectra. I will admit, my nipples were not quite ready for the second pump session so I didn’t stay in simulation mode and went straight into expression mode. Had I remained in the former mode for a short while, I would bet my output would have been greater.
Overall, I am very pleased with this pump. Portability is fantastic, charging is a breeze and cleanup is moderate - slightly more parts than the spectra, but not enough of a detractor to not recommend this pump. It’s a closed system too - have to love that. One tip - make sure you have the valve opening pointed outward so they properly empty into the bottles. I had placed one improperly pointed in toward me and the milk was not flowing into the bottle due to the wrong angle.
I woke up the next morning after my first two pump sessions the night before with this pump and there is a noticeable difference. My husband even noted that my left breast was ‘huge’ as compared to my right. I could see it sagging quite a bit more due to being filled up over night. I can confidently say that this pump emptied me far more efficiently than my spectra. I have a Spectra S1 and S2 (one at home, one at work). I used them through my first bf journey and wasn’t able to find anything better for my second child...until now. Sorry Spectra, you are now second on my list as I just can’t compare the efficiency of emptying my breasts and portability to the baby Buddha.
In terms of loudness, I would say they are both similar - I don’t feel this is any more quiet than the spectra. In fact, it may seem more loud just because it is closer to your body, but it isn’t a big deal. I have pumped through meetings and conference calls with the spectra and wouldn’t hesitate to do the same with this.
Buy this pump and do yourself a favor and read the instructions while you are sterilizing - do not just hook up and figure it out on the fly. Your nipples will thank you. I tried with and without the silicone covers and given the suction on this unit, the silicone covers are necessary. Understand the modes, how to switch between them and how it will go on automatic initially if you don’t manually change the setting or speed.
Overall, great product. So glad to see a portable unit on the market that meets all the demands I could hope for. I love that I can choose to go between simulation and expression mode however I please too. Highly recommend this pump!

Review Title: I wish I would have gotten this earlier.
Author: Andrea D
Review Text:
I went through a couple different pumps before I found this one. I used the medela pump in style, but would have terrible suction when I tried double pumping (and frankly the suction single pumping wasn't all that great either). I tried the Elive wearable pumps- which I loved when they worked, but unfortunately this was only about 50% of the time, at best and I ended up wasting A LOT of time at work trying to troubleshoot issues with these.

I was searching for something that was portable and handsfree so I could keep up with my busy work schedule while still doing the best I can for my baby. I got the babybuddah this week and I am so happy I did.

Pro's:
1. The suction is strong. To the other comments here- I agree- it is an intense sensation on the nipples at first, but you get used to it about a minute into the pumping session. I need a pump with strong suction to fully express without also having to do breast massage like I did with the medela PISA and my manual pump.

2. It pumps fast- I get the same amount in less than 10 minutes it took the Elvie's to get in a half hour or more.

3.  It is adaptable - I am using it with my medela parts because they are less bulky than the babybuddah collection system. I also like that I would be able to try this with a more discrete collection system- like the freemie cups if I want to in the future.

4. It is super portable- the little pump on its lanyard  is light around my neck and I can actually do things around the house and at work in my office without losing suction or leaking like I did with the Elvie's.  Of course I can't bend over too far or do any yoga or acrobatics, but I am amazed at how much more I can comfortably do with these.

5. It is relatively affordable- at $200. The Elvie's and Willow's are upwards of $500.

Con's:

1. the tubing can be a little cumbersome and not nearly as sleek looking and discrete as the Elvie's

2. Battery issues? I've yet to have any, but from reading the previous comments and instruction manual, I am being careful not to leave it charging for more than 3 hours. This may be problematic in the future given the chaos of working 10 hours a day and caring for my baby all evening and night might lead me to forget it is plugged in once in awhile.

3. the pump kit on comes with size 24 mm breast shields. if you are a different size, you have to order them separately, directly from their website (for about only $20). it would be good if they either came with a couple sizes or let you determine which size you needed with your kit when ordering it. As I said above, I was able to get my medela parts to work with it easily, so this wasn't a major issue.

...and that's it for the con's. The pro's vastly outweigh them, in my opinion.

It's hard enough being a working mom and breastfeeding. It's awesome to have actually found a pumping system that is making my life easier, rather than harder. I am very impressed with this pump and would recommend to any mom who needs an easy, reliable, hands-free option.

Review Title: My favorite out of all my pumps
Author: Paula
Review Text:
I personally love how strong this is but I realize everyone is built differently. I have willow go, spectra s1, and modela harmony hand pump but so far I am loving the baby Buddha the best due to the suction strength because it gets that last little bit out to fully empty me in 10min! However, I’m not in my first week of pumping so I can see how it would have hurt quite a bit had this been my first pump. This is definitely a down the road pump on the breastfeeding journey (I’d say after maybe the first month).

Willow go is nice for portability but it doesn’t do the job well and actually has caused me to have painful clogged ducts 3 times now, is annoying to clean and none of the parts can be sterilized, pouring the milk from it is difficult, and it is heavy and bulky so it falls down in my bra often. Also it is hard to see if you have it positioned exactly right on the nipple. If you don’t, no milk will flow and you waste a lot of time. The wearables like the willow go are made for use once your supply is established about 3 months postpartum because their suction is not as strong. This can hurt your supply if you use it in the beginning months postpartum.

The spectra works better to empty than the willow go and has a stronger pull to help empty more out but it takes twice as long as the baby Buddha and just isn’t strong enough for me anymore. I have gained about 20% more so far with the baby Buddha. I also like the different type of suction pattern that the baby Buddha has where it does 10 short tugs and one long one for the stimulation mode. The downside is that you cannot adjust the cycle and vacuum independently like you can on the spectra.

The most annoying part about the baby Buddha for me is that you can only order the original spare parts directly from their website (not on Amazon). They take 7 days to arrive and cost over $50 if you buy the flanges, bottles, and covers. [Update: they are selling some on Amazon now that I see!] I’m also having some issues with the rolling ball button on the pump as sometimes it’s difficult to get it to scroll to high levels quickly enough (especially at 3am) but I do like that there are only two buttons on the instrument for simplicity. This is still my main go to pump though by far due to its portability and strength.

UPDATE: my supply had tanked last month so badly that I was down to only getting about half an ounce every two hours due to using the willow go too early postpartum and not pumping enough at night which was why I looked for a new pump and now am up to 2.5oz every 2hrs and it is increasing every day! I think it is because this pump is emptying me each time, signaling to my body to make more. This pump saved my supply!

Review Title: Love the portability, hate the pump button
Author: J. Nelson
Review Text:
Review of original baby Buddha pump.

First time mama here! Since having my baby, I’ve been working mostly from home and going into the office occasionally. When I did go in, I was lugging my spectra s1 to and from the office which felt like a chore, but I do love the power of the spectra!

I’m 5 months into motherhood and needed to start traveling for work again; there was no way I was traveling on a plane with my spectra pump. I found the baby buddah after getting so frustrated with a wearable breast pump; too many parts to clean! I immediately purchased and was happily surprised. I was able to hook my spectra parts easily up to this unit, which made switching between my two pumps seamless.

I just got back from a week long Vegas trip for work. I was pumping 4 times per day, 20-30 minutes each pump. This unit is so portable and easy to hook up. A full charge lasts about 2 30-minute sessions but then will require full charge. However, I love that you can plug the unit in and pump at the same time. I was able to pump anywhere I had a little privacy, and with the small profile I was able to store this thing in my backpack on the plane. So easy!

Compared to the spectra S1, my milk output is the same. On my spectra, I usually start on a level 3 for 2 minutes then switch to level 10 for 28 minutes. On this, I start out on letdown level 1 and let it work its way up to level 3, then switch to pump level 4. I’ve been getting the same output by doing this which has been amazing; I was nervous about screwing my production up by switching between pumps.

The only thing I really dislike is the pump remote button. It’s a ball that scrolls up and down to control the speed. My issue is that the ball easily moves when the pump is hanging around my neck, or even when I’m walking while holding the pump in my hand. The ball button is so sensitive that I had to be very still to prevent it from changing suction levels. This was a bit frustrating as I wanted to be able to move around while I was wearing this pump, but the sensitivity of the button kind of prevented me from doing so.

All in all 3/5 stars because it is an amazing and small profile pump that can easily be traveled with. I’m taking off 2 stars because the functionality of the scroll button is really frustrating. I hope the new version of this pump corrects the issue!

Product Title: BabyBuddha Breast Pump 2.0, Wearable Electric Breastfeeding Pump with Soft Stimulation Mode, Portable, Hands-Free Milk Extractor, Hospital Grade, 3 Modes, 21 Suction Levels, 22 to 24mm Flange
Author: LucyLu
Review Text:
I bought this out of pocket because (a) a lactation consultant had recommended it to me to use in lieu of a wearable and (b) I needed to travel while breastfeeding. My other pump is a Spectra S2, which I have an external battery pack on to make it portable.
Pros of this device:
(1) It's small. carrying your pump and cooler and whatnot is still a pain, but at least this thing is pocket-sized.
(2) It's powerful. Maybe *too* powerful for some, but I'd rather have it be a tad too aggressive than to risk my supply
(3) It charges via USB-C. Who doesn't have some of those cords lying around? (it comes with one as well)
Cons:
(1) The battery doesn't last as long as I'd assumed. The battery goes down after maybe 2 pumping sessions. The manual says it lasts for "2 to 4" sessions and also says to not overcharge it, so it's not like you can leave it in at night or whatnot (or risk degrading the battery, I assume). If I were to take this on a long plane ride or on an international trip, I would probably carry an external battery to be safe. My external battery on my Spectra goes for days without being recharged (though it's probably bigger than the whole pump of the BabyBuddha, so I get it). You CAN use it while charging and you can just plug it in while using as well, but of course this drastically decreases the pro of having it be portable.
(2) The letdown mode is not great. It's 10 short suctions (which are fine) and 1 long and VERY aggressive one. It's painful. I switch on and off after the short suctions to avoid the long one, which is annoying. I know they have gotten this feedback for years, so I'm not sure why they haven't modified it in this time.
(3) It's loud. I'd say at least twice as loud as my Spectra.
(4) The parts that need to be replaced are not standard. It comes with the extra duckbill membranes, and it looks like "Motif Medical" makes the membranes on the top (that look like little bowls). However, they don't have the kind of knockoff parts like a Spectra.

Review Title: Absolute "must have" for breast reduction mamas!
Author: The Olivers
Review Text:
I'm an exclusive pumper and post breast reduction mama. I pump around 75-100% of baby's supply depending on cluster feeding. This is hands down the strongest suction on the market. Incredibly affordable. Can be hacked to work with anything, even the Legendairy Milk collection cups (I avoid cups because breast massage is essential for my let downs/complete emptying). I prefer my Medela Symphony parts (most hospitals get you started with this pump before discharge if you ask for a pump while in the hospital and you take the parts home - kits include colostrum collection cups now!!!) with duckbill valves. I absolutely have to use the Pumpin' Pals flanges on this to be comfortable while pumping. You definitely need to make sure you are measured and sized into very comfortable flanges because the suction is so strong. Pumping spray is also a game changer in terms of comfortable pumping. The Medela Symphony and Spectra S1/S2 with Comfort Fit Flex flanges tie as second best in terms of being hospital grade with excellent suction, and I still use these pumps, but the Baby Buddha empties me in half the time and is completely hands free (the Medela pumping bustier and the Kindred Bravely Sublime pumping bras are the bomb!). The set up makes power pumping sessions a breeze. Hopefully future models will allow for more personalized settings in terms of independent cycles and vacuum adjustments, but ultimately not sure if it'd change anything given how great the suction is. Also I agree with other reviewers who mention to rolling the ball down during the let down mode to prevent the long draw until your breasts/nipples "warm up." If I could only have one pump, it'd be this one. I think it's fine even if you're a newbie as long as you do the things above to ensure optimal comfort!

P.S. If lactation nurses discourage pumping because of a "risk" over oversupply - kindly ignore that because it's a LOT easier to dial back oversupply than try to recover under supply, ESPECIALLY for mamas who have had breast reductions, have short maternity leave, and/or work long hours etc. Also ignore the, sadly often perpetuated, myth that pumps can't empty the breasts as well as babies. This is patently false if you dial in the right pumping supplies and techniques. Highly recommend the ExclusivePumping.com resources even if your nursing and pumping. Sadly had to teach myself all this too late in the game with my first, but with my second, starting ahead of the curve and proud to exclusively pump a full supply for my little guy!

Review Title: So powerful! Drastically improved my quality of life!
Author: Lexie
Review Text:
This little device has drastically improved the quality of my daily life. My little lady had severe ties, and couldn't transfer well at all. So pumping and bottles were a necessity. Then at five weeks she started getting symptoms of laryngomalacia, just as breastfeeding was starting to go better, she began to struggle at the bottle and at the breast, and with reflux and choking. So I thought we were done with pumping and bottles, and we had to bring them right back in.

And my mom had left, so I was on my own during the day. Trying to figure out how to care for a newborn while trying to breastfeed, offer bottles, and pump attached to tubing attached to a wall was seriously difficult. It was so hard, and I was having to get up to pump during the night while she slept because I couldn't physically get in enough sessions in the day.

This pump changed the game. I have to use 15 mm flanges, so I use the maymom flanges that are compatible with my Medela peices. So all I needed to get where the maymom long stem back flow protectors, and the Buddha Baby is then compatible with all my Medela peices I've already bought. So it's hardly any tubing, and I can just tuck this little guy into my pumping bra and BOOM I'm mobile! I can go grab a snack, go get something for baby, and not easily care for her when all the tubing is tucked away and I don't need to worry about accidently pulling it out.

Not to mention it's POWER. This pump is stronger than my Spectra S2. It's better than my Medela Symphony. It can get the job done in 12 minutes that took 20-25 on those pumps. I goes up to level 9 on the suction, and I rarely go past 3 max. It did take some adjustment at first, even on level 1 it was stronger than my symphony on half power. It isn't quite as graceful as the big pumps, but what it lacks in finesse it makes up for in efficiency, and a bit of coconut oil in the flanges makes for a smooth pumping experience.

So not only am I mobile, but I don't have to pump as long. I pump 7-8 times a day, and this pump easily lasts for 5-6 sessions on a full charge. When I used it for a full 24 hour period my nipples were a tad sore, so I do 1-2 sessions a day on my Spectra. But that is also combined with a few nursing sessions too, and my baby's latch isn't great, so I can't even fully attribute that to the pump, it's most likely the combination.

But I've been able to ge the same or better output then my Medela Symphony, which I can now return! Being able to just sit in the bed and hook this thing up quickly and be done in 15 minutes has made my days so much better. I'm not sure how long my little lady will need me to pump, but having this pump makes that future look much brighter. I have ordered the freemie cups to try with this, I'll defintely update with how that goes! Thank you to the creators of this product, I was so worried 8 would have to sacrifice power for mobility, which I so often see in reviews on other mobile pumps. Not this pump!

Review Title: One baby product I couldn’t do without
Author: Melanie
Review Text:
Review Update: I’ve been pumping 2.5 hours per day with this little workhorse for 4 months and counting.  I prefer it to my Spectra.  Without this product, I would not still be providing milk for my babies—I would’ve given up and put them on formula long ago.  I’m grateful every day for this product.

Positives:
- AMAZING customer support.
- This thing gets more milk out of me (and in less time) than any other pump I’ve tried. The stimulation mode is super effective, though I found the rhythm uncomfortable the first couple of times—but I can’t argue with the results.
- Extremely versatile, hackable, and compatible.  It works with all my Spectra parts, the Medela parts from the NICU, and with the Freemie parts too (though the Freemie is a nightmare to clean and gives me blocked ducts, so I never use it.)
- As advertised, I can now do the dishes and putter around while pumping. This alone is worth a review of at least four stars.  I can even hold the babies while I pump.  People say “game-changer” about a lot of baby products, but this really did change my life for the better.

Negatives:
- Battery. Takes a long time to charge and does not hold a charge over more than a few sessions (about 90 minutes total). Even with optimal, fresh out of the box battery function, the product takes about twice as long to charge fully as it takes to use up its charge while running.  That being said—that’s not unusual for a lithium battery! The technology just isn’t super efficient yet.  It’s vital to take good care of the battery—I don’t let mine charge more than 3 hours at a time or keep it plugged in once it has reached full charge, and I avoid depleting the battery fully. My battery life has diminished little if at all over four months of regular daily use.
- The flanges it comes with are overdesigned and hard to clean; fortunately, as stated above, it is highly compatible with parts from other pumps, including Medela and Spectra.
- Even the lowest setting on stimulation mode is uncomfortably strong. The highest settings are nipple death for me—but I know some people really value power in a pump, so that could be a feature and not a bug for you!

After a week and a half of use, the pump ceased to charge fully—or even halfway—in three hours, which is the recommended max charging time.  I emailed customer service at about 11pm and had a response by early the next morning; they said they’d had a faulty batch of charger/adapter complexes, and they FedEx overnight-ed me a replacement for mine.  I haven’t had a problem with the battery or charger since.

Product Title: BabyBuddha Breast Pump 2.0, Wearable Electric Breastfeeding Pump with Soft Stimulation Mode, Portable, Hands-Free Milk Extractor, Hospital Grade, 3 Modes, 21 Suction Levels, 22 to 24mm Flange
Author: M. Brown
Review Text:
I've been using this pump exclusively for 3 days and I am very impressed with the suction on this pump. I have sensitive nipples (usually pump on level 4 or 5 on my S1), so I'm still trying to get used to the strong suction. On the Baby Buddah, I can't go past level 1! The battery lasted about 180 minutes of pump time before I had to charge it again.

I “hacked” it to use my Medela parts and pumpin pals. Just pull off the white connector piece on the ends of the tubes that connect to the flanges. The tubes fit perfectly on the end of my backflow connectors (longstem backflows). I have also used it with my Freemies while driving and the suction is great.

Since my nipples are sensitive, I've found I get the best results using the pump a little differently. I start in expression mode on level 1 until I get a let down and then switch to the massage mode (10 short quick suctions plus one long suction). I get the most milk this way and I love seeing the milk pool up in the duckbills before the suction releases! When my let down is done, I'll switch back to expression mode level 1 and repeat. I hope that at some point I can tolerate leaving it in massage mode the entire pump. Also it's important to know that the default setting is massage mode when you turn it on and it auto increases the level up to 5. When I turn on the pump I immediately change it to expression mode level 1 to “prime” my nipples first. Then when you change it back to massage mode, it does not automatically increase the levels anymore.

This pump has cut my pump time by 15-20 minutes. It takes me 45-50 minutes to empty with my S1, where as it takes me 25-30 minutes with the Baby Buddah. I believe that over the next couple days I may see my supply increase, since I have never had a pump empty me quite like this one. #floppyboobs

It's not as quiet as the S1, but more quiet than the S9. I use it at work with no issues. I'm so excited that I don't have to lug my S1 to work anymore! My husband says the pump sounds like it's moo-ing. It auto shuts off at 30 minutes.

Seriously the smallest pump ever. It fits in my pocket, bra, purse, etc. The drawstring bag it comes with is plenty big enough to fit the pump and tubes, 3 sets of pump parts and bottles, bags, small kitchen scale, and a small cooler.

My only issue with the pump is how strong the level 1 suction is on massage mode. My nips are still sore going on day 3 now. I imagine I will develop a tolerance for it eventually. For those of us who have sensitive nipples, this pump will take some getting used to.

Overall, I love this pump and haven't touched my S1 since using this one!

Review Text:

Initially after I turned it on, I thought the suction was really weak...and then it did a really long pull and I wasn’t prepared! I had to turn it on the lowest expression mode until I thought my nipples were ready.

The suck pattern is super amazing. It brought on more letdowns than I’m used to. It is really strong though, even on the lowest letdown mode. Typically I can max out on level 12 on the Spectra, and I barely made it to level 5.

It took a little longer to pump than my Spectra, and my nipples are a little sore, but I think there’s definitely a learning curve, and an adjustment period. Since the suction is so strong, proper flange size and placement is SO IMPORTANT! On a weaker pump you can get by with something close to the right size. This guy isn’t going to work with that.

All in all, I’m really happy with this pump! I definitely recommend it, just make sure your flange size and placement are perfect, and your nipple are ready for that first long pull!
